writers: James Gunn, Dan Abnett, Andy Lanning, Steve Englehart, Steve Gan, Jim Starlin, Stan Lee, Larry Lieber, Jack Kirby, Bill Mantlo, Keith Giffen, Steve Gerber, Val Mayerik
name: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2
cleanNameArticles: guardians of the galaxy vol ii
overview: The Guardians must fight to keep their newfound family together as they unravel the mysteries of Peter Quill's true parentage.
tagline: Anyone can save the galaxy once.
review:
Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 is the kind of cosmic popcorn flick that leans hard into heart and humor, balancing its space-opera spectacle with surprisingly tender family drama. James Gunn’s sequel doubles down on the quirky charm and colorful chaos that made the first one a hit, though it’s less about saving the galaxy this time and more about saving the makeshift family Peter Quill has assembled. If the original felt like a clever mashup of Star Wars and a ’70s mixtape, this one feels like that mix got turned up to eleven—sometimes delightfully overstuffed, sometimes a bit much, but always a wild ride.

What stands out here is the emotional undercurrent beneath all the zany action and snarky banter. The tagline, "Anyone can save the galaxy once," hints at the film’s deeper theme of redemption and belonging, which plays out through Quill’s complicated relationship with his cosmic dad, Ego (Kurt Russell). The visual feast is complemented by a killer soundtrack that somehow makes talking raccoons and baby Groot even more lovable. The voice work of Vin Diesel and Bradley Cooper continues to add layers to the CGI characters, keeping them from slipping into mere comic relief. It’s not the tightest Marvel film, but it’s elevated by its willingness to mix goofy moments with genuine emotional stakes.

Heads-up for animal lovers: this one’s a minefield. The film features multiple instances of animal deaths—including pets and non-human characters—and some scenes of animal abuse and dog fighting. If any of these triggers are on your list, be especially cautious. Also, creepy crawlies and snakes make appearances, so those with bug or snake sensitivities should keep an eye out. The movie’s charm won’t erase these moments, so it’s worth knowing before you dive in.
emailReview:
Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 cranks up the cosmic charm with a vibrant mix of goofy antics, heartfelt family drama, and an irresistible ’70s-flavored soundtrack that makes even a talking raccoon feel like kin.

Be prepared for: multiple animal deaths including pets and non-human characters, scenes of animal abuse and dog fighting, and appearances by creepy crawlies and snakes.

writers: Bret Easton Ellis, Mary Harron, Guinevere Turner
name: American Psycho
overview: A wealthy New York investment banking executive hides his alternate psychopathic ego from his co-workers and friends as he escalates deeper into his illogical, gratuitous fantasies.
review:
American Psycho is a darkly satirical dive into the deranged mind of a Wall Street yuppie gone off the rails. Christian Bale’s chilling portrayal of Patrick Bateman anchors this 2000 cult classic, which rides the razor’s edge between horror and black comedy. It’s like if American greed met a slasher flick — stylish, disturbing, and uncomfortably funny in its critique of vanity and superficiality. While it doesn’t reinvent the genre, Mary Harron’s direction and the sharp, witty script lift it well above your average psycho-thriller.

What really sticks with you is the film’s razor-sharp tone and the way it balances Bateman’s mundane corporate life with his increasingly unhinged fantasies. The tagline, “Killer looks,” nails it — the obsession with surface-level perfection is both the joke and the horror. The supporting cast, including Reese Witherspoon and Justin Theroux, add texture to the hollow world Bateman inhabits, but it’s Bale’s performance that makes the descent into madness hypnotic. The film plays with genre conventions, blending slick 80s aesthetics with brutal moments that feel both gratuitous and pointedly absurd.

Be heavily warned if animal harm is on your list, as the movie includes several distressing scenes involving animals, including a dog and a horse. There’s also a fair amount of creepy crawlies—notably spiders and snakes—which might unsettle bug-sensitive viewers. Overall, this one’s a stylish but savage ride that doesn’t pull punches on its darker, more disturbing content.
emailReview:
Christian Bale’s chilling turn as a Wall Street psycho anchors this darkly satirical cult classic, which blends slick 80s style with brutal, absurd horror and razor-sharp social critique.

Be prepared for: disturbing animal harm involving a dog and a horse, unsettling scenes with spiders and snakes, and moments of graphic violence that cut right through the glossy surface.

writers: Rhett Reese, Paul Wernick, Ryan Reynolds, Rob Liefeld, Fabian Nicieza
name: Deadpool 2
overview: Wisecracking mercenary Deadpool battles the evil and powerful Cable and other bad guys to save a boy's life.
review:
Deadpool 2 doubles down on the irreverent, self-aware superhero chaos that made the first film a cult hit, blending R-rated comedy with action-packed spectacle. It’s like if a Marvel movie and a raunchy buddy comedy had a loud, foul-mouthed baby. Ryan Reynolds returns as the wisecracking Wade Wilson, and while the story leans on a classic “save the kid” plot, the film’s personality keeps it from feeling like just another superhero sequel. Fans of the original will appreciate how it balances meta humor with surprisingly heartfelt moments, even if it sometimes stumbles over its own ambition.

What stands out here is the chemistry among the cast, especially Zazie Beetz as the luck-defying Domino and Josh Brolin’s brooding Cable, whose more serious tone adds an interesting contrast to Deadpool’s manic energy. The film also leans into genre-savvy jokes and fourth-wall-breaking gags, which can be a bit much if you’re not already on board with Deadpool’s brand of comedy. Director David Leitch’s background in stunt work shines through in the slick, chaotic action sequences that never let up. The tagline “Prepare for the Second Coming” feels fitting—this is a sequel that knows it has to top the first and mostly succeeds by leaning into its own outrageousness.

Trigger-wise, electro-therapy is a notable presence here, so those sensitive to that treatment should be cautious. It’s not a heavy-handed horror element, but it does play a key role in some scenes that might be uncomfortable for some viewers. Otherwise, this one’s mostly a high-energy, adult-skewing superhero romp with all the usual comic violence and crude humor you’d expect.
emailReview:
Deadpool 2 cranks up the chaos with Ryan Reynolds’ sharp wit and a standout cast that balances manic energy and brooding intensity, all wrapped in relentless R-rated action and meta humor.

Be prepared for: electro-therapy scenes, graphic comic violence, crude language, and intense stunt sequences.

name: Superbad
overview: Two co-dependent high school seniors are forced to deal with separation anxiety after their plan to stage a booze-soaked party goes awry.
review:
Superbad is a raunchy high school comedy that helped define the mid-2000s teen party genre, sitting comfortably alongside titles like *Pineapple Express* and *American Pie*. It’s a wild ride of awkwardness and over-the-top antics, elevated by Jonah Hill and Michael Cera’s chemistry as co-dependent seniors trying to navigate one last big night before graduation. The film’s tagline, “Come and get some!” perfectly captures its no-holds-barred attitude, though it doesn’t quite reach the cleverness of some of its contemporaries—it’s more about delivering laughs through outrageous situations than sharp satire.

What stands out is the way *Superbad* leans hard into the over-sexualized, booze-fueled chaos of teenage life, pushing genre tropes to their limits with memorable characters like Fogell (Christopher Mintz-Plasse) and the two incompetent cops played by Bill Hader and Seth Rogen. The writing by Rogen and Goldberg packs a lot of crude humor, but also a genuine undercurrent of friendship and separation anxiety, as the two leads face the prospect of growing apart. While the humor lands for many, the film’s treatment of women and sexuality is often problematic, largely playing into objectification and uncomfortable scenarios that don’t age well.

Be heavily warned if sexual assault, sexual objectification, and homophobic slurs are on your list—these recur throughout and are central to some of the film’s main plot points and jokes. Vomiting and spitting also pop up repeatedly, alongside ableist language and some graphic imagined violence. This is a comedy that revels in pushing buttons, so if those triggers are sensitive for you, keep that in mind before diving in.
emailReview:
Superbad is a wildly raunchy high school comedy that rides the chaos of teenage excess with unforgettable performances from Jonah Hill and Michael Cera, fueled by outrageous antics and a sharp sense of friendship anxiety.

Be prepared for: sexual assault, sexual objectification, homophobic slurs, vomiting, and graphic imagined violence.

writers: Cinco Paul, Ken Daurio, Sergio Pablos
name: Despicable Me
overview: Villainous Gru lives up to his reputation as a despicable, deplorable and downright unlikable guy when he hatches a plan to steal the moon from the sky. But he has a tough time staying on task after three orphans land in his care.
review:
Despicable Me is a surprisingly sweet twist on the villain origin story, mixing sharp comedy with heartfelt moments in a way that sets it apart from the usual animated family fare. If you ever wondered what Gru might be like if Gru met a sitcom dad, this is your movie. The tagline "Superbad. Superdad." nails the tone perfectly—it's goofy and irreverent, but the heart is genuinely there, especially once the three orphans shake up Gru’s evil plans. It’s not just another kids’ movie; it’s a sly riff on what it means to grow up and care for others, wrapped in a brightly colored, minion-filled package.

The voice cast, led by Steve Carell as Gru, nails the mix of gruffness and unexpected warmth that carries the film. The writing leans into classic villain tropes while subverting them with the chaos and charm of the kids, making for plenty of laughs and surprisingly tender moments. The visuals are bright and cartoonishly exaggerated, which helps balance the darker themes lurking beneath the surface. The plot’s moon-stealing scheme is wacky enough to keep things lively, but what really sticks is how the film handles the idea of family—messy, imperfect, but ultimately redemptive.

That said, be heavily warned if animal harm or death is a sensitive spot. The film includes multiple instances where various animals die or are abused, including a dog, cat, horse, and even a dragon, plus some scenes involving bugs. There are also mentions of child abuse, domestic violence, and dog fighting, which might catch some viewers off guard in what otherwise feels like a lighthearted animation. If those triggers are on your radar, approach with caution.
emailReview:
Despicable Me flips the villain origin story into a goofy, heartfelt romp full of sharp comedy and surprisingly warm family vibes, all brought to life by Steve Carell’s perfectly gruff yet tender Gru.

Be prepared for: multiple animal deaths including a dog, cat, horse, and dragon, scenes of dog fighting, and mentions of child abuse and domestic violence.

writers: Jane Goldman, Matthew Vaughn, Mark Millar, John Romita Jr.
name: Kick-Ass
overview: Dave Lizewski is an unnoticed high school student and comic book fan who one day decides to become a super-hero, even though he has no powers, training or meaningful reason to do so.
review:
Kick-Ass is a wild, darkly comic take on the superhero origin story, blending teen angst with brutal, no-holds-barred action. It’s like if Spider-Man’s earnestness collided head-on with Deadpool’s irreverence — only with a far grittier, blood-spattered edge. Aaron Taylor-Johnson’s underdog Dave Lizewski is a relatable every-guy thrust into a violent world where costumes don’t guarantee safety or justice. Fans of subversive comic adaptations will appreciate how Matthew Vaughn’s direction keeps it fun but uncomfortably real.

What stands out here is the film’s willingness to lean into the absurdity of an untrained kid trying to be a hero, while simultaneously delivering some genuinely brutal fight scenes and a sharp dose of dark humor. Chloë Grace Moretz as Hit Girl steals every scene she’s in with her lethal precociousness, adding a twisted mentor vibe that complicates the typical superhero formula. The tagline, “Shut up. Kick-ass.” perfectly sums up the film’s no-nonsense, in-your-face tone. It’s a mix of coming-of-age awkwardness, comic book fantasy, and violent vigilante justice that never quite softens the blow.

Be heavily warned if animal harm or death is on your list — Kick-Ass features multiple animal deaths and scenes depicting animal abuse that are hard to overlook. Those sensitive to this content should proceed with caution, as these moments are fairly prominent and unsettling within the film’s otherwise chaotic energy.
emailReview:
Kick-Ass delivers a wild, darkly comic superhero origin story with brutal fight scenes and a standout performance from Chloë Grace Moretz as the fiercely lethal Hit Girl.

Be prepared for: multiple animal deaths, animal abuse, graphic violence, intense bloodshed.

overview: A highly intelligent chimpanzee named Caesar has been living a peaceful suburban life ever since he was born. But when he gets taken to a cruel primate facility, Caesar decides to revolt against those who have harmed him.
review:
Rise of the Planet of the Apes is a smart, emotionally charged reboot that blends sci-fi thrills with a surprisingly poignant animal rights allegory. It’s got that classic “evolution meets rebellion” vibe, but this one’s elevated by Andy Serkis’s standout performance as Caesar, delivering a motion-capture role that feels genuinely alive. Fans of thoughtful blockbusters like District 9 or even the original Planet of the Apes series will find this a compelling mix of spectacle and heart, even if it occasionally leans into familiar tropes.

What really sticks here is the film’s willingness to explore the ethics of scientific experimentation through Caesar’s journey—from a peaceful suburban existence to leading a revolt against his captors. The tagline, “Evolution Becomes Revolution,” nails the tone perfectly: it’s both a literal and metaphorical uprising. Rupert Wyatt directs with enough grit to keep the tension high, while the writing by Amanda Silver and Rick Jaffa grounds the sci-fi elements in relatable family drama, especially through the human characters played by James Franco and Freida Pinto. The visuals and effects—especially the motion-capture work—push the boundaries of what you expect from an ape-centric story.

That said, be heavily warned if animal harm is a big no-go for you. The film features animal abuse, several animal deaths (including pets), and some pretty intense scenes of captivity and violence that might be rough for sensitive viewers. There’s also dog fighting and general cruelty that underscore the darker side of the story’s themes, making it a tough watch for anyone who pins those triggers.
emailReview:
Rise of the Planet of the Apes delivers a gripping blend of sci-fi spectacle and heartfelt animal rights drama, anchored by Andy Serkis’s astonishingly lifelike motion-capture performance as Caesar.

Be prepared for: animal abuse, several pet deaths, dog fighting, intense captivity scenes, and brutal violence.

name: The Butterfly Effect
overview: A young man struggles to access sublimated childhood memories. He finds a technique that allows him to travel back into the past, to occupy his childhood body and change history. However, he soon finds that every change he makes has unexpected consequences.
review:
The Butterfly Effect is a moody sci-fi thriller that rides the wave of early 2000s teen angst and time-travel paranoia. If you like your mind-benders with a side of emotional trauma and a dash of supernatural creepiness, this one’s right up your alley. Ashton Kutcher leads the charge as Evan Treborn, a guy who discovers he can hop back into his childhood body and rewrite his past—only to find that every tweak to history spirals into new, darker fallout. It’s like Donnie Darko meets The Jacket, but with more soap-opera twists and teenage melodrama.

What stands out here is the film’s grim tone and obsession with the butterfly effect itself—how small changes ripple into massive consequences. The tagline, “Change one thing. Change everything,” nails the core theme, and the movie doesn’t shy away from some pretty bleak outcomes. The narrative leans heavily into psychological trauma, memory repression, and the dangers of messing with time, all wrapped in a sometimes uneven but compelling package. The supporting cast, including Amy Smart and Melora Walters, add weight to the emotional stakes, though Ashton Kutcher’s performance carries most of the film’s questionable charm.

Heads up: This one is heavy on unsettling animal content, including the death of a horse and a cat, and has some distressing scenes involving animal abuse and dog fighting. There are also plenty of creepy crawlies—spiders, snakes, bugs—to keep the arachnophobes wary. Those sensitive to animal harm or intense psychological distress will want to approach with caution.
emailReview:
The Butterfly Effect is a moody sci-fi thriller drenched in early 2000s teen angst and supernatural creepiness, with Ashton Kutcher anchoring its dark, twisty time-travel chaos.

Be prepared for: horse death, cat death, animal abuse, dog fighting, and plenty of creepy crawlies like spiders and snakes.

overview: A group of scientists in San Francisco struggle to stay alive in the aftermath of a plague that is wiping out humanity, while Caesar tries to maintain dominance over his community of intelligent apes.

review:
Dawn of the Planet of the Apes is a smart, tense sci-fi thriller that leans hard into its post-apocalyptic vibe while balancing intense character drama. It’s not just another action-heavy blockbuster; this one feels like a thoughtful follow-up to Rise of the Planet of the Apes, with Matt Reeves at the helm giving the story some much-needed emotional weight. Fans of intelligent, morally complex franchises like The Walking Dead or even The Last of Us will appreciate how this film juggles survival stakes with the fragile politics between humans and apes. Andy Serkis’s motion-capture performance as Caesar remains the emotional core, elevating the film beyond standard CGI spectacle.

What’s most striking here is how the movie handles leadership and loyalty, especially through Caesar’s efforts to maintain peace in his community while dealing with a dangerous internal rival, Koba. The tagline “The future is worth fighting for” really hits home as both sides wrestle with trust and fear in a world falling apart. The film’s visuals—lush forests contrasted with ruined San Francisco—underscore the sense of a world in flux, while the human and ape conflict feels grounded rather than cartoonish. It’s a solid blend of blockbuster thrills and thoughtful storytelling, with Gary Oldman and Keri Russell adding strong support as the human survivors.

Those who pin the animal death and abuse triggers should be cautious here—there’s significant animal harm depicted, including the deaths of dogs, horses, cats, and other creatures that might upset sensitive viewers. Also, spiders, snakes, and various bugs appear, which could be a surprise for anyone with arachnophobia or entomophobia. Be warned if animal suffering is a major red flag for you, as it plays a notable role in the film’s darker moments.
emailReview:
Dawn of the Planet of the Apes is a smart, tense sci-fi thriller that blends emotional depth with gripping post-apocalyptic survival and features Andy Serkis’s standout motion-capture performance as Caesar.

Be prepared for: multiple animal deaths including dogs and horses, intense animal suffering, and unsettling scenes with spiders and snakes.

tagline: How do you wake up from a nightmare if you’re not asleep?

name: Die Hard with a Vengeance
overview: New York detective John McClane is back and kicking bad-guy butt in the third installment of this action-packed series, which finds him teaming with civilian Zeus Carver to prevent the loss of innocent lives. McClane thought he'd seen it all, until a genius named Simon engages McClane, his new "partner" -- and his beloved city -- in a deadly game that demands their concentration.
tagline: Think fast. Look alive. Die hard.
review:
Pretty amazing that the third film in a franchise can still feel so exciting, but this one pulls it off extremely well. Absolutely breathless action, with a lot of added suspense, thanks to many bomb-defusing scenes requiring quick-thinking and a delicate touch.

Bruce Willis is great once again as our favorite everyman action hero, John McClane. Samuel L. Jackson is a breath of fresh air, bringing quick-wit and a sharp tongue to new character Zeus Carver, and Jeremy Irons brings gravitas, a knowing smile, and a commanding voice to his role as Simon.
It’s an absolute blast for action fans to watch. 

Keep in mind: it’s a very violent film, so those with pinned triggers relating to violence, blood, and death: be heavily warned. Also, pretty loaded with racially-motivated arguments and language, so those who are sensitive to possible hate speech or slurs will want to glance at those respective triggers prior to a viewing. 

Special note: If you pinned the triggers involving car crashes or screeching tires and car horns, this will not be an easy watch at all.
emailReview:
Die Hard with a Vengeance delivers breathless action and sharp-witted banter, with Bruce Willis and Samuel L. Jackson lighting up the screen amid high-stakes suspense and bomb-defusing tension.

Be prepared for: intense violence, racially charged language, brutal car crashes, and lots of blood.

directors: Ron Clements, John Musker, Don Hall, Chris Williams
writers: Jared Bush, Ron Clements, John Musker, Chris Williams, Don Hall, Pamela Ribon, Aaron Kandell, Jordan Kandell
name: Moana
overview: In Ancient Polynesia, when a terrible curse incurred by Maui reaches an impetuous Chieftain's daughter's island, she answers the Ocean's call to seek out the demigod to set things right.

writers: Scott Neustadter, Michael H. Weber, John Green
name: The Fault in Our Stars
overview: Despite the tumor-shrinking medical miracle that has bought her a few years, Hazel has never been anything but terminal, her final chapter inscribed upon diagnosis. But when a patient named Augustus Waters suddenly appears at Cancer Kid Support Group, Hazel's story is about to be completely rewritten.
tagline: Life doesn't have to be perfect for love to be extraordinary.

name: Inside Man
overview: When an armed, masked gang enter a Manhattan bank, lock the doors and take hostages, the detective assigned to effect their release enters negotiations preoccupied with corruption charges he is facing.
tagline: It looked like the perfect bank robbery. But you can’t judge a crime by its cover.

name: The Others
overview: Grace is a religious woman who lives in an old house kept dark because her two children, Anne and Nicholas, have a rare sensitivity to light. When the family begins to suspect the house is haunted, Grace fights to protect her children at any cost in the face of strange events and disturbing visions.
tagline: Sooner or later they’ll find you.

writers: Shay Hatten, Michael Finch, Derek Kolstad
name: John Wick: Chapter 4
overview: With the price on his head ever increasing, John Wick uncovers a path to defeating The High Table. But before he can earn his freedom, Wick must face off against a new enemy with powerful alliances across the globe and forces that turn old friends into foes.
tagline: No way back, one way out.
review:
John Wick: Chapter 4 cranks up the action to full-throttle in this global assassin showdown. If you’re a fan of the series’ signature blend of slick choreography and relentless pacing, this installment delivers more of the same—but with an expanded scope and even higher stakes. It feels like John Wick meets a globe-trotting spy thriller, with Keanu Reeves still owning the role with a stoic intensity that anchors the chaos. While it doesn’t reinvent the wheel, it certainly spins it faster and sharper than its predecessors.

What stands out in this chapter is the way it deepens the underworld mythology without losing sight of the visceral punch. The tagline “No way back, one way out” perfectly captures the sense of no-escape tension that propels the story, as John Wick faces enemies who blur the lines between friend and foe. The supporting cast, including Donnie Yen and Bill Skarsgård, add intriguing layers to the mix, upping the stakes and injecting fresh energy. Chad Stahelski’s direction keeps the visual storytelling tight and stylish, with fight scenes that are brutal ballets and a score that pulsates with urgency.

Heads up for those sensitive to intense violence and emotional hits: the film includes several heavy triggers like a dog dying, a kid dying, and disturbing scenes of people being burned alive. There’s also jump scares, flashing lights, and graphic blood and gore. If those topics are on your list, be prepared for a relentless and often grim ride.
emailReview:
John Wick: Chapter 4 ramps up its signature slick action and globe-trotting scope with brutal fight choreography and Keanu Reeves’ unflappable intensity keeping the chaos grounded.

Be prepared for: a dog dying, a kid dying, people burned alive, graphic blood and gore, and jump scares.

name: The Blind Side
overview: The story of Michael Oher, a homeless and traumatized boy who became an All American football player and first round NFL draft pick with the help of a caring woman and her family.
tagline: Based on the extraordinary true story

writers: Joel Coen, Ethan Coen, Charles Portis
name: True Grit
overview: Following the murder of her father by a hired hand, a 14-year-old farm girl sets out to capture the killer. To aid her, she hires the toughest U.S. Marshal she can find—a man with 'true grit'—Reuben J. 'Rooster' Cogburn.
tagline: Punishment comes one way or another.
review:
True Grit is a classic Western through and through, but elevated by the Coen brothers’ trademark blend of grit and dark humor. It’s a revenge tale that doesn’t just lean on shootouts and dusty trails—there’s a sharp, almost literary quality to the dialogue, and Hailee Steinfeld’s portrayal of the fierce 14-year-old Mattie Ross really anchors the film. Jeff Bridges as Rooster Cogburn is grizzled and grumpy in just the right way, making this feel like True Grit meets a Coen-ified The Searchers. Fans of Westerns or character-driven dramas will find plenty to appreciate here, even if the pacing is a bit more deliberate than your average action flick.

What stands out most is how the movie balances its old-school Western vibes with a subtle modern sensibility. The tagline “Punishment comes one way or another” sets the tone for a story that’s less about glory and more about stubborn justice. The Coens’ screenplay is sharp, filled with dry wit and memorable lines, while the cinematography captures the unforgiving landscape that mirrors the harshness of the characters’ lives. It’s a story about determination and morality, with Mattie’s relentless pursuit of her father’s killer driving the narrative forward. The supporting cast—including Matt Damon and Josh Brolin—adds depth without stealing the spotlight.

Heads up for anyone sensitive to animal-related triggers: this film features multiple scenes involving animal deaths and abuse, including horses and dogs. There’s also a fair share of creepy critters like spiders and snakes, which might catch some viewers off guard. If you’re someone who’s triggered by animal harm or death, be prepared—these moments are woven into the gritty realism of the Western setting and aren’t exactly skippable.
emailReview:
True Grit delivers a classic Western vibe with the Coen brothers’ signature dark humor and sharp dialogue, anchored by Hailee Steinfeld’s fierce performance as Mattie Ross.

Be prepared for: multiple scenes of animal deaths including horses and dogs, animal abuse, spiders, and snakes.

name: Lord of War
overview: Yuri Orlov is a globetrotting arms dealer and, through some of the deadliest war zones, he struggles to stay one step ahead of a relentless Interpol agent, his business rivals and even some of his customers who include many of the world’s most notorious dictators. Finally, he must also face his own conscience.
tagline: Where there's a will, there's a weapon.

overview: Inspired by a true story, a comedy centered on a 27-year-old guy who learns of his cancer diagnosis and his subsequent struggle to beat the disease.
tagline: It takes a pair to beat the odds.

writers: Halsted Welles, Michael Brandt, Derek Haas, Elmore Leonard
name: 3:10 to Yuma
overview: In Arizona in the late 1800s, infamous outlaw Ben Wade and his vicious gang of thieves and murderers have plagued the Southern Railroad. When Wade is captured, Civil War veteran Dan Evans, struggling to survive on his drought-plagued ranch, volunteers to deliver him alive to the "3:10 to Yuma", a train that will take the killer to trial.

writers: Matt Charman, Ethan Coen, Joel Coen
name: Bridge of Spies
overview: During the Cold War, the Soviet Union captures U.S. pilot Francis Gary Powers after shooting down his U-2 spy plane. Sentenced to 10 years in prison, Powers' only hope is New York lawyer James Donovan, recruited by a CIA operative to negotiate his release. Donovan boards a plane to Berlin, hoping to win the young man's freedom through a prisoner exchange. If all goes well, the Russians would get Rudolf Abel, the convicted spy who Donovan defended in court.
tagline: In the shadow of war, one man showed the world what we stood for.

name: The Royal Tenenbaums
overview: Royal Tenenbaum and his wife Etheline had three children and then they separated. All three children are extraordinary --- all geniuses. Virtually all memory of the brilliance of the young Tenenbaums was subsequently erased by two decades of betrayal, failure, and disaster. Most of this was generally considered to be their father's fault. "The Royal Tenenbaums" is the story of the family's sudden, unexpected reunion one recent winter.
tagline: Family isn't a word... it's a sentence.

writers: Ryan Coogler, Aaron Covington, Sylvester Stallone
name: Creed
overview: The former World Heavyweight Champion Rocky Balboa serves as a trainer and mentor to Adonis Johnson, the son of his late friend and former rival Apollo Creed.
tagline: Your legacy is more than a name.

name: Seven Pounds
overview: An IRS agent with a fateful secret embarks on an extraordinary journey of redemption by forever changing the lives of seven strangers.
tagline: Seven names. Seven strangers. One secret.

name: Moulin Rouge
overview: A celebration of love and creative inspiration takes place in the infamous, gaudy and glamorous Parisian nightclub, at the cusp of the 20th century. A young poet, who is plunged into the heady world of Moulin Rouge, begins a passionate affair with the club's most notorious and beautiful star.
tagline: The greatest thing you'll ever learn is just to love.... and be loved in return.

writers: John Musker, Ron Clements, Hans Christian Andersen, Howard Ashman, Gerrit Graham, Sam Graham, Chris Hubbell
name: The Little Mermaid
overview: This colorful adventure tells the story of an impetuous mermaid princess named Ariel who falls in love with the very human Prince Eric and puts everything on the line for the chance to be with him. Memorable songs and characters -- including the villainous sea witch Ursula.
tagline: Somewhere under the sea and beyond your imagination is an adventure in fantasy.
review:
The Little Mermaid is a classic Disney animated musical that still sparkles decades after its 1989 release. It’s a fairy tale fantasy with catchy songs, colorful underwater visuals, and a plucky heroine in Ariel who’s willing to risk everything for love. Think of it as a cornerstone of the Disney Renaissance era—fans of animated musicals and fairy tale retellings will appreciate its timeless charm, even if it leans on some well-worn genre tropes. It’s not quite as sharp or subversive as later Disney outings, but it’s really beautiful in its world-building and character design.

What stands out here is the vibrant animation and memorable voice work—Jodi Benson’s Ariel is instantly iconic, and Pat Carroll’s Ursula is deliciously wicked. The story’s tagline, “Somewhere under the sea and beyond your imagination is an adventure in fantasy,” captures the film’s escapist spirit well. The narrative is straightforward but effective, with themes of self-discovery, sacrifice, and the classic battle between good and evil. The score, especially songs like “Part of Your World” and “Under the Sea,” is a major highlight, helping this film endure as a family favorite.

Heads up for sensitive viewers: this film features multiple instances of animal deaths and distress, including a dog, cat, horse, and other creatures, which can be tough for animal lovers. There’s also a car crash and some mild instances of possession and bugs that might catch some off guard. Those who pin the animal death or harm triggers should be cautious going in.
emailReview:
The Little Mermaid dazzles with its vibrant animation and unforgettable voice performances, especially Jodi Benson’s iconic Ariel and Pat Carroll’s wicked Ursula, making it a timeless Disney classic full of charm and catchy tunes.

Be prepared for: multiple animal deaths including a dog and horse, a car crash, mild possession, and unsettling bug scenes.

writers: Ben Affleck, Aaron Stockard, Dennis Lehane
name: Gone Baby Gone
overview: When 4 year old Amanda McCready disappears from her home and the police make little headway in solving the case, the girl's aunt, Beatrice McCready hires two private detectives, Patrick Kenzie and Angie Gennaro. The detectives freely admit that they have little experience with this type of case, but the family wants them for two reasons - they're not cops and they know the tough neighborhood in which they all live. As the case progresses, Kenzie and Gennaro face drug dealers, gangs and pedophiles. When they are about to solve the case, they are faced with a moral dilemma that tears them apart.
tagline: Everyone wants the truth... until they find it.

writers: John Lasseter, Andrew Stanton, Josh Cooley, Valerie LaPointe, Rashida Jones, Will McCormack, Martin Hynes, Stephany Folsom
name: Toy Story 4
overview: Woody has always been confident about his place in the world and that his priority is taking care of his kid, whether that's Andy or Bonnie. But when Bonnie adds a reluctant new toy called "Forky" to her room, a road trip adventure alongside old and new friends will show Woody how big the world can be for a toy.

name: Office Space
overview: Three office workers strike back at their evil employers by hatching a hapless attempt to embezzle money.

name: RoboCop
overview: In a violent, near-apocalyptic Detroit, evil corporation Omni Consumer Products wins a contract from the city government to privatize the police force. To test their crime-eradicating cyborgs, the company leads street cop Alex Murphy into an armed confrontation with crime lord Boddicker so they can use his body to support their untested RoboCop prototype. But when RoboCop learns of the company's nefarious plans, he turns on his masters.
tagline: Part man, part machine, all cop.
review:
RoboCop is a gritty, satirical sci-fi action classic that blends dystopian noir with pulpy ’80s violence and dark humor. Paul Verhoeven’s direction leans into the film’s cynical take on corporate greed and privatized law enforcement, making it feel like Blade Runner meets Robocop meets a cautionary news report on capitalism gone wild. Peter Weller’s stiff but compelling portrayal of Alex Murphy, the cop turned cyborg, grounds the spectacle with a tragic core. While some effects and action scenes feel dated, the film’s biting social commentary and over-the-top villains keep it sharply entertaining even decades later.

What really stands out is the film’s tone—equal parts brutal and absurd—which is underscored by Michael Miner and Edward Neumeier’s clever script. The tagline “Part man, part machine, all cop” perfectly sums up the moral and physical battles at play, as RoboCop struggles with his humanity while dismantling the corrupt system that created him. The world-building is vivid, with a near-apocalyptic Detroit that feels both familiar and exaggerated, and the supporting cast—including Nancy Allen as the loyal Officer Anne Lewis and Kurtwood Smith as the sadistic crime lord Boddicker—adds memorable flavor. The movie doesn’t shy away from gore or bleak moments, but it’s all in service of a story about identity, power, and resistance.

Heads up: this movie is heavy on animal-related triggers. There are multiple instances of animal deaths and abuse, including a dog dying and dog fighting, which might be tough to watch. Plus, the sound design includes some unsettling animal noises that could be distressing if you’re sensitive to that. If these are on your list, be prepared for some rough scenes alongside the human carnage.
emailReview: RoboCop is a gritty, satirical sci-fi action classic that mixes dystopian noir with dark humor and a biting take on corporate greed, anchored by Peter Weller’s compelling cyborg cop performance. Be prepared for: dog death, dog fighting, animal abuse, unsettling animal noises, and intense human violence.

writers: Jane Goldman, Matthew Vaughn, Neil Gaiman, Charles Vess
name: Stardust
overview: In a countryside town bordering on a magical land, a young man makes a promise to his beloved that he'll retrieve a fallen star by venturing into the magical realm. His journey takes him into a world beyond his wildest dreams and reveals his true identity.
tagline: This summer a star falls. The chase begins.

name: Train to Busan
overview: When a zombie virus pushes Korea into a state of emergency, those trapped on an express train to Busan must fight for their own survival.

name: Lethal Weapon
overview: A veteran cop and an unstable detective become partners who must put their differences aside in order to bring down a heroin-smuggling ring run by ex-Special Forces.
tagline: If these two can learn to stand each other... the bad guys don't stand a chance.

writers: Eric Roth, Martin Scorsese, David Grann
name: Killers of the Flower Moon
overview: When oil is discovered in 1920s Oklahoma under Osage Nation land, the Osage people are murdered one by one—until the FBI steps in to unravel the mystery.
tagline: Can you find the wolves in this picture?

name: End of Watch
overview: Two young officers are marked for death after confiscating a small cache of money and firearms from the members of a notorious cartel during a routine traffic stop.
tagline: Every moment of your life they stand watch

name: Eastern Promises
overview: A Russian teenager, living in London, dies during childbirth but leaves clues to a midwife in her journal, that could tie her child to a rape involving a violent Russian mob family.

name: The Reader
overview: The story of Michael Berg, a German lawyer who, as a teenager in the late 1950s, had an affair with an older woman, Hanna, who then disappeared only to resurface years later as one of the defendants in a war crimes trial stemming from her actions as a concentration camp guard late in the war. He alone realizes that Hanna is illiterate and may be concealing that fact at the expense of her freedom.
tagline: Behind the mystery lies a truth that will make you question everything you know.

name: Hell or High Water
overview: A divorced dad and his ex-con brother resort to a desperate scheme in order to save their family's farm in West Texas.

name: The Boondock Saints
overview: With a God-inspired moral obligation to act against evil, twin brothers Conner and Murphy set out to rid Boston of criminals. However, rather than working within the system, these Irish Americans decide to take swift retribution into their own hands.
tagline: Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done.
review:
The Boondock Saints is that cult classic vigilante flick that leans hard into its own mythos, blending crime thriller with darkly comic religious fervor. It feels like a grittier, more stylized take on the classic “good guys taking justice into their own hands” trope—think a Boston-born, Irish-American answer to something like Fight Club with a holy mission twist. While it’s not exactly high art, the film’s pulpy charm and over-the-top bravado have earned it a devoted following, even if the moral ambiguity sometimes feels a little on the nose.

What stands out most is the swagger of the MacManus twins, played by Sean Patrick Flanery and Norman Reedus, who give the film its heart and swagger, while Willem Dafoe’s eccentric detective Paul Smecker adds some much-needed quirky energy. Troy Duffy’s direction embraces stylized violence and brooding urban grit, and the religious undertones—“Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done.”—give the story an oddly Shakespearean flair. The film thrives on its blend of brotherhood, justice, and a twisted sense of divine duty, even if that sometimes leads to questionable ethical territory.

Be heavily warned if the idea of animal harm is on your list—there’s a cat death here that might catch you off guard. Beyond that, the film dives into some pretty graphic vigilante violence, so if you’re sensitive to that, tread carefully.
emailReview:
The Boondock Saints packs gritty Boston swagger and darkly comic vigilante justice with standout performances from the MacManus twins and Willem Dafoe’s delightfully quirky detective.

Be prepared for: a shocking cat death, graphic gun violence, and intense scenes of vigilante brutality.

name: The Whale
overview: A reclusive English teacher suffering from severe obesity attempts to reconnect with his estranged teenage daughter for one last chance at redemption.

name: 21 Grams
overview: This is the story of three gentle persons: Paul Rivers, an ailing mathematician lovelessly married to an English émigré; Christina Peck, an upper-middle-class suburban housewife, happily married and mother of two little girl; and Jack Jordan, an ex-convict who has found in his Christian faith the strength to raise a family. They will be brought together by a terrible accident that will change their lives. By the final frame, none of them will be the same as they will learn harsh truths about love, faith, courage, desire and guilt, and how chance can change our worlds irretrievably—forever.

name: Sinners
overview: Trying to leave their troubled lives behind, twin brothers return to their hometown to start again, only to discover that an even greater evil is waiting to welcome them back.
review:
Quite a genre-bender of a film, mixing horror with historical drama, even adding in elements from musicals and comedies. Lots of well-deserved awards nominations, and it will definitely win quite a few of those nomination categories. 

Many have compared this feature with the film, From Dusk Till Dawn, and that is fairly accurate. Personally, I view the comparison as a big compliment, but Sinners contributes its own unique vision, allowing it to stand on its own in the big world of monsters and undead horror.
emailReview:
Sinners is a wild genre mashup that flips between horror, historical drama, musicals, and comedy with enough flair to earn serious awards buzz and carve out its own monstrous legacy.

Be prepared for: brutal vampire attacks, intense undead violence, graphic blood splatter, and a gritty atmosphere that blends gore with dark humor.

name: Match Point
overview: Match Point is Woody Allen’s satire of the British High Society and the ambition of a young tennis instructor to enter into it. Yet when he must decide between two women - one assuring him his place in high society, and the other that would take him far from it - palms start to sweat and a dark psychological match in his head begins.

tagline: The Happiest, Dopiest, Grumpiest, Sneeziest movie of the year.

primaryTitle: Close Encounters of the Third Kind
writers: Steven Spielberg, Hal Barwood, Jerry Belson, John Hill, Matthew Robbins
Title_IMDb_Link: Close Encounters of the Third Kind
name: Close Encounters of the Third Kind
cleanNameArticles: close encounters of the third kind
overview: After an encounter with UFOs, a line worker feels undeniably drawn to an isolated area in the wilderness where something spectacular is about to happen.
review:
Steven Spielberg’s *Close Encounters of the Third Kind* is a classic sci-fi drama that still holds up as a thoughtful, awe-inspiring exploration of humanity’s place in the universe. It’s less about flashy alien battles and more about subtle wonder, obsession, and connection. Think of it as *E.T.*’s more serious, slower-burning cousin — fans of thoughtful, character-driven sci-fi will appreciate its deliberate pacing and iconic moments. Richard Dreyfuss shines as Roy Neary, a man irresistibly drawn to a mysterious convergence in the wilderness, capturing the mix of confusion and wonder that defines the film.

What really stands out here is Spielberg’s ability to build tension and curiosity without heavy-handed effects or constant action. The tagline “We are not alone” captures the film’s hopeful yet eerie tone perfectly. The storytelling leans into the idea that contact with the unknown is transformative and deeply personal. The score, with its famous five-tone motif, is unforgettable and plays a key role in communicating the alien encounter’s significance. The supporting cast, including François Truffaut as the enigmatic scientist, adds an international flavor that broadens the film’s scope beyond a simple American UFO story.

That said, be warned if you’re sensitive to animal-related content. The film features multiple instances of animal deaths and abuse, including a dog, horse, and cat, as well as scenes involving spiders, snakes, and bugs that might unsettle arachnophobes or entomophobes. Those who pin the “animal harm” or “animal death” triggers should approach with caution.
emailReview:
Steven Spielberg’s *Close Encounters of the Third Kind* offers a slow-burning, awe-filled exploration of humanity’s connection to the unknown, anchored by Richard Dreyfuss’s captivating performance and a haunting, iconic score.

Be prepared for: multiple animal deaths including a dog, horse, and cat, as well as unsettling scenes with spiders, snakes, and bugs.

name: The Raid
overview: Deep in the heart of Jakarta's slums lies an impenetrable safe house for the world's most dangerous killers and gangsters. Until now, the run-down apartment block has been considered untouchable to even the bravest of police. Cloaked under the cover of pre-dawn darkness and silence, an elite swat team is tasked with raiding the safe house in order to take down the notorious drug lord that runs it.  But when a chance encounter with a spotter blows their cover and news of their assault reaches the drug lord, the building's lights are cut and all the exits blocked. Stranded on the sixth floor with no way out, the unit must fight their way through the city's worst to survive their mission. Starring Indonesian martial arts sensation Iko Uwais.
tagline: 1 Ruthless Crime Lord, 20 Elite Cops, 30 Floors of Hell.

writers: Alex Proyas, Lem Dobbs, David S. Goyer
name: Dark City
overview: A man struggles with memories of his past, including a wife he cannot remember, in a nightmarish world with no sun and run by beings with telekinetic powers who seek the souls of humans.
tagline: They built the city to see what makes us tick. Last night, one of us went off.

name: Falling Down
overview: An ordinary man frustrated with the various flaws he sees in society begins to psychotically and violently lash out against them.
tagline: The adventures of an ordinary man at war with the everyday world.

writers: George Langelaan, Charles Edward Pogue, David Cronenberg
name: The Fly
overview: When Seth Brundle makes a huge scientific and technological breakthrough in teleportation, he decides to test it on himself. Unbeknownst to him, a common housefly manages to get inside the device and the two become one.

name: Another Round
overview: It is time to sweep off the dust of everyday life. A Norwegian philosopher argues man is born with a blood alcohol level that is 0.5% too low. Inspired by that theory Martin and three of his friends and high school teachers launch a drinking experiment. Their mundane existence is an endless row of trivialities so this project might be exactly what they need. It is all about living life to the fullest! If Churchill won WW2 in a heavy daze of alcohol, imagine how the powerful drops can affect the daily humdrum? The four teachers - and a handful of students - decide to uphold a constant level of intoxication. Under the influence our four friends become braver, more musical, teaching grows interesting amd results soar. The group feels alive again! As the units are knocked back the experiment both progresses and derails. It becomes clear that while alcohol historically has fuelled great results, all actions have consequences.
tagline: What is youth? A dream. What is love? The content of the dream.

name: The Birds
overview: Chic socialite Melanie Daniels enjoys a passing flirtation with an eligible attorney in a San Francisco pet shop and, on an impulse, follows him to his hometown bearing a gift of lovebirds. But upon her arrival, the bird population runs amok. Suddenly, the townsfolk face a massive avian onslaught, with the feathered fiends inexplicably attacking people all over Bodega Bay.
tagline: ...and remember, the next scream you hear may be your own!

name: Lola
overview: Lola receives a phone call from her boyfriend Manni. He lost 100,000 DM in a subway train that belongs to a very bad guy. She has 20 minutes to raise this amount and meet Manni. Otherwise, he will rob a store to get the money. Three different alternatives may happen depending on some minor event along Lola's run.
tagline: Every second of every day you're faced with a decision that can change your life.

name: Dazed And Confused
overview: The adventures of a group of Texas teens on their last day of school in 1976, centering on student Randall Floyd, who moves easily among stoners, jocks and geeks. Floyd is a star athlete, but he also likes smoking weed, which presents a conundrum when his football coach demands he sign a "no drugs" pledge.
tagline: It was the last day of school in 1976. A time they'd never forget. (If only they could remember)

writers: Richard Maibaum, Paul Dehn, Ian Fleming, Johanna Harwood, Berkely Mather
name: Goldfinger
overview: Special agent 007 comes face to face with one of the most notorious villains of all time, and now he must outwit and outgun the powerful tycoon to prevent him from cashing in on a devious scheme to raid Fort Knox -- and obliterate the world's economy.
tagline: Everything he touches turns into excitement!

name: Adaptation
overview: A love-lorn script writer grows increasingly desperate in his quest to adapt the book 'The Orchid Thief'.
tagline: From the creator of Being John Malkovich, comes the story about the creator of Being John Malkovich.

primaryTitle: What We Do in the Shadows
Title_IMDb_Link: What We Do in the Shadows
name: What We Do in the Shadows
cleanNameArticles: what we do in the shadows
overview: Vampire housemates try to cope with the complexities of modern life and show a newly turned hipster some of the perks of being undead.
review:
What We Do in the Shadows is a brilliantly offbeat mockumentary that tosses vampires into the mundane mess of modern life with hilarious results. This 2014 cult favorite by Jemaine Clement and Taika Waititi feels like The Office meets classic vampire lore, and it’s a wild ride of awkward immortals fumbling through everything from dating apps to energy drinks. It’s not your typical horror-comedy — it leans hard into the deadpan absurdity and character-driven humor, making it a must-watch for fans of quirky, smart genre mashups.

The film’s charm largely comes from its wonderfully awkward ensemble, especially Jemaine Clement’s Vladislav and Taika Waititi’s Viago, whose chemistry anchors the chaos. The tagline, “Some interviews with some vampires,” perfectly captures the mockumentary’s tone — just casual, deadpan conversations that reveal the hilarious struggles of undead roommates. The writing cleverly pokes fun at vampire clichés while grounding it in relatable themes like friendship, loneliness, and adapting to change. Plus, the subtle use of low-key practical effects keeps the silliness grounded without overshadowing the humor.

Heads up to anyone sensitive to animal-related content: this one is heavy on animal deaths and abuse, including a dog, horse, cat, and other creatures meeting grim fates. There’s also some unsettling body horror and bug-related scenes that might sneak up on you. If you’re on the lookout for triggers involving animals or creepy crawlies, proceed with caution.
emailReview: What We Do in the Shadows is a brilliantly offbeat mockumentary that blends deadpan humor with vampire lore, anchored by a delightfully awkward ensemble led by Jemaine Clement and Taika Waititi. Be prepared for: multiple animal deaths including a dog and horse, unsettling body horror, and creepy bug scenes that add a surprising edge to the laughs.

writers: Terry Hayes, George Miller, Brian Hannant, Byron Kennedy
name: Mad Max 2
overview: Max Rockatansky returns as the heroic loner who drives the dusty roads of a postapocalyptic Australian Outback in an unending search for gasoline. Arrayed against him and the other scraggly defendants of a fuel-depot encampment are the bizarre warriors commanded by the charismatic Lord Humungus, a violent leader whose scruples are as barren as the surrounding landscape.
tagline: Just one man can make a difference.

name: The Thin Red Line
overview: Based on the graphic novel by James Jones, The Thin Red Line tells the story of a group of men, an Army Rifle company called C-for-Charlie, who change, suffer, and ultimately make essential discoveries about themselves during the fierce World War II battle of Guadalcanal. It follows their journey, from the surprise of an unopposed landing, through the bloody and exhausting battles that follow, to the ultimate departure of those who survived. A powerful frontline cast - including Sean Penn, Nick Nolte, Woody Harrelson and George Clooney - explodes into action in this hauntingly realistic view of military and moral chaos in the Pacific during World War II.
tagline: Every man fights his own war.

primaryTitle: The Naked Gun: From the Files of Police Squad!
writers: Jerry Zucker, Jim Abrahams, David Zucker, Pat Proft
Title_IMDb_Link: The Naked Gun: From the Files of Police Squad!
name: The Naked Gun: From the Files of Police Squad!
cleanName: naked gun from files police squad
cleanNameArticles: naked gun from the files of police squad
overview: When the bumbling Lieutenant Frank Drebin investigates events following the shooting of his partner, he stumbles upon an assassination plot.
tagline: You've read the ad, now see the movie!
review:
The Naked Gun: From the Files of Police Squad! is a classic ’80s slapstick crime comedy that’s as relentlessly goofy as it is quotable. If you like your humor absurd, fast-paced, and full of pun-laden sight gags, this film is a must-watch—think Airplane! meets a police procedural farce. Leslie Nielsen’s deadpan performance as the bumbling Lt. Frank Drebin anchors the chaos, turning what could have been a standard spoof into a comedy staple that still holds up decades later. It’s not just a film; it’s a barrage of jokes that rarely lets up, which will delight fans of classic Zucker, Abrahams, and Zucker humor.

What stands out here is the way the film gleefully subverts typical cop thriller tropes, turning everything from assassination plots to high-speed chases into opportunities for ridiculous pratfalls and visual puns. The tagline “You’ve read the ad, now see the movie!” perfectly captures the self-aware, irreverent tone. The film’s writing is packed with layered gags—from a priceless unbreakable pen causing chaos to one of the most infamous “Nice beaver” jokes involving a taxidermy mount. The physical comedy is complemented by some surprisingly elaborate set pieces, like the erratic police car driving through wildly inappropriate places and a chaotic baseball game sequence. While it’s mostly lighthearted, the film doesn’t shy away from absurdly over-the-top violence of the cartoony kind, all delivered with a wink.

Heads up for sensitive viewers: this movie features a number of triggers related to animal harm—real goldfish are shown in distress and dying, which can be unsettling. There’s also gun violence and mild blood/gore, though it’s handled in a slapstick, non-gratuitous way. Sexual content and objectification show up as frequent jokes and sight gags, including some scenes involving nudity (mostly implied or from behind) and a particularly uncomfortable sequence where Frank accidentally gropes a woman. Physical mishaps like falls and unconsciousness are common, all played for laughs but potentially jarring in their frequency and some of the absurd violent outcomes. If any of these sound like dealbreakers, consider watching with a heads-up.
emailReview:
Leslie Nielsen’s deadpan charm anchors this relentlessly goofy ’80s slapstick that turns every cop cliché into a pun-filled punchline, making it a timeless comedy riot.

Be prepared for: goldfish distress and death, slapstick gun violence, accidental groping, and chaotic physical mishaps.

name: Evil Dead II
overview: Ash Williams and his girlfriend Linda find a log cabin in the woods with a voice recording from an archeologist who had recorded himself reciting ancient chants from "The Book of the Dead." As they play the recording an evil power is unleashed taking over Linda's body.
review:
Evil Dead II is a cult classic that rides the fine line between horror and slapstick comedy, making it a wild ride for fans of campy scares and over-the-top gore. Directed by Sam Raimi and starring Bruce Campbell as the ever-grimacing Ash Williams, it’s the kind of film that feels like Peter Jackson’s early splatter antics meet a haunted house gone absolutely bonkers. If you love your horror with a side of absurdity and some genuinely inventive practical effects, this one’s a must-watch — though it’s definitely not for the faint of heart or those expecting subtlety.

What stands out here is the way the film leans hard into its tagline, “Kiss your nerves goodbye!” The premise is classic haunted cabin fare — a cursed tape unleashing evil forces — but the execution is anything but typical. The practical effects, from possessed limbs to demonic transformations, are wildly creative and still hold up as a testament to DIY horror ingenuity. Bruce Campbell’s performance as Ash adds a lot of charm, mixing bravado with genuine terror that keeps the film from becoming a pure parody. Plus, the soundtrack and pacing keep the tension high while allowing for some genuinely hilarious moments amidst the chaos.

Heads up for anyone sensitive to animal harm and death: this movie includes multiple scenes involving animals dying or being harmed, including a dog, a horse, and a cat, as well as some unsettling imagery with bugs, spiders, and snakes. Those who pin the animal abuse or death triggers should be cautious — it’s an unsettling part of the film’s atmosphere rather than a standalone shock, but it’s definitely there. If those elements are a dealbreaker, this one might not be your cup of tea.
emailReview:
Evil Dead II is a wild cult classic that perfectly blends slapstick comedy with inventive practical gore, anchored by Bruce Campbell’s unforgettable performance as Ash Williams.

Be prepared for: graphic animal deaths including a dog, horse, and cat, creepy insect and spider scenes, and unsettling snake imagery.

name: 25Th Hour
overview: In New York City in the days following the events of 9/11, Monty Brogan is a convicted drug dealer about to start a seven-year prison sentence, and his final hours of freedom are devoted to hanging out with his closest buddies and trying to prepare his girlfriend for his extended absence.
tagline: Can you change your whole life in one day?
review:
Spike Lee’s 2002 drama 25th Hour is a gritty, introspective character study set against the raw backdrop of post-9/11 New York City. It’s a somber meditation on regret and the weight of impending consequences, with Edward Norton anchoring the film as Monty Brogan, a man facing seven years in prison. Fans of character-driven, urban dramas like Requiem for a Dream or even early Paul Schrader will find this one resonates, though it’s less about shock and more about slow-burning emotional truth.

What stands out most is the way the film captures a city—and a man—on the edge of transformation, fraught with tension and the looming shadow of loss. The dialogue crackles with authenticity, especially in the scenes between Monty and his fiercely loyal friends, played memorably by Philip Seymour Hoffman and Barry Pepper. Spike Lee’s direction is restrained but potent, letting the dense New York atmosphere seep through every frame. The tagline, “Can you change your whole life in one day?” feels like a question Monty wrestles with throughout, making the film a poignant exploration of choice, fate, and redemption.

Those sensitive to animal-related content should be cautious here. While it’s a bit of a mess in the database, the film does contain scenes involving animal abuse and dead animals, including a horse, which could be upsetting. Additionally, viewers who flag themes like vomiting or gaslighting might want to brace themselves. The emotional weight and these darker moments make 25th Hour a tough but rewarding watch.
emailReview:
Spike Lee’s 25th Hour is a gritty, slow-burning urban drama anchored by a powerhouse performance from Edward Norton, capturing the tension and regret of a man facing life-altering consequences in post-9/11 New York City.

Be prepared for: animal abuse involving a horse, dead animals, vomiting, and gaslighting moments that add to the film’s raw emotional weight.

name: Searching
overview: After David Kim's 16-year-old daughter goes missing, a local investigation is opened and a detective is assigned to the case. But 37 hours later and without a single lead, David decides to search the one place no one has looked yet, where all secrets are kept today: his daughter's laptop.
tagline: No one is lost without a trace.

name: Thelma and Louise
overview: Whilst on a short weekend getaway, Louise shoots a man who had tried to rape Thelma. Due to the incriminating circumstances, they make a run for it and thus a cross country chase ensues for the two fugitives. Along the way, both women rediscover the strength of their friendship and surprising aspects of their personalities and self-strengths in the trying times.
tagline: Somebody said get a life...so they did.
review:
Thelma and Louise is a classic early ’90s road movie that blends feminist themes with a high-stakes crime drama, all wrapped in Ridley Scott’s sleek direction. It’s a wild ride fueled by the electric chemistry between Susan Sarandon and Geena Davis, who bring depth and grit to their characters’ desperate bid for freedom. Think of it as Thelma & Louise meets Bonnie and Clyde, but with a sharper focus on female empowerment and the complexities of friendship under pressure. It’s not just a women-on-the-run flick—it’s a cultural touchstone that still resonates today.

What stands out is how the film balances tension with moments of genuine warmth and humor, allowing the characters to grow beyond their initial stereotypes. The tagline, “Somebody said get a life...so they did,” perfectly captures that spirit of rebellion and self-discovery. Thelma and Louise’s journey is as much about breaking free from societal constraints as it is about evading the law, and the writing by Callie Khouri hits that sweet spot between melodrama and realism. Plus, the supporting cast adds texture without stealing the spotlight, keeping the focus firmly on these two unforgettable leads.

Heads up for sensitive viewers: this movie includes several instances of animal deaths and abuse, which can be jarring if you’re sensitive to that kind of content. There’s also the heavy subject matter of attempted sexual assault that kicks off the entire plot, so if those trigger your discomfort, proceed with caution. The film doesn’t shy away from harsh realities, and those moments are integral to the story’s emotional weight.
emailReview:
Thelma and Louise is a razor-sharp early ’90s road movie powered by the fierce chemistry of Susan Sarandon and Geena Davis, blending feminist grit with moments of humor and heart.

Be prepared for: attempted sexual assault, animal deaths and abuse, and intense emotional confrontations.

name: Anatomy of a Fall
overview: A woman is suspected of her husband's murder, and their blind son faces a moral dilemma as the sole witness.
review:
Anatomy of a Fall is a tense, cerebral courtroom drama that leans heavily on atmosphere and moral ambiguity, reminding me a bit of classic European legal thrillers with a modern, psychological twist. It’s less about flashy courtroom showdowns and more about the slow burn of suspicion and emotional complexity, anchored by Sandra Hüller’s quietly powerful performance as Sandra Voyter. If you’re into films that ask “Did she do it?” without handing you easy answers, this one’s a solid pick.

What stands out here is how the story folds the family’s intimate trauma into the trial’s procedural grind, especially through the perspective of their blind son, Daniel. The tagline “Did she do it?” is almost a red herring — the film’s real intrigue lies in the tension between truth, perception, and loyalty. Justine Triet’s direction along with the writing by Triet and Arthur Harari crafts a narrative that’s as much about what’s left unsaid as what’s revealed in court. The subtle performances, particularly by Milo Machado-Graner as Daniel, add a layer of emotional depth that keeps the story grounded amid its legal twists.

On the trigger front, be prepared if animal-related content is on your list: this film features a dog dying, animal abuse, and dead animals, plus indications that animals were harmed during production. Those sensitive to animal harm will definitely want to approach with caution here.
emailReview:
Anatomy of a Fall is a quietly gripping courtroom drama where moral ambiguity and intimate family trauma simmer beneath a slow-burning psychological mystery, anchored by Sandra Hüller’s compelling lead performance.

Be prepared for: a dog dying, animal abuse, dead animals, and distressing implications of animal harm during production.

name: Ponyo

tagline: Welcome to a world where anything is possible.

writers: Harry Julian Fink, Rita M. Fink, Dean Riesner, Terrence Malick, Jo Heims, John Milius
name: Dirty Harry
overview: When a madman dubbed 'Scorpio' terrorizes San Francisco, hard-nosed cop, Harry Callahan – famous for his take-no-prisoners approach to law enforcement – is tasked with hunting down the psychopath. Harry eventually collars Scorpio in the process of rescuing a kidnap victim, only to see him walk on technicalities. Now, the maverick detective is determined to nail the maniac himself.
tagline: Detective Harry Callahan. He doesn't break murder cases. He smashes them.
review:
Dirty Harry is the prototypical tough cop thriller that set the template for the anti-hero detective genre. Clint Eastwood’s gruff, no-nonsense Harry Callahan smashes through San Francisco’s criminal underbelly with a swagger that’s equal parts charm and menace. It’s hard not to see this as a blueprint for every renegade cop movie that followed—fans of gritty 70s crime dramas or later fare like *Lethal Weapon* will find plenty to chew on, though it’s definitely rougher around the edges and less polished than modern entries.

What stands out is the film’s relentless tone and the way it leans into its tagline: “He doesn’t break murder cases. He smashes them.” The moral ambiguity and procedural frustration—especially when the villain slips through legal cracks—give the story a dark, almost nihilistic edge. Don Siegel’s direction keeps things tight and gritty, while Eastwood’s performance is full of iconic one-liners and steely grit that feel like they’ve been quoted endlessly for a reason. The tension between Harry's brutal methods and the system’s limitations remains a fascinating axis for debate even today.

Heads up for animal lovers: this one’s heavy on animal-related triggers, including some disturbing deaths and abuse of animals on screen. If the thought of harmed pets or wildlife is a dealbreaker, approach with caution. Otherwise, prepare for a landmark cop thriller that’s as unapologetically tough as its lead character.
emailReview:
Dirty Harry is a gritty, no-nonsense cop thriller that defined the anti-hero detective genre with Clint Eastwood’s iconic blend of charm and menace.

Be prepared for: on-screen animal abuse, disturbing deaths of pets and wildlife, and a relentless gritty tone that doesn’t hold back on harsh realities.

writers: Stephen Chow, Kan-Cheung Tsang, Xin Huo, Man-Keung Chan
name: Kung Fu Hustle
overview: Set in Canton, China in the 1940s, the story revolves in a town ruled by the Axe Gang, Sing who desperately wants to become a member. He stumbles into a slum ruled by eccentric landlords who turns out to be the greatest kung-fu masters in disguise. Sing's actions eventually cause the Axe Gang and the slumlords to engage in an explosive kung-fu battle. Only one side will win and only one hero will emerge as the greatest kung-fu master of all.
tagline: So many gangsters… so little time.
review:
Kung Fu Hustle is a wild, genre-bending kung-fu comedy that feels like a mashup of classic Shaw Brothers martial arts flicks and Looney Tunes energy. Stephen Chow’s signature blend of slapstick humor and over-the-top action makes this one a cult favorite, especially for fans of martial arts movies with a heavy dose of absurdity and heart. It’s not your typical kung-fu film—there’s an irreverent, almost cartoonish tone that elevates the usual gangland showdown into something genuinely memorable and ridiculously fun.

What really stands out here is the way the film uses its 1940s Canton setting as a backdrop for an all-out brawl between the Axe Gang and the secret kung-fu masters disguised as quirky slum landlords. The choreography is inventive and explosive, and the characters—especially the seemingly meek Landlady and Landlord—are delightfully eccentric, turning genre stereotypes on their head. The tagline “So many gangsters… so little time” perfectly captures the breakneck pace and sheer amount of chaos packed into the story. Plus, Stephen Chow’s performance as Sing, a hapless wannabe gangster who stumbles into greatness, adds just the right mix of goofiness and charm.

Heads up for anyone sensitive to animal-related content: this movie features multiple instances of animal deaths, including dogs, cats, and a horse, as well as some scenes involving spiders and snakes. There’s also dog fighting and reports of animal harm during production, so it’s definitely one to approach cautiously if those triggers are on your list.
emailReview:
Kung Fu Hustle is a riotous kung-fu comedy that blends Looney Tunes-style slapstick with jaw-dropping martial arts mayhem, all set against a quirky 1940s Canton backdrop.

Be prepared for: multiple animal deaths including dogs, cats, and a horse, scenes with spiders and snakes, and dog fighting.

overview: Walt Disney's timeless masterpiece is an extravaganza of sight and sound! See the music come to life, hear the pictures burst into song and experience the excitement that is Fantasia over and over again.
tagline: The most sensational sound you'll ever see!
review:
Fantasia is a dazzling and ambitious blend of classical music and animation that still feels fresh despite its 1940 release. It’s less a traditional narrative and more a series of inventive visual poems set to iconic orchestral pieces, with Mickey Mouse’s “Sorcerer’s Apprentice” segment stealing the spotlight as the most memorable. Fans of experimental animation and classical music mashups will appreciate this as a foundational piece that paved the way for many music-driven visual projects since.

What really stands out is the sheer creativity and variety across the segments, from the abstract shapes dancing to Stravinsky’s Rite of Spring to the serene beauty of “Ave Maria.” The film doesn’t just entertain; it invites you to see sound itself as a living, breathing entity. The narration by Deems Taylor adds a classical concert vibe, while Leopold Stokowski’s role as conductor grounds the experience in genuine musical excellence. It’s a feast for the senses that pushes the boundaries of what animation can do when paired with a symphony.

Heads up: those sensitive to animal harm should be cautious, as there is at least one instance where an animal dies. It’s handled in the context of the music and animation, but it’s a notable emotional beat that might catch some viewers off guard.
emailReview:
Fantasia is a mesmerizing fusion of classical music and imaginative animation that still dazzles with its bold artistry and iconic moments like Mickey’s “Sorcerer’s Apprentice.”

Be prepared for: an animal death, surreal abstract imagery, and emotionally charged scenes that blend music with striking visual storytelling.

overview: A tribute to the controversial black activist and leader of the struggle for black liberation. He hit bottom during his imprisonment in the '50s, he became a Black Muslim and then a leader in the Nation of Islam. His assassination in 1965 left a legacy of self-determination and racial pride.
tagline: Scholar, convict, leader, disciple, hipster, father, hustler, minister, black man, every man.

writers: Ernesto 'Che' Guevara, Alberto Granado, Jose Rivera
name: The Motorcycle Diaries
overview: Based on the journals of Che Guevara, leader of the Cuban Revolution. In his memoirs, Guevara recounts adventures he and best friend Alberto Granado had while crossing South America by motorcycle in the early 1950s.
tagline: Let the world change you...and you can change the world.

name: Detachment
overview: A chronicle of three weeks in the lives of several high school teachers, administrators and students through the eyes of substitute teacher, Henry Barthes. Henry roams from school to school, imparting modes of knowledge, but never staying long enough to form any semblance of sentient attachment.

writers: Yasutaka Tsutsui, Seishi Minakami, Satoshi Kon
name: Paprika
overview: When a machine that allows therapists to enter their patient's dreams is stolen, all hell breaks loose. Only a young female therapist can stop it and recover it before damage is done: Paprika.
tagline: This is your brain on anime.

writers: Alan Jay Lerner, George Bernard Shaw
name: My Fair Lady
overview: A snobbish phonetics professor agrees to a wager that he can take a flower girl and make her presentable in high society.
tagline: The loverliest motion picture of them all!

writers: Rob Reiner, Andrew Scheinman, Wendelin Van Draanen
name: Flipped
overview: When Juli meets Bryce in the second grade, she knows it's true love. After spending six years trying to convince Bryce the same, she's ready to give up - until he starts to reconsider.

name: The Great Beauty
overview: Jep Gambardella has seduced his way through the lavish nightlife of Rome for decades, but after his 65th birthday and a shock from the past, Jep looks past the nightclubs and parties to find a timeless landscape of absurd, exquisite beauty.

name: The Color Purple
overview: An epic tale spanning forty years in the life of Celie, an African-American woman living in the South who survives incredible abuse and bigotry.  After Celie's abusive father marries her off to the equally debasing "Mister" Albert Johnson, things go from bad to worse, leaving Celie to find companionship anywhere she can.  She perseveres, holding on to her dream of one day being reunited with her sister in Africa. Based on the novel by Alice Walker.
tagline: It's about life. It's about love. It's about us.

writers: Claude Chabrol, Jean-Luc Godard, François Truffaut
name: À bout de souffle
overview: A young car thief kills a policeman and tries to persuade a girl to hide in Italy with him.

name: Beasts of No Nation
overview: A drama based on the experiences of Agu, a child fighting in the civil war of an unnamed, fictional West African country. Follows the journey of Agu as he's forced to join a group of soldiers. While Agu fears his commander and many of the men around him, his fledgling childhood has been brutally shattered by the war raging through his country, and he is at first torn between conflicting revulsion and fascination. Depicts the mechanics of war and does not shy away from explicit, visceral detail, painting a complex, difficult picture of Agu as a child soldier.

name: Fried Green Tomatoes
overview: Amidst her own personality crisis, southern housewife Evelyn Couch meets Ninny, an outgoing old woman who tells her the story of Idgie Threadgoode and Ruth Jamison, two young women who experienced hardships and love in Whistle Stop, Alabama in the 1920s.
tagline: The secret of life? The secret's in the sauce.

primaryTitle: The Day the Earth Stood Still
Title_IMDb_Link: The Day the Earth Stood Still
name: The Day the Earth Stood Still
overview: An alien (Klaatu) with his mighty robot (Gort) land their spacecraft on Cold War-era Earth just after the end of World War II. They bring an important message to the planet that Klaatu wishes to tell to representatives of all nations; however, communication turns out to be difficult; so, after learning something about the natives, Klaatu decides on an alternative approach.
tagline: From out of space...A warning and an ultimatum.

name: Badlands
overview: Dramatization of the Starkweather-Fugate killing spree of the 1950s, in which a teenage girl and her twenty-something boyfriend slaughtered her entire family and several others in the Dakota badlands.
tagline: In 1959 a lot of people were killing time. Kit and Holly were killing people.

name: The Man from Nowhere
overview: His only friend called him 'the man from nowhere'... Taesik, a former special agent becomes a loner after losing his wife in a miserable accident and lives a bitter life running a pawnshop. He only has a few customers and a friend named Somi, a little girl next door. As Taesik spends more and more time with Somi, he gets attached to her. Then Somi is kidnapped by a gang, and as Taesik tries to save Somi by becoming deeply associated with the gang his mysterious past is revealed...

name: Happiness
