overview: The lives of many individuals connected by the desire for happiness, often from sources usually considered dark or evil.
tagline: You want. He wants. She wants. But nobody wants what I want.

name: Mother
overview: Mother compiles clips of mother figures from classic Hollywood cinema and television dramas. The figures range from the Virgin Mary and Mother Courage, to characters from Maude (1972–78), Aliens (1986), Imitation of Life (1959), and American Gangster (2007). The characters play out scenes of care, loss, emotional manipulation, abandonment, and grief. The intense relationships between mothers and daughters are especially prominent.

name: Open Your Eyes
overview: A very handsome man finds the love of his life, but he suffers an accident and needs to have his face rebuilt by surgery after it is severely disfigured.

writers: Filippo Bologna, Paolo Costella, Paolo Genovese, Paola Mammini, Rolando Ravello
name: Perfect Strangers
overview: During a dinner, a group of friends decide to share whatever text message or phone call they will receive during the evening - and all hell breaks loose.

writers: Thornton Wilder, Sally Benson, Alma Reville, Gordon McDonell
name: Shadow of a Doubt
overview: A bored teen living in Santa Rosa, California, Charlotte "Charlie" Newton, is frustrated because nothing seems to be happening in her life and that of her family. Then, she receives wonderful news: her uncle (for whom she was named), Charlie Oakley, is arriving for a visit. But Uncle Charlie may not be the man he seems to be.
tagline: What horror did her secret life hold… that made her dread this man of her dreams?

name: A Man Called Ove
overview: Despite grumpy 59 year-old Ove being deposed as president of his condominium association, but he keeps looking over the neighbourhood with an iron fist. When pregnant Parvaneh and her family move into the terraced house opposite Ove and she accidentally back into Ove’s mailbox, it sets off a series of unexpected changes in his life.

writers: Georges Chaperot, René Wheeler, Noël-Noël, Christophe Barratier, Philippe Lopes-Curval
name: The Chorus
overview: Set in 1940's France, a new teacher at a school for disruptive boys gives hope and inspiration.

name: Night on Earth
overview: A quintet of cabbies in five cities and their remarkable fares on the same eventful night.
tagline: Five taxis. Five cities. One night.

name: Bringing Up Baby
overview: David Huxley is waiting to get a bone he needs for his museum collection. Through a series of strange circumstances, he meets Susan Vance, and the duo have a series of misadventures which include a leopard called Baby.
tagline: And so begins the hilarious adventure of Professor David Huxley and Miss Susan Vance, a flutter-brained vixen with love in her heart!

name: The Right Stuff
overview: A chronicle of the original Mercury astronauts in the formation of America's space program: Alan Shepherd, the first American in space; Gus Grissom, the benighted astronaut for whom nothing works out as planned; John Glenn, the straight-arrow 'boy scout' of the bunch who was the first American to orbit the earth; and the remaining pilots: Deke Slayton, Scott Carpenter and Wally Schirra.

name: The Salesman
overview: Forced out of their apartment due to dangerous works on a neighboring building, Emad and Rana move into a new flat in the center of Tehran. An incident linked to the previous tenant will dramatically change the young couple’s life.

name: I, Daniel Blake
overview: A middle aged carpenter, who requires state welfare after injuring himself, is joined by a single mother in a similar scenario.

writers: DK Welchman, Hugh Welchman, Jacek Dehnel
name: Loving Vincent
overview: The film brings the paintings of Vincent van Gogh to life to tell his remarkable story. Every one of the 65,000 frames of the film is an oil-painting hand-painted by 125 professional oil-painters who travelled from all across the world to the Loving Vincent studios in Poland and Greece to be a part of the production. As remarkable as Vincent’s brilliant paintings are his passionate and ill-fated life and mysterious death.

name: Days of Heaven
overview: In 1910, a Chicago steel worker accidentally kills his supervisor and flees to the Texas panhandle with his girlfriend and little sister to work harvesting wheat in the fields of a stoic farmer. A love triangle, a swarm of locusts, a hellish fire—Malick captures it all with dreamlike authenticity, creating at once a timeless American idyll and a gritty evocation of turn-of-the-century labor.

writers: Charles Lederer, Ben Hecht, Charles MacArthur, Morrie Ryskind
name: His Girl Friday
overview: Hildy, the journalist former wife of newspaper editor Walter Burns, visits his office to inform him that she's engaged and will be getting remarried the next day. Walter can't let that happen and frames the fiancé, Bruce Baldwin, for one thing after another, to keep him temporarily held in prison, while trying to steer Hildy into returning to her old job as his employee.
tagline: They're at each other's throats when they're not in each other's arms!

name: Aguirre, the Wrath of God
overview: A few decades after the destruction of the Inca empire, a Spanish expedition leaves the mountains of Peru and goes down the Amazon river in search of gold and wealth. Soon, they come across great difficulties and Don Aguirre, a ruthless man who cares only about riches, becomes their leader. But will his quest lead them to "the golden city", or to certain destruction?

name: Grizzly Man
overview: Follows the story of "Grizzly Man" Timothy Treadwell and what the thirteen summers in a National Park in Alaska were like in his attempt to protect the grizzly bears. The film is full of unique images and a look into the spirit of a man who sacrificed himself for nature.
tagline: In nature, there are boundaries. One man spent the last thirteen years of his life crossing them.

name: The Lunchbox
overview: A mistaken delivery in Mumbai's famously efficient lunchbox delivery system (Mumbai's Dabbawallahs) connects a young housewife to a stranger in the dusk of his life. They build a fantasy world together through notes in the lunchbox. Gradually, this fantasy threatens to overwhelm their reality.

writers: Bert Kalmar, Harry Ruby, Arthur Sheekman, Nat Perrin
name: Duck Soup
overview: Rufus T. Firefly is named president/dictator of bankrupt Freedonia and declares war on neighboring Sylvania over the love of wealthy Mrs. Teasdale.
tagline: War is swell...when the Marx Brothers are in it. They'll be out of the trenches by Christmas...if the food doesn't improve!

name: Pride
overview: Set in the summer of 1984 – Margaret Thatcher is in power and the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) is on strike. At the Gay Pride March in London, a group of gay and lesbian activists decides to raise money to support the families of the striking miners. But there is a problem. The Union seems embarrassed to receive their support.
tagline: Based on the inspirational true story.

writers: Joe Masteroff, John Van Druten, Christopher Isherwood, Jay Presson Allen
name: Cabaret
overview: Inside the Kit Kat Club of 1931 Berlin, starry-eyed singer Sally Bowles and an impish emcee sound the clarion call to decadent fun, while outside a certain political party grows into a brutal force.

name: Crimes and Misdemeanors
overview: An ophthalmologist's mistress threatens to reveal their affair to his wife, while a married documentary filmmaker is infatuated by another woman.

name: The Killing Fields
overview: The Killing Fields tells the real-life story of a friendship between two journalists, an American and a Cambodian, during the bloody Khmer Rouge takeover of Cambodia in 1975, which led to the death of 2-3 million Cambodians during the next four years, until Pol Pot's regime was toppled by the intervening Vietnamese in 1979.

name: Veer-Zaara
overview: Squadron Leader Veer Pratap Singh, a pilot in the Indian air force, rescues the stranded Zaara, a woman from Pakistan, following a bus accident, and their lives are forever bound.

directors: Ken Annakin, Andrew Marton, Gerd Oswald, Bernhard Wicki, Darryl F. Zanuck
writers: Cornelius Ryan, Romain Gary, James Jones, David Pursall, Jack Seddon
name: The Longest Day
overview: The retelling of June 6, 1944, from the perspectives of the Germans, US, British, Canadians, and the Free French. Marshall Erwin Rommel, touring the defenses being established as part of the Reich's Atlantic Wall, notes to his officers that when the Allied invasion comes they must be stopped on the beach. "For the Allies as well as the Germans, it will be the longest day"
tagline: THE INTERNATIONAL ACCLAIMED HIT JUST AS IT WAS SHOWN IN THE MAJOR CAPITALS OF THE WORLD!

directors: Kevin Altieri, Boyd Kirkland, Frank Paur, Dan Riba, Eric Radomski, Bruce Timm
writers: Alan Burnett, Paul Dini, Martin Pasko, Michael Reaves, Bob Kane
name: Batman: Mask of the Phantasm
overview: Andrea Beaumont strolls back into town, rekindling an old romance with Bruce Wayne. At the same time, Batman is mistaken for a masked vigilante assassin who has begun systematically eliminating Gotham's crime bosses. Now on the run, Batman must solve the mystery, while navigating his relationship with Andrea.

name: Man on Wire
overview: On August 7th 1974, French tightrope walker Philippe Petit stepped out on a high wire, illegally rigged between New York's World Trade Center twin towers, then the world's tallest buildings. After nearly an hour of performing on the wire, 1,350 feet above the sidewalks of Manhattan, he was arrested. This fun and spellbinding documentary chronicles Philippe Petit's "highest" achievement.

writers: Ethel Lina White, Sidney Gilliat, Frank Launder
name: The Lady Vanishes
overview: On a train headed for England a group of travelers is delayed by an avalanche. Holed up in a hotel in a fictional European country, young Iris befriends elderly Miss Froy. When the train resumes, Iris suffers a bout of unconsciousness and wakes to find the old woman has disappeared. The other passengers ominously deny Miss Froy ever existed, so Iris begins to investigate with another traveler and, as the pair sleuth, romantic sparks fly.
tagline: Comedy! Chills! Chuckles! in a Mystery Express!

writers: Judith Guest, Alvin Sargent, Nancy Dowd
name: Ordinary People
overview: Beth, Calvin, and their son Conrad are living in the aftermath of the death of the other son. Conrad is overcome by grief and misplaced guilt to the extent of a suicide attempt. He is in therapy. Beth had always preferred his brother and is having difficulty being supportive to Conrad. Calvin is trapped between the two trying to hold the family together.

name: Head-On
overview: Head On is German director Fatih Akin’s story of the alcoholic Cahit and Turkish Sibel. Akin tells the story of a love that can never be between two people who are too alike to not be together.

name: The Triplets of Belleville
overview: When her grandson is kidnapped during the Tour de France, Madame Souza and her beloved pooch Bruno team up with the Belleville Sisters--an aged song-and-dance team from the days of Fred Astaire--to rescue him.
tagline: Get your hands together for The Triplets of Belleville!

writers: Daniel Mainwaring, Jack Finney, Richard Collins
name: Invasion of the Body Snatchers
overview: A small-town doctor learns that the population of his community is being replaced by emotionless alien duplicates.
tagline: There was nothing to hold onto - except each other.

name: Adam's Apples
overview: A neo-nazi sentenced to community service at a church clashes with the blindly devotional priest.

name: Amy
overview: AMY is short film directed by Rithin Joseph with editing & VFX by Jobin Joseph of Petrova Films.

writers: Ernest Haycox, Dudley Nichols, Ben Hecht
name: Stagecoach
overview: A group of people traveling on a stagecoach find their journey complicated by the threat of Geronimo, and learn something about each other in the process.
tagline: A powerful story of nine strange people.

writers: Mary Shelley, William Hurlbut, John L. Balderston, Josef Berne, Lawrence G. Blochman, Robert Florey, Philip MacDonald, Tom Reed, R.C. Sherriff, Edmund Pearson, Morton Covan
name: The Bride of Frankenstein
overview: Bride of Frankenstein begins where James Whale's Frankenstein from 1931 ended. Dr. Frankenstein has not been killed as previously portrayed and now he wants to get away from the mad experiments. Yet when his wife is kidnapped by his creation, Frankenstein agrees to help him create a new monster, this time a woman.
tagline: More fearful than the monster himself!

directors: Shin'ichirô Watanabe, Tensai Okamura, Hiroyuki Okiura, Yoshiyuki Takei
name: Cowboy Bebop: the Movie
overview: The year is 2071. Following a terrorist bombing, a deadly virus is released on the populace of Mars and the government has issued the largest bounty in history, for the capture of whoever is behind it. The bounty hunter crew of the spaceship Bebop; Spike, Faye, Jet and Ed, take the case with hopes of cashing in the bounty. However, the mystery surrounding the man responsible, Vincent, goes deeper than they ever imagined, and they aren't the only ones hunting him.
tagline: They're here to save the planet. But not for free.

name: Lilya 4-Ever
overview: Lilya lives in poverty and dreams of a better life. Her mother moves to the United States and abandons her to her aunt, who neglects her. Lilya hangs out with her friends, Natasha and Volodya, who is suicidal. Desperate for money, she starts working as a prostitute, and later meets Andrei. He offers her a good job in Sweden, but when Lilya arrives her life quickly enters a downward spiral.

writers: Clarence Aaron 'Tod' Robbins, Willis Goldbeck, Leon Gordon, Al Boasberg, Charles MacArthur, Edgar Allan Woolf
name: Freaks
overview: A circus' beautiful trapeze artist agrees to marry the leader of side-show performers, but his deformed friends discover she is only marrying him for his inheritance.
tagline: Can a full grown woman truly love a midget?

primaryTitle: Once Upon a Time in Anatolia
writers: Ebru Ceylan, Nuri Bilge Ceylan, Ercan Kesal
Title_IMDb_Link: Once Upon a Time in Anatolia
name: Once Upon a Time in Anatolia
cleanNameArticles: once upon a time in anatolia
overview: In the rural area around the Anatolian town of Keskin, the local prosecutor, police commissar, and doctor lead a search for a victim of a murder to whom a suspect named Kenan and his mentally challenged brother confessed. However, the search is proving more difficult than expected as Kenan is fuzzy as to the body's exact location. As the group continues looking, its members can't help but chat among themselves about both trivia and their deepest concerns in an investigation that is proving more trying than any of them expected.

name: Tokyo Godfathers
overview: During a Christmas Eve in Tokyo, three homeless people, middle-aged alcoholic Gin, former drag queen Hana, and dependent runaway girl Miyuki, discover an abandoned newborn while looking through the garbage. With only a handful of clues to the baby's identity, the three misfits search the city to find its parents.

name: Guess Who's Coming to Dinner
overview: Matt and Christina Drayton are a couple whose attitudes are challenged when their daughter brings home a fiancé who is black.

name: East of Eden
overview: In the Salinas Valley, in and around World War I, Cal Trask feels he must compete against overwhelming odds with his brother for the love of their father. Cal is frustrated at every turn, from his reaction to the war, to how to get ahead in business and in life, to how to relate to estranged mother.
tagline: Sometimes you can't tell who's good and who's bad! ...

name: Amarcord
overview: In an Italian seaside town, young Titta gets into trouble with his friends and watches various local eccentrics as they engage in often absurd behavior. Frequently clashing with his stern father and defended by his doting mother, Titta witnesses the actions of a wide range of characters, from his extended family to Fascist loyalists to sensual women, with certain moments shifting into fantastical scenarios.

name: Land of Mine
overview: In the days following the surrender of Germany in May 1945, a group of young German prisoners of war is handed over to the Danish authorities and subsequently sent to the West Coast, where they are ordered to remove the more than two million mines that the Germans had placed in the sand along the coast. With their bare hands, crawling around in the sand, the boys are forced to perform the dangerous work under the leadership of a Danish sergeant.

name: Close
overview: Two 13-year-old boys spend an idyllic summer together, but their connection is put to the test when they become the subject of speculation at school.

name: Ninja Scroll
overview: Jubei is a masterless ninja who travels the land alone, lending his services to those with gold—or a worthy cause. His fearsome abilities have served him well, but a plot to overthrow the government threatens to end his wandering ways—and possibly his life.

writers: Charles R. Jackson, Charles Brackett, Billy Wilder
name: The Lost Weekend
overview: Don Birnam, a long-time alcoholic, has been sober for ten days and appears to be over the worst... but his craving has just become more insidious. Evading a country weekend planned by his brother and girlfriend, he begins a four-day bender that just might be his last - one way or another.

name: Fitzcarraldo
overview: Fitzcarraldo is a dreamer who plans to build an opera house in Iquitos, in the Peruvian Amazon, so, in order to finance his project, he embarks on an epic adventure to collect rubber, a very profitable product, in a remote and unexplored region of the rainforest.

writers: Antonio Skármeta, Furio Scarpelli, Giacomo Scarpelli, Anna Pavignano, Michael Radford, Massimo Troisi
name: The Postman
overview: Simple Italian postman learns to love poetry while delivering mail to a famous poet; he uses this to woo local beauty Beatrice.

name: Kagemusha
overview: Akira Kurosawa's lauded feudal epic presents the tale of a petty thief who is recruited to impersonate Shingen, an aging warlord, in order to avoid attacks by competing clans. When Shingen dies, his generals reluctantly agree to have the impostor take over as the powerful ruler. He soon begins to appreciate life as Shingen, but his commitment to the role is tested when he must lead his troops into battle against the forces of a rival warlord.
tagline: The Shadow of a man can never stand up and walk on its own.

name: Touching the Void
overview: The true story of Joe Simpson about Simon Yates' disastrous and near-fatal attempt to climb 6,344m Siula Grande in the Cordillera Huayhuash in the Peruvian Andes in 1985.

name: The Normal Heart
overview: The story of the onset of the HIV-AIDS crisis in New York City in the early 1980s, taking an unflinching look at the nation's sexual politics as gay activists and their allies in the medical community fight to expose the truth about the burgeoning epidemic to a city and nation in denial.

name: Cries and Whispers
overview: As Agnes slowly dies of cancer, her sisters are so deeply immersed in their own psychic pains that they can't offer her the support she needs. Maria is wracked with guilt at her husband's suicide, caused by his discovery of her extramarital affair. The self-loathing, suicidal Karin seems to regard her sister with revulsion. Only Anna, the deeply religious maid who lost her young child, seems able to offer Agnes solace and empathy.

name: All That Jazz
overview: Joe Gideon is at the top of the heap, one of the most successful directors and choreographers in musical theater. But he can feel his world slowly collapsing around him - his obsession with work has almost destroyed his personal life, and only his bottles of pills keep him going.
tagline: All that work. All that glitter. All that pain. All that love. All that crazy rhythm.

name: Once Were Warriors
overview: A drama about a Maori family living in Auckland, New Zealand. Lee Tamahori tells the story of Beth Heke’s strong will to keep her family together during times of unemployment and abuse from her violent and alcoholic husband.

name: Hiroshima Mon Amour
overview: The deep conversation between a Japanese architect and a French actress forms the basis of this celebrated French film, considered one of the vanguard productions of the French New Wave. Set in Hiroshima after the end of World War II, the couple -- lovers turned friends -- recount, over many hours, previous romances and life experiences. The two intertwine their stories about the past with pondering the devastation wrought by the atomic bomb dropped on the city.

writers: Andrew Solt, Edmund H. North, Dorothy B. Hughes
name: In a Lonely Place
overview: An aspiring actress begins to suspect that her temperamental boyfriend is a murderer.

name: The Conformist
overview: A weak-willed Italian man becomes a fascist flunky who goes abroad to arrange the assassination of his old teacher, now a political dissident.

name: 怪物
overview: When her young son Minato starts to behave strangely, his mother feels that there is something wrong. Discovering that a teacher is responsible, she storms into the school demanding to know what's going on. But as the story unfolds through the eyes of mother, teacher, and child, the truth gradually emerges.

name: Vivre Sa Vie
overview: Twelve episodic tales in the life of a Parisian woman and her slow descent into prostitution.

writers: Ross Thomas, Jimmy Santiago Baca, Jeremy Iacone, Floyd Mutrux
name: Bound by Honor
overview: Based on the true life experiences of poet Jimmy Santiago Baca, the film focuses on half-brothers Paco and Cruz, and their bi-racial cousin Miklo. It opens in 1972, as the three are members of an East L.A. gang known as the "Vatos Locos", and the story focuses on how a violent crime and the influence of narcotics alter their lives. Miklo is incarcerated and sent to San Quentin, where he makes a "home" for himself. Cruz becomes an exceptional artist, but a heroin addiction overcomes him with tragic results. Paco becomes a cop and an enemy to his "carnal", Miklo.

writers: John Van Druten, Walter Reisch, John L. Balderston, Patrick Hamilton
name: Gaslight
overview: A newlywed fears she's going mad when strange things start happening at the family mansion.
tagline: Strange drama of a captive sweetheart!

name: A Taxi Driver
overview: May, 1980. Man-seob is a taxi driver in Seoul who lives from hand to mouth, raising his young daughter alone. One day, he hears that there is a foreigner who will pay big money for a drive down to Gwangju city. Not knowing that he’s a German journalist with a hidden agenda, Man-seob takes the job.

name: The Lion in Winter
overview: 1183 AD: King Henry II's three sons all want to inherit the throne, but he won't commit to a choice. They and his wife variously plot to force him.  An aging and conniving King Henry II of England and Ireland plans a reunion where he hopes to name his successor. He summons the following people for the holiday at his chateau and primary residence in Chinon, Anjou, within the Angevin Empire of medieval France: his scheming but imprisoned wife, Queen Eleanor of Aquitaine; his mistress, Princess Alais, whom he wishes to marry; his three sons, gay Richard the Lionheart , Geoffrey, and John, all of whom desire the throne; and the young, but crafty King Philip II of France, who is also Alais' half-brother.

writers: George S. Kaufman, Morrie Ryskind, James Kevin McGuinness, Buster Keaton, Al Boasberg, Bert Kalmar, George Oppenheimer, Robert Pirosh, Harry Ruby, George Seaton, Carey Wilson
name: A Night at the Opera
overview: The Marx Brothers take on high society and the opera world to bring two lovers together. A sly business manager and two wacky friends of two opera singers help them achieve success while humiliating their stuffy and snobbish enemies.
tagline: Don't miss it! The funniest picture ever made!

name: Knockin' on Heaven's Door
overview: Two young men, Martin and Rudi, both suffering from terminal cancer, get to know each other in a hospital room. They drown their desperation in tequila and decide to take one last trip to the sea. Drunk and still in pajamas they steal the first fancy car they find, a 60's Mercedes convertible. The car happens to belong to a bunch of gangsters, which immediately start to chase it, since it contains more than the pistol Martin finds in the glove box.

name: Millennium Actress
overview: Documentary filmmaker Genya Tachibana has tracked down the legendary actress Chiyoko Fujiwara, who mysteriously vanished at the height of her career. When he presents her with a key she had lost and thought was gone forever, the filmmaker could not have imagined that it would not only unlock the long-held secrets of Chiyoko’s life... but also his own.
tagline: The magic of movies, the mystery of memory.

name: C.R.A.Z.Y.
overview: A story of two love affairs. A father's love for his five sons. And one son's love for his father, a love so strong it compels him to live a lie. That son is Zac Beaulieu, born on the 25th of December 1960, different from all his brothers, but desperate to fit in. During the next 20 years, life takes Zac on a surprising and unexpected journey that ultimately leads him to accept his true nature and, even more importantly, leads his father to love him for who he really is.

writers: Albert Hackett, Frances Goodrich, Dashiell Hammett
name: The Thin Man
overview: A husband-and-wife detective team takes on the search for a missing inventor and almost get killed for their efforts.
tagline: A laugh tops every thrilling moment!

name: The Sacrifice
overview: Alexander, a journalist, philosopher and retired actor, celebrates a birthday with friends and family when it is announced that nuclear war has begun.
tagline: The final film of Andrei Tarkovsky

name: The Rules of the Game
overview: A weekend at a marquis’ country château lays bare some ugly truths about a group of haut bourgeois acquaintances.

name: Weapons
overview: When all but one child from the same class mysteriously vanish on the same night at exactly the same time, a community is left questioning who or what is behind their disappearance.
tagline: Last night at 2:17 AM, every child from Mrs. Gandy's class woke up, got out of bed, went downstairs, opened the front door, walked into the dark ...and they never came back.
review: Superb storytelling makes this movie worth watching twice (which I did). The acting is also top-notch (Josh Brolin, Julia Garner, Benedict Wong).  I counted nine jump-scares but only one vomit scene although it is quite substantial. There are no clowns but definitely people painted like clowns.  There’s not one but two needle prick scenes!
emailReview: This thriller hooks you with superb storytelling and standout performances from Josh Brolin, Julia Garner, and Benedict Wong, all wrapped in a tense atmosphere that rewards repeat viewing. Be prepared for: multiple jump-scares, two needle prick scenes, and a memorable vomit moment.

name: Nostalgia
overview: The Russian poet Andrei Gorchakov, accompanied by guide and translator Eugenia, is traveling through Italy researching the life of an 18th-century Russian composer. In an ancient spa town, he meets the lunatic Domenico, who years earlier had imprisoned his own family in his house for seven years to save them from the evils of the world. Seeing some deep truth in Domenico's act, Andrei becomes drawn to him. In a series of dreams, the poet's nostalgia for his homeland and his longing for his wife, his ambivalent feelings for Eugenia and Italy, and his sense of kinship with Domenico become intertwined.

name: In Cold Blood
overview: After a botched robbery results in the brutal murder of a rural family, two drifters elude police, in the end coming to terms with their own mortality and the repercussions of their vile atrocity.

name: Le Cercle Rouge
overview: When French criminal Corey gets released from prison, he resolves to never return. He is quickly pulled back into the underworld, however, after a chance encounter with escaped murderer Vogel. Along with former policeman and current alcoholic Jansen, they plot an intricate jewel heist. All the while, quirky Police Commissioner Mattei, who was the one to lose custody of Vogel, is determined to find him.

writers: Roger Nimier, Louis Malle, Noël Calef
name: Elevator to the Gallows
overview: A self-assured businessman murders his employer, the husband of his mistress, which unintentionally provokes an ill-fated chain of events.
tagline: Frantic for life and love, frantic for excitement.

writers: Ranald MacDougall, James M. Cain, William Faulkner, Margaret Gruen, Albert Maltz, Louise Randall Pierson, Catherine Turney, Margaret Buell Wilder, Thames Williamson
name: Mildred Pierce
overview: After her unfaithful husband leaves her, Mildred Pierce proves she can become independent and successful. However winning the approval of her spoiled daughter proves a greater challenge.
tagline: Please don't tell anyone what Mildred Pierce did!

name: Sullivan's Travels
overview: Successful movie director John L. Sullivan, convinced he won't be able to film his ambitious masterpiece until he has suffered, dons a hobo disguise and sets off on a journey, aiming to "know trouble" first-hand. When all he finds is a train ride back to Hollywood and a beautiful blonde companion, he redoubles his efforts, managing to land himself in more trouble than he bargained for when he loses his memory and ends up a prisoner on a chain gang.

writers: Ebru Ceylan, Nuri Bilge Ceylan, Akin Aksu
name: The Wild Pear Tree
overview: Sinan is passionate about literature and has always wanted to be a writer. Returning to the village where he was born, he pours his heart and soul into scraping together the money he needs to be published, but his father’s debts catch up with him.

writers: Jean Cocteau, Jeanne-Marie Leprince de Beaumont
name: La belle et la bête
overview: The story of a gentle-hearted beast in love with a simple and beautiful girl. She is drawn to the repellent but strangely fascinating Beast, who tests her fidelity by giving her a key, telling her that if she doesn't return it to him by a specific time, he will die of grief. She is unable to return the key on time, but it is revealed that the Beast is the genuinely handsome one. A simple tale of tragic love that turns into a surreal vision of death, desire, and beauty.

name: Jodorowsky's Dune
overview: Shot in France, England, Switzerland and the United States, this documentary covers director Alejandro Jodorowsky (El Topo, Holy Mountain, Santa Sangre) and his 1974 Quixotic attempt to adapt the seminal sci-fi novel Dune into a feature film. After spending 2 years and millions of dollars, the massive undertaking eventually fell apart, but the artists Jodorowsky assembled for the legendary project continued to work together. This group of artists, or his “warriors” as Jodorowsky named them, went on to define modern sci-fi cinema with such films as Alien, Blade Runner, Star Wars and Total Recall.
tagline: What is to give light must endure burning

name: The Way He Looks
overview: Leonardo is a blind teenager dealing with an overprotective mother while trying to live a more independent life. To the disappointment of his best friend, Giovana, he plans to go on an exchange program abroad. When Gabriel, a new student in town, arrives at their classroom, new feelings blossom in Leonardo making him question his plans.

name: Through a Glass Darkly
overview: Karin hopes to recover from her recent stay at a mental hospital by spending the summer at her family's cottage on a tiny island. Her husband, Martin, cares for her but is frustrated by her physical withdrawal. Her younger brother, Minus, is confused by Karin's vulnerability and his own budding sexuality. Their father, David, cannot overcome his haughty remoteness. Beset by visions, Karin descends further into madness.

writers: Morrie Ryskind, Eric Hatch, Zoe Akins, Gregory La Cava, Robert Presnell Sr.
name: My Man Godfrey
overview: Fifth Avenue socialite Irene Bullock needs a "forgotten man" to win a scavenger hunt, and no one is more forgotten than Godfrey Park, who resides in a dump by the East River. Irene hires Godfrey as a servant for her riotously unhinged family, to the chagrin of her spoiled sister, Cornelia, who tries her best to get Godfrey fired. As Irene falls for her new butler, Godfrey turns the tables and teaches the frivolous Bullocks a lesson or two.

writers: Julio Alejandro, Luis Buñuel, Benito Pérez Galdós
name: Viridiana
overview: Viridiana is preparing to start her life as a nun when she is sent, somewhat unwillingly, to visit her aging uncle, Don Jaime. He supports her; but the two have met only once. Jaime thinks Viridiana resembles his dead wife. Viridiana has secretly despised this man all her life and finds her worst fears proven when Jaime grows determined to seduce his pure niece. Viridiana becomes undone as her uncle upends the plans she had made to join the convent.

name: Evangelion: 2.0 You Can (Not) Advance
overview: Under constant attack by monstrous creatures called Angels that seek to eradicate humankind, U.N. Special Agency NERV introduces two new EVA pilots to help defend the city of Tokyo-3: the mysterious Makinami Mari Illustrous and the intense Asuka Langley Shikinami. Meanwhile, Gendo Ikari and SEELE proceed with a secret project that involves both Rei and Shinji.

name: The Thin Blue Line
overview: This unique documentary dramatically re-enacts the crime scene and investigation of a police officer's murder in Dallas.
tagline: Erases the border between art and activism.

primaryTitle: A Matter of Life and Death
Title_IMDb_Link: A Matter of Life and Death
name: Matter of Life and Death
overview: When a young airman miraculously survives bailing out of his aeroplane without a parachute, he falls in love with an American radio operator. But the officials in the other world realise their mistake, and despatch an angel to collect him.

writers: Walter Bernstein, Eugene Burdick, Harvey Wheeler, Peter George
name: Fail-Safe
overview: Because of a technical defect an American bomber team mistakenly orders the destruction of Moscow. The President of the United States has but little time to prevent an atomic catastrophe from occurring.
tagline: It will have you sitting on the brink of eternity!
review:
Fail-Safe is a taut Cold War thriller that holds up as a masterclass in tension and moral dread, thanks largely to Sidney Lumet’s steady direction and a cast led by Henry Fonda’s measured, weary President. It feels like Dr. Strangelove’s much grimmer cousin—no satire here, just the relentless build-up to potential nuclear disaster. If you’re into political dramas that explore the terrifying fragility of command and control, this one’s a gripping, sobering watch.

What stands out most is how the film squeezes suspense out of dialogue-heavy scenes and limited sets, relying on sharp writing from Walter Bernstein and the weight of the actors’ performances rather than flashy visuals. The premise—a mistaken order for atomic destruction—feels chillingly plausible, and the tagline, “It will have you sitting on the brink of eternity!” isn’t an exaggeration. The film’s slow burn is punctuated by moments of quiet desperation as leaders scramble to avert apocalypse, making the stakes feel uncomfortably real.

Heads-up for anyone sensitive to animal harm: the opening dream sequence includes real bullfighting footage that’s quite graphic and prolonged, showing the bull’s slow, painful death. It’s an intense start that sets a grim tone but might be rough for some viewers.
emailReview:
Fail-Safe is a masterclass in Cold War tension, with Henry Fonda’s weary President anchoring a grim, slow-burning thriller that feels like Dr. Strangelove’s serious sibling.

Be prepared for: graphic bullfighting footage with a slow, painful bull death, intense political despair, and the looming threat of nuclear apocalypse.

writers: Lamar Trotti, Walter Van Tilburg Clark
name: The Ox-Bow Incident
overview: Gil Carter and Art Croft ride into a small Nevada town plagued by cattle thieves. Initially suspected of being the rustlers themselves, Carter and Croft eventually join a posse out to get the criminals, who also may be involved in a recent shooting. When the posse closes in on a group that could be the fugitives, they must decide on a course of action, with numerous lives hanging in the balance.

name: The Fog of War
overview: Using archival footage, United States Cabinet conversation recordings, and an interview of the 85-year-old Robert McNamara, THE FOG OF WAR depicts his life, from working as a WWII whiz kid military officer, to being the Ford Motor Company's president, to managing the American Vietnam War, as defense secretary for presidents Kennedy and Johnson.

writers: François Truffaut, Jean-Louis Richard, Suzanne Schiffman
name: Day for Night
overview: A committed film director struggles to complete his movie while coping with a myriad of crises, personal and professional, among the cast and crew.

writers: Michelangelo Antonioni, Ennio Flaiano, Tonino Guerra
name: La Notte
overview: Set during a single day and night in a Milan where steel and glass skyscrapers are going up and old buildings being pulled down, it opens with a disillusioned novelist and his embittered wife visiting their dying friend, a leftwing critic.

name: Threads
overview: Documentary style account of a nuclear holocaust and its effect on the working class city of Sheffield, England; and the eventual long run effects of nuclear war on civilization.
tagline: The closest you'll ever want to come to nuclear war.

writers: Marcel Pagnol, Claude Berri, Gérard Brach
name: Manon of the Spring
overview: In this, the sequel to Jean de Florette, Manon (Beart) has grown into a beautiful young shepherdess living in the idyllic Provencal countryside. She plots vengeance on the men whose greedy conspiracy to acquire her father's land caused his death years earlier.

name: Tampopo
overview: A pair of truck drivers happen onto a decrepit roadside fast food stop selling ramen noodles. The widowed owner, Tampopo, begs them to help her turn her establishment into a paragon of the "art of noodle soup making".

writers: Jon Spaihts, Scott Derrickson, C. Robert Cargill, Stan Lee, Steve Ditko
name: Doctor Strange
overview: After his career is destroyed, a brilliant but arrogant surgeon gets a new lease on life when a sorcerer takes him under her wing and trains him to defend the world against evil.
review:
Doctor Strange is your classic Marvel origin story with a mystic twist—think Iron Man meets Inception, but with more kaleidoscopic magic and less tech. Benedict Cumberbatch brings his usual brooding charm to the role of the arrogant surgeon-turned-sorcerer, and the film manages to balance blockbuster spectacle with a surprisingly grounded redemption arc. It’s not the most emotionally deep Marvel outing, but it’s elevated by Scott Derrickson’s confident direction and some genuinely inventive visuals that make the “impossibilities” feel endless.

What really stands out is the film’s embrace of mind-bending magic and alternate dimensions, which is a refreshing departure from the typical superhero punch-fest. The Ancient One, played by Tilda Swinton, adds an enigmatic presence that helps anchor the fantasy elements, while Mads Mikkelsen’s Kaecilius provides a compelling villain with a cause you can at least sympathize with. The tagline, “The impossibilities are endless,” is no joke—there’s a lot of trippy, visually inventive stuff here, including some memorable sequences where reality folds in on itself. Rachel McAdams’s Dr. Christine Palmer offers a much-needed emotional connection amid the chaos, though her role is a bit undercooked.

Heads up for animal lovers: this one’s notable for a distressing number of pet and animal deaths, including dogs, cats, horses, and even a dragon, plus some scenes of animal abuse and abandonment. If you have strong feelings about animal welfare triggers, this is a major flag. Also, those who pin bugs, spiders, and snakes should be cautious—there’s a fair helping of creepy crawlies scattered throughout.
emailReview:
Doctor Strange dazzles with kaleidoscopic magic and mind-bending visuals that turn typical superhero fare into a trippy journey through alternate dimensions, all anchored by Benedict Cumberbatch’s brooding charm.

Be prepared for: multiple pet and animal deaths including dogs, cats, horses, and a dragon, scenes of animal abuse and abandonment, plus plenty of creepy bugs, spiders, and snakes.

name: John Wick
overview: Ex-hitman John Wick comes out of retirement to track down the gangsters that took everything from him.
review:
John Wick is a slick, relentless action thriller that revitalized the assassin genre with style and grit. Keanu Reeves nails the role of the titular ex-hitman with a stoic intensity that anchors the film’s hyper-violent world. It’s like Die Hard meets a ballet of bullets, with choreography that’s as precise as it is brutal. While it follows the classic revenge revenge plot, the movie’s mood and execution elevate it beyond standard fare—fans of tightly wound, stylish action will appreciate its lean, mean storytelling.

What stands out here is the film’s visual flair and world-building. The tagline "Don't set him off" perfectly captures the simmering tension that explodes into jaw-dropping action sequences. The story centers on John Wick’s return from retirement after gangsters destroy everything dear to him, including a deeply symbolic puppy gifted by his late wife. The blend of gritty realism and almost mythic underworld rules gives the movie a unique tone, with a memorable mix of neon-lit cityscapes and close-quarters combat. The supporting cast, including Willem Dafoe and Michael Nyqvist, add weight without stealing the spotlight from Reeves’ quiet, lethal presence.

Triggers to note: this movie is heavy on gun violence and blood/gore throughout, with some intense fight scenes featuring eye and finger mutilation and bone-breaking. The death of John’s puppy is a particularly tough moment, and there’s also a fair share of car crashes and physical torture. Those sensitive to graphic violence or animal death should tread carefully.
emailReview:
John Wick is a slick, relentless action thriller with Keanu Reeves delivering a stoic, lethal performance that turns gunfights into a brutal ballet of bullets and bone-crunching combat.

Be prepared for: the heartbreaking death of a puppy, eye and finger mutilation, intense gun violence, and visceral car crashes.

writers: Stan Lee, Steve Ditko, Alfred Gough, Miles Millar, Michael Chabon, Alvin Sargent
name: Spider-Man 2
overview: Peter Parker is going through a major identity crisis. Burned out from being Spider-Man, he decides to shelve his superhero alter ego, which leaves the city suffering in the wake of carnage left by the evil Doc Ock. In the meantime, Parker still can't act on his feelings for Mary Jane Watson, a girl he's loved since childhood. A certain anger begins to brew in his best friend Harry Osborn as well...
tagline: There's a hero in all of us.
review:
Spider-Man 2 stands out as one of the best superhero sequels, balancing action, heart, and a surprisingly deep identity crisis for Peter Parker. Directed by Sam Raimi and featuring Tobey Maguire in his prime, this film feels like a perfect mix of comic book thrills and genuine emotional stakes. It’s definitely more thoughtful than your average blockbuster, with Peter’s burnout and inner turmoil giving it a grounded feel that fans of character-driven superhero tales will appreciate. Think of it as Spider-Man meets a coming-of-age drama, with a dash of that classic Raimi quirkiness.

What really makes Spider-Man 2 shine is how it juggles everything from spectacular set pieces to the quieter moments — like Peter’s complicated love for Mary Jane (Kirsten Dunst) and the tragic transformation of Doc Ock (Alfred Molina). The tagline, “There’s a hero in all of us,” underscores the film’s core theme of responsibility and self-discovery, and it never feels preachy. The villain is both menacing and sympathetic, thanks to Molina’s layered performance and a smart script by Alvin Sargent. Plus, J.K. Simmons’ J. Jonah Jameson keeps the comic relief sharp and memorable.

Heads up for those sensitive to animal-related content: this film includes multiple scenes where animals die or are harmed, including dogs, cats, and a horse. If you’ve got a soft spot for furry friends or a low tolerance for that kind of distress, you’ll want to brace yourself here. Also, spider and bug triggers are present, which fits the theme but could be unsettling if those are on your list.
emailReview:
Spider-Man 2 masterfully blends blockbuster thrills with heartfelt character drama, anchored by Tobey Maguire’s earnest performance and Alfred Molina’s unforgettable Doc Ock.

Be prepared for: multiple scenes of animal harm involving dogs, cats, and a horse, as well as unsettling spider and bug imagery.

writers: Simon Beaufoy, Michael Arndt, Suzanne Collins
name: The Hunger Games: Catching Fire
overview: After surviving the Hunger Games, Katniss and Peeta struggle with the consequences of their victory as unrest spreads across Panem. Forced back into the spotlight, they become symbols of hope and resistance while the Capitol prepares a new and deadly challenge that will change the future of the nation forever.
review:
The Hunger Games: Catching Fire doubles down on the gritty dystopian drama that made the first film a hit, blending brutal survival action with a simmering political rebellion. It’s a lean, tense follow-up that feels like The Hunger Games meets a high-stakes Cold War thriller—less about flashy spectacle and more about the psychological toll of being thrust into a deadly game twice. Jennifer Lawrence remains magnetic as Katniss, grounding the chaos with a raw vulnerability that keeps this from feeling like just another young adult franchise sequel. It’s not quite as surprising as the original, but it’s elevated by its darker tone and the growing undercurrents of resistance.

What stands out here is the way the film leans into trauma and the cost of violence, rather than glossing over it. Katniss’s PTSD is front and center, shown through panic attacks and flashbacks that add depth to her character and the story’s bleakness. The new arena, a beach surrounded by jungle, is a clever twist on the survival game trope, offering visually striking yet claustrophobic dangers like poisonous fog and aggressive monkeys. The tagline, “Remember who the enemy is,” echoes throughout as the Capitol’s cruelty becomes more overt, culminating in some truly harrowing moments—especially the brutal and emotional sacrifice scenes that underscore just how high the stakes are. The film also brings in sharper political commentary, showing the growing unrest beyond the arena, which adds layers to the narrative.

Those sensitive to intense violence, especially involving torture and blood/gore, should be cautious here. The movie doesn’t shy away from showing people (including women) being brutalized for spectacle, and there are multiple scenes of gun violence, physical restraint, and death. Mental health triggers like PTSD, anxiety attacks, and panic are depicted in detail, alongside scenes of addiction and alcohol abuse. There’s also sexual assault and non-consensual touching that might be upsetting, plus some jump scares and trypophobic imagery. Finally, animal harm occurs both visually and thematically, from rabbits to monkeys. It’s a tough watch in many ways, but it’s part of what makes Catching Fire such a powerful, if difficult, installment in the series.
emailReview:
The Hunger Games: Catching Fire turns up the tension with a darker, more psychological edge, anchored by Jennifer Lawrence’s raw and vulnerable performance as Katniss facing trauma and rebellion.

Be prepared for: intense torture and blood/gore, detailed PTSD and panic attacks, sexual assault and non-consensual touching, animal harm involving rabbits and monkeys, and jump scares.

primaryTitle: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
Title_IMDb_Link: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
name: Harry Potter And the Chamber of Secrets
cleanNameArticles: harry potter and the chamber of secrets
overview: Cars fly, trees fight back, and a mysterious house-elf comes to warn Harry Potter at the start of his second year at Hogwarts. Adventure and danger await when bloody writing on a wall announces: The Chamber Of Secrets Has Been Opened. To save Hogwarts will require all of Harry, Ron and Hermione’s magical abilities and courage.
tagline: Something evil has returned to Hogwarts!

writers: Michael Robert Johnson, Anthony Peckham, Simon Kinberg, Lionel Wigram, Arthur Conan Doyle
name: Sherlock Holmes
overview: Eccentric consulting detective, Sherlock Holmes and Doctor John Watson battle to bring down a new nemesis and unravel a deadly plot that could destroy England.
review:
Guy Ritchie's 2009 *Sherlock Holmes* is a raucous, stylized take on the classic detective tale that feels like *Sherlock* meets *Snatch*. Robert Downey Jr. brings his signature manic energy to the role, turning Holmes into a brawling, quick-witted badass rather than the Victorian armchair philosopher. Jude Law’s Watson is the perfect grounded counterbalance, adding warmth and dry humor. While the plot leans heavily on a shadowy occult conspiracy and explosive action, it’s the chemistry between Holmes and Watson that elevates this beyond a typical mystery thriller.

What stands out here is the film’s kinetic style—Ritchie's direction turns every deduction and fight into a choreographed spectacle, complete with slow-motion breakdowns that show Holmes mentally planning his moves. The tagline, “Nothing escapes him,” rings true not just for Holmes’ intellect but for the movie’s attention to gritty, grimy detail. From underground fight clubs to occult rituals and a sinister villain with a penchant for chemical torture, the film blends mystery with pulp adventure. Rachel McAdams’ Irene Adler adds a layer of seductive intrigue, though her storyline sometimes feels undercooked compared to the main plot.

Trigger-wise, brace yourself for intense violence peppered throughout—the fighting is brutal, with choking, bone-breaking, and plenty of blood. There’s also significant animal harm, including scenes of dog and horse distress, and brief but unsettling glimpses of animal abuse and dead animals. The film’s darker themes include kidnapping, occult rituals, and sexual assault, some of which are played for laughs in a way that might feel off-putting. If you’re sensitive to graphic violence, animal suffering, or scenes involving fire and burning, this one will require some caution.
emailReview:
Guy Ritchie's 2009 Sherlock Holmes crackles with manic energy and sharp wit, turning the classic detective into a brawling genius whose every move unfolds in stylish slow-motion spectacle.

Be prepared for: brutal choking and bone-breaking fights, animal distress including dog and horse harm, occult rituals, and unsettling scenes of fire and chemical torture.

primaryTitle: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix
Title_IMDb_Link: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix
name: Harry Potter And the Order of the Phoenix
cleanNameArticles: harry potter and the order of the phoenix
overview: Returning for his fifth year of study at Hogwarts, Harry is stunned to find that his warnings about the return of Lord Voldemort have been ignored. Left with no choice, Harry takes matters into his own hands, training a small group of students – dubbed 'Dumbledore's Army' – to defend themselves against the dark arts.

name: Baby Driver
overview: After being coerced into working for a crime boss, a young getaway driver finds himself taking part in a heist doomed to fail.
tagline: All you need is one killer track.

name: Zombieland
overview: Columbus has made a habit of running from what scares him. Tallahassee doesn't have fears. If he did, he'd kick their ever-living ass. In a world overrun by zombies, these two are perfectly evolved survivors. But now, they're about to stare down the most terrifying prospect of all: each other.
review:
Zombieland is a wild, gory comedy that blends zombie apocalypse chaos with sharp, self-aware humor. If you like your horror laced with laughs and a little bit of buddy-cop energy, this one’s a solid pick. Jesse Eisenberg’s neurotic Columbus paired with Woody Harrelson’s fearless, taco-loving Tallahassee make a mismatched duo that drives the film’s zippy pace and punchy one-liners. It’s like Shaun of the Dead meets The Road Warrior — a mashup that doesn’t take itself too seriously but still delivers on zombie carnage and quirky character moments.

What really stands out here is the way Zombieland plays with survival rules (“Nut up or shut up”) as a running gag and thematic spine. The film’s tagline nails the tone: it’s brash, bold, and oddly heartfelt under the gore. The cast, including Emma Stone and Abigail Breslin, adds layers beyond the usual zombie fare, giving it a surprisingly warm core amid the undead mayhem. Plus, Bill Murray’s cameo is a memorable, meta highlight that sneaks in some absurd humor without breaking the flow. The writing by Paul Wernick and Rhett Reese keeps things tight, balancing action, comedy, and just enough creepy to keep you on edge.

Heads up for those sensitive to animal-related triggers: while no animals are actually harmed on screen, there are mentions and implications around dogs, cats, and horses that might be unsettling for some. If you’re watching with a soft spot for furry friends, be cautious around those moments. Otherwise, Zombieland delivers the kind of over-the-top zombie romp that’s hard not to enjoy if you like your horror with a side of snark.
emailReview:
Zombieland is a wild, gory comedy that pairs sharp, self-aware humor with zombie apocalypse chaos, powered by Jesse Eisenberg’s neurotic charm and Woody Harrelson’s fearless taco-loving bravado.

Be prepared for: implied animal deaths including dogs and horses, zombie gore, and chaotic survival violence.

writers: Bryan Woods, Scott Beck, John Krasinski
name: A Quiet Place
overview: A family is forced to live in silence while hiding from creatures that hunt by sound.
tagline: If they hear you, they hunt you.
review:
A Quiet Place is a tense, nerve-wracking thriller that turns silence into its scariest weapon. It’s a clever mashup of horror and family drama, where the stakes are life or death with every whisper or footstep. If you like your horror movies with a side of emotional depth and some genuinely suspenseful set-pieces, this one delivers. Think of it as a quieter, more intimate cousin to other creature features, but elevated by a strong central cast and a smart, minimalist approach to scares.

What really stands out here is how the film uses sound—or the lack of it—to create atmosphere. The tagline says it all: “If they hear you, they hunt you.” The family’s attempts to communicate and survive in silence adds tension that’s almost palpable. Emily Blunt’s performance as Evelyn Abbott anchors the film with a mix of fierce protectiveness and vulnerability, and John Krasinski’s direction makes the quiet moments as gripping as the loud ones. The idea of creatures that hunt by sound isn’t new, but the execution here feels fresh and immersive.

Those sensitive to animal harm or death should be cautious—there are multiple instances involving pets and other animals meeting grim fates. Also, be heavily warned if jump scares, the death of a child, or intense scenes involving spiders and other creepy crawlies are on your list. This one definitely keeps you on edge in more ways than one.
emailReview:
A Quiet Place turns silence into its deadliest weapon with a taut mix of suspense and emotional stakes, anchored by Emily Blunt’s fierce, vulnerable performance.

Be prepared for: multiple pet deaths, the death of a child, jump scares, and intense scenes featuring spiders and creepy crawlies.

name: The Conjuring
overview: Paranormal investigators Ed and Lorraine Warren work to help a family terrorized by a dark presence in their farmhouse. Forced to confront a powerful entity, the Warrens find themselves caught in the most terrifying case of their lives.
tagline: Based on the true case files of the Warrens.

name: Source Code
overview: Decorated soldier Captain Colter Stevens wakes up in the body of an unknown man, discovering he's involved in a mission to find the bomber of a Chicago commuter train. He learns he's part of a top-secret experimental program that enables him to experience the final 8 minutes of another person's life. Colter re-lives the train incident over and over again, gathering more clues each time.

name: Love Actually
overview: Follows seemingly unrelated people as their lives begin to intertwine while they fall in – and out – of love. Affections languish and develop as Christmas draws near.
review:
Love Actually is the quintessential holiday rom-com that’s both a comfort blanket and a bit of a guilty pleasure. Richard Curtis’s interwoven tales of love at Christmas have become iconic in the genre, blending warmth and awkwardness with a hefty dose of British charm. It’s got the ensemble cast energy of something like Valentine’s Day but with a more sentimental, sometimes bittersweet edge that fans of classic rom-coms will appreciate. While it’s not exactly subtle or groundbreaking, it’s elevated by its memorable performances—Hugh Grant’s cheeky Prime Minister and Emma Thompson’s quietly heartbreaking Karen stand out—and a sharp script that balances humor and heart.

What’s worth talking about here is how Love Actually juggles so many storylines without feeling totally scattershot. From unrequited crushes to marital strain, the film captures the messy, unpredictable nature of love “actually” being all around. The Christmas setting adds a festive glow without turning the whole thing into syrupy holiday cheese. The soundtrack, the witty dialogue, and those iconic moments—like the cue card confession—have cemented this as a modern classic, even if some of the humor hasn’t aged perfectly. It’s the kind of movie that’s cozy and familiar, but not afraid to peek behind the curtain of romantic idealism.

Heads up for animal lovers and anyone sensitive to pet-related content: the film includes several scenes where animals die or are mistreated, which might catch some viewers off guard in what's otherwise a light-hearted romp. Those who pin the “animal death” and “animal abuse” triggers should be cautious going in. There are also some bugs and spiders on the list, so if critters are a no-go, keep that in mind.
emailReview:
Love Actually wraps its many love stories in a cozy, charming holiday package, buoyed by standout performances from Hugh Grant and Emma Thompson that add heart and humor to the festive spirit.

Be prepared for: multiple scenes of animal death and abuse, bug and spider appearances, and some pet mistreatment that might surprise fans expecting pure holiday cheer.

primaryTitle: Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom
writers: Willard Huyck, Gloria Katz, George Lucas
Title_IMDb_Link: Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom
name: Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom
cleanNameArticles: indiana jones and the temple of doom
overview:
Second film in the Indiana Jones franchise.

After arriving in India, Indiana Jones is asked by a desperate village to find a mystical stone. He agrees – and stumbles upon a secret cult plotting a terrible plan in the catacombs of an ancient palace.
tagline: If adventure has a name... it must be Indiana Jones.
review:
Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom is the wild, darker sibling to Raiders of the Lost Ark—still packed with high-stakes adventure but with a decidedly more intense and sometimes unsettling tone. Steven Spielberg’s 1984 sequel leans into pulpy thrills and exotic locales, blending globe-trotting action with moments that veer into horror and mysticism. Fans of the franchise will appreciate Harrison Ford’s iconic turn as Indy, but brace yourself: it’s less lighthearted than the first film, more like Indiana Jones meets a supernatural thriller with a dash of Indiana Jones and the darker ‘80s blockbusters.

What stands out here is the film’s willingness to delve into genuinely creepy territory—the secret cult, the underground rituals, and the palpable sense of menace lurking beneath the adventure. The tagline, “If adventure has a name... it must be Indiana Jones,” feels both fitting and ironic, given how much of the film challenges the classic hero’s journey with moments that are genuinely unsettling. Kate Capshaw’s Willie Scott adds comic relief, though sometimes feels a little out of place amid the darker beats. The film’s mix of action, mysticism, and exoticism is classic Spielberg, but it also leans into genre conventions in ways that don’t always age well, especially culturally.

Heads up for animal lovers and anyone sensitive to animal harm—Temple of Doom is notorious for its disturbing scenes involving animals, including the death and abuse of multiple creatures. Spiders, snakes, and other critters crawl through the film’s shadowy corners, and there’s dog fighting and various instances of pets and other animals meeting grim fates. If you’re on the lookout for animal harm or death triggers, this one is definitely a heavy hitter.
emailReview:
Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom cranks up the tension with a darker, spookier vibe that blends globe-trotting action and supernatural chills, all anchored by Harrison Ford’s classic swagger.

Be prepared for: dog fighting, multiple animal deaths, spiders, snakes, and unsettling ritual violence.

writers: Michael J. Wilson, Michael Berg, Peter Ackerman, James Bresnahan, Doug Compton, Jeff Siergey, Michael Thurmeier, Galen T. Chu, Xeth Feinberg
name: Ice Age
overview: Manny the mammoth, Sid the loquacious sloth, and Diego the sabre-toothed tiger go on a comical quest to return a human baby back to his father, across a world on the brink of an ice age.

writers: James Cameron, Rick Jaffa, Amanda Silver, Josh Friedman, Shane Salerno
name: Avatar: The Way of Water
overview: Set more than a decade after the events of the first film, learn the story of the Sully family (Jake, Neytiri, and their kids), the trouble that follows them, the lengths they go to keep each other safe, the battles they fight to stay alive, and the tragedies they endure.
review:
Avatar: The Way of Water is James Cameron’s long-awaited return to Pandora, and it’s exactly the kind of lush, epic sci-fi fantasy you’d expect from the director who practically invented the modern blockbuster. More family drama than the first film, it leans into the Sully clan’s attempts to survive and protect each other amid new threats. Fans of the original’s visual spectacle will appreciate the underwater world-building here, which feels like Avatar meets a nature documentary on steroids — though the story itself sometimes stumbles under the weight of its own ambitions.

What stands out most is the jaw-dropping underwater cinematography and immersive world design. The tagline “Return to Pandora” is more than a promise; it’s a dive into a visually rich ecosystem filled with new tribes, creatures, and conflicts. The Sully family’s dynamic adds emotional stakes, but the screenplay occasionally gets bogged down by clichés and melodrama. Still, Kate Winslet and Sigourney Weaver bring memorable new characters that help expand the universe beyond the original’s scope.

Heads up for sensitive viewers: this one features a heavy dose of animal-related distress, including multiple animal deaths and abuse, which might be tough to handle. If the thought of spiders, snakes, or bugs crawling around makes you uneasy, be warned—they’re part of this wild, natural world. Also, those who are sensitive to themes of gaslighting and body horror should take caution. The film’s darker moments aren’t just about visual thrills but also some grim emotional beats.
emailReview:
James Cameron’s Avatar: The Way of Water dazzles with jaw-dropping underwater cinematography and memorable performances from Kate Winslet and Sigourney Weaver, turning Pandora into a lush, immersive world that’s part sci-fi fantasy, part nature documentary on steroids.

Be prepared for: multiple animal deaths and abuse, unsettling spiders and snakes, intense body horror, and themes of gaslighting.

writers: Ryan Reynolds, Rhett Reese, Paul Wernick, Zeb Wells, Shawn Levy, Rob Liefeld, Fabian Nicieza, Len Wein, John Romita Sr., Herb Trimpe, Roy Thomas, Joe Simon, Jack Kirby, Frank Miller
name: Deadpool & Wolverine
overview: A listless Wade Wilson toils away in civilian life with his days as the morally flexible mercenary, Deadpool, behind him. But when his homeworld faces an existential threat, Wade must reluctantly suit-up again with an even more reluctant Wolverine.
review:
Deadpool & Wolverine is the ultimate odd couple superhero flick that leans hard into the irreverent, meta humor Deadpool fans crave while giving Wolverine his usual brooding edge. It’s a wild ride that feels like a mashup of classic Deadpool antics and the grittier, more reluctant hero vibes of Logan, with Ryan Reynolds and Hugh Jackman slipping back into their iconic roles with ease. While it doesn’t completely reinvent the wheel, it’s a satisfying punch of action and comedy that fans of Marvel’s more chaotic side will appreciate, even if it’s not as sharp as the best Deadpool solo outings.

What stands out here is the dynamic between Wade and Logan—two very different flavors of anti-hero forced to “come together” against a bigger threat. The tagline nails the tone: a partnership that’s equal parts reluctant and ridiculous. Emma Corrin and Matthew Macfadyen add some intriguing layers as Cassandra Nova and Mr. Paradox, respectively, giving the story some unexpected depth amid the chaos. The writing team, including Reynolds himself, keeps the snark flying, and Shawn Levy’s direction balances the blockbuster spectacle with moments that feel genuinely fun rather than just loud.

Heads up for anyone sensitive to intense content: this one throws a lot at you, including blood/gore, animal deaths (including a dog and a cat), and some scenes with flashing lights that might be a headache for folks prone to seizures. There’s also sexual assault mentioned and depicted, along with several crashes and drownings, so those triggers are worth noting before diving in. It’s a messy, loud, and sometimes brutal superhero romp that doesn’t shy away from the darker or more graphic moments.
emailReview:
Deadpool & Wolverine serves up a wild, irreverent superhero mashup with Ryan Reynolds and Hugh Jackman slipping easily back into their iconic roles amid sharp snark and unexpected depth.

Be prepared for: graphic blood and gore, animal deaths including a dog and a cat, flashing lights that may trigger seizures, sexual assault depictions, and intense crash and drowning scenes.

name: 28 Days Later
overview: Twenty-eight days after a killer virus was accidentally unleashed from a British research facility, a small group of London survivors are caught in a desperate struggle to protect themselves from the infected. Carried by animals and humans, the virus turns those it infects into homicidal maniacs -- and it's absolutely impossible to contain.
review:
Danny Boyle’s 2002 thriller *28 Days Later* is a game-changer in the zombie genre — a grim, relentless plunge into a post-apocalyptic London that feels more raw and urgent than the usual undead fare. If you’re into fast-paced, high-stakes horror that blends the desolation of *The Road* with the adrenaline of *Dawn of the Dead*, this one’s a must-watch. Cillian Murphy’s performance as Jim, waking up to a world overrun by rage-infected humans, grounds the chaos with a mix of vulnerability and grit. It’s not just about scares — there’s a bleak emotional core that sticks with you.

What stands out is how the film leans hard into the horror of infection and societal collapse, using the tagline “The days are numbered” to good effect. The infected aren’t slow shamblers but rabid maniacs, which cranks up the tension. The abandoned hospital scene and the eerie emptiness of London streets are iconic visuals, while Alex Garland’s writing keeps the story tight and thematically heavy — exploring survival, trust, and the dark side of humanity when the world falls apart. Danny Boyle’s kinetic direction and the pulsing score ratchet up the dread without ever feeling gratuitous.

That said, this film is not for the faint of heart. Those who pin the blood/gore and jump scares triggers should be cautious — the infected attacks are frequent and brutal. Animal lovers beware: early scenes show chimpanzees in cages, experiments, and distress. The film also includes graphic depictions of sexual assault and child abuse, making it a tough watch in its later act. If any of those hit your list hard, brace yourself.
emailReview:
Danny Boyle’s 28 Days Later reinvents zombie horror with a relentless pace, stark London landscapes, and a gripping lead performance from Cillian Murphy that grounds the chaos in raw emotion.

Be prepared for: graphic chimpanzee distress and experiments, brutal infected attacks, sexual assault, and child abuse.

primaryTitle: Back to the Future Part III
Title_IMDb_Link: Back to the Future Part III
name: Back to the Future Part III
cleanNameArticles: back to the future part iii
overview: The final installment of the Back to the Future trilogy finds Marty digging the trusty DeLorean out of a mineshaft and looking for Doc in the Wild West of 1885. But when their time machine breaks down, the travelers are stranded in a land of spurs. More problems arise when Doc falls for pretty schoolteacher Clara Clayton, and Marty tangles with Buford Tannen.
tagline: They've saved the best trip for last... But this time they may have gone too far.

writers: Jay Cocks, Steven Zaillian, Kenneth Lonergan
name: Gangs of New York
overview: In early 1860s New York, Irish immigrant Amsterdam Vallon is released from prison and returns to the Five Points, seeking revenge against his father's killer, William Cutting, a powerful anti-immigrant gang leader. He knows that revenge can only be attained by infiltrating Cutting's inner circle. Vallon's journey becomes a fight for personal survival and to find a place for the Irish people.
tagline: America was born in the streets.
review:
Gangs of New York is a brutal, sprawling historical epic that feels like Scorsese’s blood-soaked answer to a revenge western set in the roiling chaos of 1860s New York. It’s got the swagger of classic mob films but drenched in grime and political tension, with Daniel Day-Lewis absolutely stealing the show as the merciless Bill “The Butcher” Cutting. While it’s not quite as tight or electrifying as Goodfellas, it’s elevated by its ambition and the dense, immersive world-building that pulls you into the Five Points with every dirty street and violent clash.

The film’s tagline, “America was born in the streets,” nails the theme perfectly—this is a movie about identity, immigration, and the brutal fight for survival in a city that’s as unforgiving as its characters. The gritty visuals and period detail are stunning, and the score pulses with a foreboding energy that keeps you on edge. Leonardo DiCaprio’s Amsterdam Vallon provides a solid emotional anchor, but it’s the ferocity of the power struggles and the moral ambiguity that really linger. It’s not just a revenge tale; it’s a meditation on the birth of a nation through blood and fire.

Heads up for animal lovers and those sensitive to distressing content: Gangs of New York features several scenes involving animal harm and death, including horses, dogs, and cats. If you have a low tolerance for animal suffering or unsettling imagery involving creatures, be cautious going in.
emailReview:
Gangs of New York is a gritty, blood-soaked saga that blends Scorsese’s signature mob swagger with a raw, immersive dive into 1860s New York’s violent underworld, anchored by Daniel Day-Lewis’s unforgettable ferocity as Bill “The Butcher” Cutting.

Be prepared for: graphic animal harm involving horses, dogs, and cats, intense street violence, and emotionally charged scenes of survival and brutality.

name: The Hurt Locker
overview: Forced to play a dangerous game of cat-and-mouse in the chaos of war, an elite Army bomb squad unit must come together in a city where everyone is a potential enemy and every object could be a deadly bomb.
tagline: You don't have to be a hero to do this job. But it helps.
review:
Kathryn Bigelow’s *The Hurt Locker* is a tense, immersive war drama that feels less like a traditional action film and more like a psychological thriller set in a war zone. Jeremy Renner’s magnetic portrayal of Staff Sergeant William James anchors a story that’s as much about the addictive rush of danger as it is about the physical threats of bomb disposal. It’s not your typical heroic tale—if anything, it’s a gritty, unflinching look at soldiers who don’t just face death, they almost court it. Fans of intense, character-driven war films like *Zero Dark Thirty* or *Black Hawk Down* will find this one a compelling, sometimes harrowing ride.

What stands out most here is the film’s ability to ratchet up tension without relying on explosions every five minutes. The writing and direction lean into the claustrophobia and paranoia of urban combat, making every object in the city feel ominous. The tagline, “You don’t have to be a hero to do this job. But it helps,” nails the film’s complex take on bravery and recklessness. The supporting cast, including Anthony Mackie and Guy Pearce, adds depth to the team dynamic, but it’s Renner’s jittery intensity that really drives the narrative. The film also explores how war warps normal life, subtly captured in quiet moments with Evangeline Lilly’s character back home.

Be heavily warned if animal-related content is on your list—*The Hurt Locker* includes multiple instances of animal deaths and abuse, including dog fighting and the death of various animals like cats, dogs, and horses. This is not a war film that shies away from the collateral damage on all fronts, so those sensitive to animal harm will want to approach with caution.
emailReview:
Kathryn Bigelow’s *The Hurt Locker* is a gripping psychological thriller disguised as a war film, powered by Jeremy Renner’s intense, magnetic performance that pulls you into the addictive chaos of bomb disposal.

Be prepared for: graphic animal deaths including dog fighting, harm to cats and horses, and brutal scenes of animal abuse.

writers: Michael Bacall, Edgar Wright, Bryan Lee O'Malley
name: Scott Pilgrim vs. the World
overview: As bass guitarist for a garage-rock band, Scott Pilgrim has never had trouble getting a girlfriend; usually, the problem is getting rid of them. But when Ramona Flowers skates into his heart, he finds she has the most troublesome baggage of all: an army of ex-boyfriends who will stop at nothing to eliminate him from her list of suitors.

name: Collateral
overview: Cab driver Max picks up a man who offers him $600 to drive him around. But the promise of easy money sours when Max realizes his fare is an assassin.
tagline: It started like any other night.
review:
Collateral is a sleek, tense thriller that rides the night streets of L.A. with the kind of polished style Michael Mann is known for. It feels like Heat distilled into a single night, with Tom Cruise playing a chillingly calm assassin and Jamie Foxx as the cab driver caught in his web. The film’s noir-ish vibe and tight pacing make it a gripping watch, even if it doesn’t reinvent the genre. Fans of character-driven crime dramas will appreciate the dynamic between Vincent and Max, though it leans more into mood and atmosphere than explosive twists.

What’s really worth noting is how the film uses the city itself almost as a character—the neon lights, the rain-slicked streets, and the quiet hum of nighttime L.A. give it a moody, immersive quality. The tagline, “It started like any other night,” perfectly sets the tone for a story that slowly ratchets up the stakes. Cruise is at his coldest here, playing opposite Foxx’s more grounded and increasingly desperate Max, which makes their evolving relationship the emotional core amid the violence and suspense. And if you’re into films where the score and cinematography work hand-in-hand to create a palpable tension, this one delivers.

Be heavily warned if animal harm is a sensitive topic for you. The film features multiple triggers related to animals, including deaths and abuse, which are quite prominent throughout. Those who pin the “a dog dies” or “a horse dies” triggers should definitely approach with caution.
emailReview:
Collateral prowls the neon-lit streets of L.A. with sleek style and simmering tension, anchored by Tom Cruise’s chilling assassin and Jamie Foxx’s desperate cabbie caught in the crossfire.

Be prepared for: dog death, horse death, animal abuse, and intense animal harm scenes.

writers: Peter Craig, Ben Affleck, Aaron Stockard, Chuck Hogan
name: The Town
overview: Doug MacRay is a longtime thief, who, smarter than the rest of his crew, is looking for his chance to exit the game. When a bank job leads to the group kidnapping an attractive branch manager, he takes on the role of monitoring her – but their burgeoning relationship threatens to unveil the identities of Doug and his crew to the FBI Agent who is on their case.
tagline: Welcome to the bank robbery capital of America.

writers: Andrew Neiderman, Jonathan Lemkin, Tony Gilroy
name: The Devil's Advocate
overview: Aspiring Florida defense lawyer Kevin Lomax accepts a job at a New York law firm. With the stakes getting higher every case, Kevin quickly learns that his boss has something far more evil planned.
tagline: The newest attorney at the world's most powerful law firm has never lost a case. But he's about to lose his soul.

writers: Bob Kane, Sam Hamm, Warren Skaaren
name: Batman
overview: Having witnessed his parents' brutal murder as a child, millionaire philanthropist Bruce Wayne fights crime in Gotham City disguised as Batman, a costumed hero who strikes fear into the hearts of villains. But when a deformed madman known as 'The Joker' seizes control of Gotham's criminal underworld, Batman must face his most ruthless nemesis ever while protecting both his identity and his love interest, reporter Vicki Vale.
tagline: Justice is always darkest before the dawn.

writers: Danny Boyle, Simon Beaufoy, Aron Ralston
name: 127 Hours
overview: The true story of mountain climber Aron Ralston's remarkable adventure to save himself after a fallen boulder crashes on his arm and traps him in an isolated canyon in Utah.

writers: Michael McDowell, Larry Wilson, Warren Skaaren
name: Beetlejuice
overview: A newly dead New England couple seeks help from a deranged demon exorcist to scare an affluent New York family out of their home.
tagline: In this house... if you've seen one ghost... you haven't seen them all.

writers: Stanley Kubrick, Frederic Raphael, Arthur Schnitzler
name: Eyes Wide Shut
