overview: A dog goes on quest to discover his purpose in life over the course of several lifetimes with multiple owners.
tagline: Every dog happens for a reason.
review:
A Dog’s Purpose is the kind of heartstring-tugging family drama that leans hard into the sentimental, tracing a dog’s journey through multiple lifetimes and owners in search of meaning. It’s a soft, warm-hearted tale that feels like Lassie meets a lifetime of pet Instagram stories, with Josh Gad lending a likable voice to the canine protagonist. While it doesn’t reinvent the wheel and occasionally dips into melodrama, it’s elevated by genuine moments of connection and some solid performances, especially from Dennis Quaid as Adult Ethan. Fans of animal-centric stories that explore the bond between pets and humans will find plenty to like here.

The movie’s tagline, “Every dog happens for a reason,” nails its tone—this is a story about purpose, loyalty, and the simple but profound impact a dog can have on a person’s life. The narrative hops between eras and owners, which can feel a bit episodic, but it’s balanced by a sweet score and some visually appealing, cozy scenes that capture the essence of domestic life. It’s not just a dog movie—it’s a meditation on life, loss, and the idea that love transcends time and bodies. That said, the writing sometimes slips into cliché, and the emotional beats might hit some viewers harder than others.

Heads up for viewers sensitive to animal-related content: this film includes several scenes involving animal death and abuse, including dog fighting and the death of pets, which might be tough to watch. There are also sightings of spiders, snakes, and bugs if those are on your radar. Those who pin the animal harm or pet death triggers should be cautious, as the film doesn’t shy away from some realistically harsh moments in the animals’ lives.
emailReview:
A Dog’s Purpose is a warm-hearted family drama that blends heartfelt moments with a cozy, nostalgic vibe, brought to life by Josh Gad’s charming canine narration and Dennis Quaid’s grounded performance.

Be prepared for: dog fighting, pet death, animal abuse, and unsettling scenes with spiders and snakes.

tagline: They're back from the grave and ready to party!
review:
The Return of the Living Dead is a cult-classic horror-comedy that leans hard into its 80s B-movie charm, blending goofy slapstick with genuinely creepy undead chaos. It’s like Ghostbusters meets Night of the Living Dead, only with more brains and a whole lot more punk attitude. While it doesn’t shy away from gore and scares, it’s elevated by a self-aware tone that keeps it from feeling like just another zombie flick. Fans of campy horror with a side of dark humor will find a lot to love here.

What really stands out is how the film plays with the zombie genre’s tropes — zombies craving brains instead of just flesh is a memorable twist, and the bumbling warehouse workers add a layer of chaotic fun to the proceedings. Dan O’Bannon’s direction balances horror and comedy with a wicked score and practical effects that still hold up as delightfully gross and inventive. The tagline “They’re Back From The Grave and Ready To Party!” perfectly sums up the film’s irreverent spirit, making it less about dread and more about a wild, bloody good time.

That said, be heavily warned if jump scares, intense blood and gore, or the death of kids and animals are on your list. The movie doesn’t pull punches with brutal scenes including someone being burned alive and some pretty graphic mutilation. There’s also a handful of other unsettling moments like dogs and cats dying, spiders, and flashing lights that sensitive viewers should keep in mind before diving in.
emailReview:
The Return of the Living Dead is a cult classic that mixes 80s B-movie charm with punk attitude, delivering a wild blend of slapstick comedy and undead horror that still feels fresh and fun.

Be prepared for: burned alive scenes, graphic mutilation, animal deaths, spiders, and flashing lights.

writers: Brian De Palma, Bill Mesce Jr.
name: Blow Out
overview: Jack Terry is a master sound recordist who works on grade-B horror movies. Late one evening, he is recording sounds for use in his movies when he hears something unexpected through his sound equipment and records it. Curiosity gets the better of him when the media become involved, and he begins to unravel the pieces of a nefarious conspiracy. As he struggles to survive against his shadowy enemies and expose the truth, he does not know whom he can trust.
tagline: Murder has a sound all of its own.

writers: Michelangelo Antonioni, Julio Cortázar, Tonino Guerra, Edward Bond
name: Blow-Up
overview: A successful mod photographer in London whose world is bounded by fashion, pop music, marijuana, and easy sex, feels his life is boring and despairing. But in the course of a single day he accidentally captures on film the commission of a murder. The fact that he has photographed a murder does not occur to him until he studies and then blows up his negatives, uncovering details, blowing up smaller and smaller elements, and finally putting the puzzle together.
tagline: Sometimes, reality is the strangest fantasy of all.

writers: Thomas Malory, Rospo Pallenberg, John Boorman
name: Excalibur
overview: A surreal adaptation of Sir Thomas Malory's "Le Morte d'Arthur", chronicling Arthur Pendragon's conception, his rise to the throne, the search by his Knights of the Round Table for the Holy Grail, and ultimately his death.
tagline: Forged by a god. Foretold by a wizard. Found by a king.

writers: David DiGilio, Toshirô Ishidô, Koreyoshi Kurahara, Tatsuo Nogami, Susumu Saji
name: Eight Below
overview: In the Antarctic, after an expedition with Dr. Davis McClaren, the sled dog trainer Jerry Shepherd has to leave the polar base with his colleagues due to the proximity of a heavy snow storm. He ties his dogs to be rescued after, but the mission is called-off and the dogs are left alone at their own fortune. For six months, Jerry tries to find a sponsor for a rescue mission.

name: High Plains Drifter
overview: A gunfighting stranger comes to the small settlement of Lago. After gunning down three gunmen who tried to kill him, the townsfolk decide to hire the Stranger to hold off three outlaws who are on their way.
tagline: They'd never forget the day he drifted into town.

name: The Mission
overview: When a Spanish Jesuit goes into the South American wilderness to build a mission in the hope of converting the Indians of the region, a slave hunter is converted and joins his mission. When Spain sells the colony to Portugal, they are forced to defend all they have built against the Portugese aggressors.
tagline: One will trust in the power of prayer. One will believe in the might of the sword.

name: Mirage
overview: A desperate photographer who suffers from a degenerative eye disease and a husband who wants to kill his dying wife, plot to recover her life insurance.

name: Terms of Endearment
overview: Aurora, a finicky woman, is in search of true love while her daughter faces marital issues. Together, they help each other deal with problems and find reasons to live a joyful life.

name: Pale Rider
overview: A small gold mining camp is terrorised by a ruthless land owner wanting to take their land. Clint Eastwood arrives riding a pale horse just as a young girl is praying to God to help the miners. He is revealed to be a preacher with mysterious and possible otherworldly origins who teams up with the miners to defeat the land owner and the corrupt sheriff.

name: 5 Centimeters per Second
overview: Three moments in Takaki's life: his relationship with Akari and their forced separation; his friendship with Kanae, who is secretly in love with him; the demands and disappointments of adulthood, an unhappy life in a cold city.
tagline: At what speed must I live to see you again?
review:
Really beautiful film. The artwork is incredibly stunning, the writing is poetic, and it really nails the conflicting feelings one encounters during the coming-of-age period in our lives. The first chapter, in particular, is sweet, wholesome, and surprisingly romantic.

A quick watch at just over an hour in length, featuring only a small number of triggers, makes it pretty easy to enjoy the storyline without much worry or fear.
emailReview:
A beautifully crafted coming-of-age film with stunning artwork and poetic writing that captures the bittersweet swirl of youth with a surprisingly romantic first chapter.

Be prepared for: brief emotional distress, mild language, and a moment of implied self-harm.

name: Downton Abbey: The Movie
overview: The beloved Crawleys and their intrepid staff prepare for the most important moment of their lives. A royal visit from the King and Queen of England will unleash scandal, romance and intrigue that will leave the future of Downton hanging in the balance.

name: Fish Tank
overview: Everything changes for 15-year-old Mia when her mum brings home a new boyfriend.

writers: David Zelag Goodman, Sam Peckinpah, Gordon Williams
name: Straw Dogs
overview: David Sumner, a mild-mannered academic from the United States, marries Amy, an Englishwoman. In order to escape a hectic stateside lifestyle, David and his wife relocate to the small town in rural Cornwall where Amy was raised. There, David is ostracized by the brutish men of the village, including Amy's old flame, Charlie. Eventually the taunts escalate, and two of the locals rape Amy. This sexual assault awakes a shockingly violent side of David.

name: Steel Magnolias
overview: This heart wrenching drama is about a beauty shop, in Louisana owned by Truvy, and the tragedies of all of her clients.
tagline: Six extraordinary friends. They share each other's laughter. They dry each other's tears.
review:
Steel Magnolias is a classic Southern drama that mixes heartfelt emotion with sharp humor, anchored by an unforgettable ensemble cast including Sally Field, Dolly Parton, and a young Julia Roberts. It’s the kind of film that feels like Steel Magnolias meets a warm, small-town soap opera—intimate, character-driven, and often uplifting despite its heavy themes. While it’s not exactly a laugh-out-loud comedy, it balances tears and smiles in a way that still resonates decades later.

What really stands out here is the way the film captures the tight-knit bonds forged in a Louisiana beauty shop, where Truvy (Parton) and her clients share life’s joys and tragedies. The dialogue, penned by Robert Harling, is sharp and often poetic, giving each character a distinct voice and plenty of memorable moments. The tagline, “Six extraordinary friends. They share each other's laughter. They dry each other's tears,” perfectly sums up the emotional rollercoaster that unfolds, especially as the story digs into some tough realities faced by these women.

Heads up to anyone sensitive to animal-related content: Steel Magnolias includes several upsetting animal deaths, including dogs, cats, and a horse, as well as some scenes implying animal abuse. If those triggers are on your radar, be prepared for some heavy moments on that front.
emailReview:
Steel Magnolias blends heartfelt Southern charm with sharp humor and unforgettable performances from Sally Field, Dolly Parton, and Julia Roberts, creating a warm, intimate drama that still tugs at the heartstrings.

Be prepared for: multiple upsetting animal deaths including dogs, cats, and a horse, along with implied animal abuse.

overview: Dolores Claiborne was accused of killing her abusive husband twenty years ago, but the court's findings were inconclusive and she was allowed to walk free. Things look bad for Dolores when her daughter Selena, a successful Manhattan magazine writer, returns to cover the story.

name: Far from Heaven
overview: In 1950s Connecticut, a housewife faces a marital crisis and mounting racial tensions in the outside world.

name: Starred Up
overview: 19-year-old Eric, arrogant and ultra-violent, is prematurely transferred to the same adult prison facility as his estranged father. As his explosive temper quickly finds him enemies in both prison authorities and fellow inmates — and his already volatile relationship with his father is pushed past breaking point — Eric is approached by a volunteer psychotherapist, who runs an anger management group for prisoners. Torn between gang politics, prison corruption, and a glimmer of something better, Eric finds himself in a fight for his own life, unsure if his own father is there to protect him or join in punishing him.

name: Mice And Men
overview: Two drifters, one a gentle but slow giant, try to make money working the fields during the Depression so they can fulfill their dreams.
tagline: We have a dream. Someday, we'll have a little house and a couple of acres. A place to call home.
review:
Mice And Men is a somber, faithful adaptation of Steinbeck’s classic Depression-era tale, anchored by an intense John Malkovich as Lennie and a grounded Gary Sinise pulling double duty as both George and director. It’s the kind of dusty, slow-burning drama that fans of literary adaptations or period pieces will appreciate, though it doesn’t exactly reinvent the wheel. If you’re into character-driven stories about friendship and shattered dreams, this one hits the familiar beats with a quiet dignity but doesn’t stray far from the source material’s well-trod path.

The film’s strength lies in its performances and the way it captures the bleakness of the 1930s farm life. The tagline—“We have a dream. Someday, we'll have a little house and a couple of acres. A place to call home.”—echoes through the story, emphasizing the fragile hope that drives these two drifters. Horton Foote’s screenplay keeps the dialogue sparse but meaningful, while the supporting cast, including Sherilyn Fenn and Ray Walston, adds texture to this world of hardship and small kindnesses. Visually, it’s a straightforward period piece, leaning on atmosphere rather than flashy cinematography.

A heads-up for sensitive viewers: the film contains some difficult content, notably involving bestiality and the death of non-human characters (yes, a “dragon” dies, but in this case that means animals, not fantasy creatures). Those who pin these triggers should be cautious going in, as these moments are integral to the story’s emotional weight and not treated lightly.
emailReview:
Mice And Men delivers a quietly powerful period drama anchored by John Malkovich’s intense performance and a somber look at 1930s farm life filled with fragile hope and shattered dreams.

Be prepared for: animal death, bestiality, and emotionally heavy moments involving vulnerable creatures.

name: Searching for Bobby Fischer
overview: A prepubescent chess prodigy refuses to harden himself in order to become a champion like the famous but unlikable Bobby Fischer.
tagline: Every journey begins with a single move.
review:
Searching for Bobby Fischer is a quietly compelling drama that blends the intensity of a sports movie with the charm of a coming-of-age tale. It’s less about the cutthroat world of competitive chess and more about the emotional journey of a young prodigy who wants to play on his own terms. Think of it as a gentler, more thoughtful counterpart to the usual “genius at all costs” biopics—fans of films like The Queen’s Gambit might appreciate this film’s subtler, more grounded take on the pressures of mastery.

What really stands out is the way the film captures the tension between ambition and innocence. The tagline, “Every journey begins with a single move,” feels fitting because it’s not just about chess moves but life choices. The performances are solid, especially Max Pomeranc as Josh Waitzkin, whose boyish earnestness anchors the story. The supporting cast, including Ben Kingsley as the wise coach and Laurence Fishburne in a more surprising role, adds depth without overshadowing the young lead. Steven Zaillian’s writing and direction keep the tone tender and thoughtful, avoiding the usual sports movie clichés in favor of a more nuanced portrait of childhood, competition, and integrity.

Heads up for those sensitive to animal content—this one includes multiple animal deaths and scenes of animal abuse that might hit hard for animal lovers. If you’ve got pets or animals on your trigger list, be prepared for some tough moments, as it’s not just a single fleeting scene but a recurring element throughout the film.
emailReview:
Searching for Bobby Fischer is a quietly compelling blend of sports intensity and coming-of-age charm, anchored by Max Pomeranc’s earnest performance and a thoughtful, tender tone that avoids typical clichés.

Be prepared for: multiple animal deaths, scenes of animal abuse, and emotionally charged moments involving pets.

name: Picnic at Hanging Rock

review:
Are You There God? It's Me, Margaret is a thoughtful coming-of-age dramedy that leans into the awkward, tender moments of adolescence with a gentle, nostalgic touch. Adapted from Judy Blume’s iconic 1970 novel, this 2023 film feels like a warm hug for anyone who’s ever wrestled with identity, faith, and the confusing rites of puberty. It’s not quite as sharp or funny as some modern teen comedies, but Kelly Fremon Craig’s direction and Abby Ryder Fortson’s earnest performance as Margaret give it a sincere, grounded charm that fans of heartfelt YA adaptations will appreciate.

What stands out here is the film’s candid exploration of growing up — from hormonal changes to religious questioning — all wrapped in a tone that’s neither preachy nor overly sentimental. The tagline, “Discovering who you are is a journey that lasts a lifetime,” sets the stage for a narrative that embraces uncertainty and self-discovery without easy answers. Supporting performances from Rachel McAdams and Kathy Bates add emotional depth, portraying family dynamics with both humor and heart. The film doesn’t shy away from some heavier moments, balancing the tender with the sometimes uncomfortable realities of adolescence.

Heads up for sensitive viewers: this one includes triggers around animal deaths (including a dog, horse, and cat), blood and gore, and some body-focused distress like shaving and finger/toe mutilation. There are also moments involving a parent’s death and other intense emotional beats, so those who are cautious about grief or animal harm should proceed thoughtfully.

name: A Dog's Journey
overview: A dog finds the meaning of his own existence through the lives of the humans he meets.
review:
A Dog's Journey leans hard into the emotional, family-friendly drama territory, a spiritual sequel to its predecessor that fans of tearjerker pet stories will find comforting, if not especially groundbreaking. It’s very much “Marley & Me meets The Art of Racing in the Rain” — a heartfelt canine odyssey that traces one dog’s reincarnated soul through multiple lifetimes, trying to find meaning in the humans he loves. Josh Gad’s voice work as the dog(s) adds a bit of warmth and humor, but the film’s tone stays earnest and sentimental throughout, which will either charm or wear thin depending on your tolerance for mushy pet stories.

The film’s tagline, “Some friendships transcend lifetimes,” sums up its core theme: loyalty, love, and the bittersweet nature of life and death. The writing leans on familiar tropes — dogs as emotional anchors for struggling humans, lessons about family and growing up — but it earns some points for highlighting cancer detection dogs, a neat real-world connection that adds some depth. Visually it’s straightforward, focusing on quiet moments rather than flashy effects, which fits the gentle storytelling style. While it doesn’t reinvent the wheel, the performances from the human cast, including Dennis Quaid and Betty Gilpin, provide solid grounding.

Those who pin the “a dog dies” trigger should be cautious, as multiple dog deaths are central to the plot, depicted with a surprisingly tender touch but no less heart-wrenching. The euthanasia scene involving needles is handled with care but is unavoidable, and the cancer storyline affecting both humans and dogs means this one hits some heavy emotional beats. If you’re sensitive to pet loss or illness, prepare for a full spectrum of feels.
emailReview:
A Dog's Journey delivers a heartfelt, sentimental canine saga with warm voice work from Josh Gad and solid performances from Dennis Quaid and Betty Gilpin, perfect for fans of tearjerker pet stories craving emotional depth without flashy distractions.

Be prepared for: multiple dog deaths, euthanasia scenes involving needles, cancer in both pets and humans, and the heavy emotional weight of loss and loyalty.
