writers: Ehren Kruger, Kôji Suzuki, Hiroshi Takahashi
name: The Ring
overview: Rachel Keller is a journalist investigating a videotape that may have killed four teenagers. There is an urban legend about this tape: the viewer will die seven days after watching it. Rachel tracks down the video... and watches it. Now she has just seven days to unravel the mystery of the Ring so she can save herself and her son.
review:
The Ring is a classic early-2000s horror that still holds up as a chilling blend of supernatural dread and investigative thriller. Directed by Gore Verbinski and anchored by Naomi Watts’s determined performance as journalist Rachel Keller, it feels like The X-Files meets a haunted VHS tape—and that’s a combo that really sticks with you. It’s not just your run-of-the-mill jump-scare fest; it leans heavily into atmosphere and mounting unease, making the slow unraveling of the cursed videotape’s mystery genuinely gripping.

What stands out here is the film’s clever use of urban legend and media paranoia, wrapped in a moody, rain-soaked aesthetic that’s become iconic for this era of horror. The tagline, “Before you die, you see,” perfectly captures the film’s fatalistic tension. The story’s pulse quickens as Rachel races against time to save herself and her son, weaving in smart scares with a haunting visual style. Plus, the eerie, almost hypnotic quality of the tape itself is a nightmare fuel that still lingers long after the credits roll.

Heads up for animal lovers: The Ring includes at least one upsetting scene involving a horse, so if that trigger hits hard for you, be cautious going in. It’s a small but memorable moment that adds to the film’s unsettling atmosphere. If supernatural horror with a slow-burn mystery is your thing, this one’s a must-watch—just maybe keep the lights on.
emailReview:
The Ring is a moody, rain-soaked horror classic that blends supernatural dread with a smart, slow-burning mystery anchored by Naomi Watts’s gripping performance.

Be prepared for: a disturbing horse death, eerie supernatural visuals, and mounting psychological tension.

name: Pretty Woman
overview: When a millionaire wheeler-dealer enters a business contract with a Hollywood hooker Vivian Ward, he loses his heart in the bargain.
tagline: She walked off the street, into his life and stole his heart.

writers: John Gatins, Dan Gilroy, Jeremy Leven, Richard Matheson
name: Real Steel
overview: Charlie Kenton is a washed-up fighter who retired from the ring when robots took over the sport. After his robot is trashed, he reluctantly teams up with his estranged son to rebuild and train an unlikely contender.
review:
Real Steel is a gleaming slice of sci-fi sports drama that feels like Rocky meets Transformers—minus the giant robots running amok, but with plenty of metal fists flying. Hugh Jackman carries the film as Charlie Kenton, a down-on-his-luck ex-fighter who’s got a second shot at redemption thanks to an unlikely alliance with his scrappy kid, Max. It’s a family story wrapped in a futuristic boxing ring, and while it doesn’t reinvent the wheel, it’s definitely a crowd-pleaser with enough heart to keep it from feeling like just another robot flick.

What really stands out is the chemistry between Jackman and Dakota Goyo as the estranged father and son duo trying to build a contender from scrap metal. The tagline “Courage is stronger than steel” nails the film’s emotional core—this is as much about human grit and connection as it is about robot brawling. The visuals lean into a sleek, gritty near-future vibe, and director Shawn Levy keeps the pace brisk enough to make the robot fights satisfying without overwhelming the story. Fans of underdog tales and family dramas will find plenty to like here, even if the plot hits some familiar beats.

Heads up for anyone sensitive to the death of non-human characters—there’s a notable moment that might sting if you’re attached to the robots in this world. Otherwise, Real Steel keeps its trigger profile pretty light, focusing more on emotional punches than anything graphic or upsetting.
emailReview: Real Steel combines heartfelt family drama with high-energy robot boxing, anchored by Hugh Jackman’s strong performance and a surprisingly tender father-son bond. Be prepared for: robot death, emotional loss, and tense fight scenes.

name: Shooter
overview: A marksman living in exile is coaxed back into action after learning of a plot to kill the president. Ultimately double-crossed and framed for the attempt, he goes on the run to track the real killer and find out who exactly set him up, and why??
tagline: Yesterday was about honor. Today is about justice.

name: The Mist
overview: After a violent storm, a dense cloud of mist envelops a small Maine town, trapping artist David Drayton and his five-year-old son in a local grocery store with other people. They soon discover that the mist conceals deadly horrors that threaten their lives, and worse, their sanity.

writers: Stephen Chbosky, Evan Spiliotopoulos, Linda Woolverton, Jeanne-Marie Leprince de Beaumont, Gabrielle-Suzanne Barbot de Villeneuve
name: Beauty and the Beast
overview: A live-action adaptation of Disney's version of the classic tale of a cursed prince and a beautiful young woman who helps him break the spell.

name: Pitch Perfect
overview: College student Beca knows she does not want to be part of a clique, but that's exactly where she finds herself after arriving at her new school. Thrust in among mean gals, nice gals and just plain weird gals, Beca finds that the only thing they have in common is how well they sing together. She takes the women of the group out of their comfort zone of traditional arrangements and into a world of amazing harmonic combinations in a fight to the top of college music competitions.
review:
Pitch Perfect is that oddball blend of college comedy and musical underdog story that somehow manages to hit all the right notes without ever feeling too saccharine. It’s like Mean Girls meets a cappella competitions, with a dash of Bridesmaids-style humor—anchored by Anna Kendrick’s snarky charm as Beca, who drags her new clique out of their comfort zones and into some surprisingly inventive harmonies. It’s not going to win awards for depth, but it’s a pretty solid, feel-good romp elevated by some genuinely catchy performances and Rebel Wilson’s scene-stealing antics as Fat Amy.

What makes this one stand out isn’t just the mashup of traditional collegiate stereotypes with musical mashups, but how it balances the rivalry and camaraderie in a way that feels fresh. The tagline “Get pitch slapped” perfectly captures the film’s playful tone—there’s a lot of clever wordplay and sharp writing from Kay Cannon layered under Jason Moore’s direction. The plot’s familiar—girl joins clique, they compete, they bond—but the energy and humor make it more than just another teen movie. Plus, the soundtrack and vocal arrangements are fun enough to keep even non-musical types engaged.

Heads up for those who are sensitive: the film includes some upsetting animal-related content, including a dog death which might catch some viewers off guard. There’s also a parent’s death and a few moments of spitting and blood/gore to be aware of, alongside some shaky cam sequences that could be jarring. Sexual assault is referenced, so if that’s a trigger, proceed with caution. Overall, it’s a lighthearted movie with some dark patches sprinkled in.
emailReview:
Pitch Perfect is a snarky, feel-good college comedy with catchy musical numbers and standout performances from Anna Kendrick and Rebel Wilson that turn a familiar underdog story into a lively romp.

Be prepared for: a dog death, parent’s death, moments of blood and spitting, sexual assault references, and shaky cam sequences.

writers: Bob Kane, Daniel Waters, Sam Hamm
name: Batman Returns
overview: The monstrous Penguin, who dwells in the sewers beneath Gotham, joins up with corrupt mayoral candidate Max Shreck to topple the Batman once and for all. But when Shreck's timid assistant Selina Kyle finds out, and Shreck tries to kill her, she's transformed into the sexy Catwoman. She teams up with the Penguin and Shreck to destroy Batman, but sparks fly unexpectedly when she confronts the caped crusader.
tagline: The Bat. The Cat. The Penguin.

writers: Ed Decter, John J. Strauss, Peter Farrelly, Bobby Farrelly
name: There's Something About Mary
overview: For Ted, prom night went about as bad as it’s possible for any night to go. Thirteen years later, he finally gets another chance with his old prom date, only to run up against other suitors including the sleazy detective he hired to find her.
review:
There’s Something About Mary is the kind of raunchy romantic comedy that helped define late-90s comedy, mixing outrageous physical gags with a surprisingly sweet love story. It’s basically a Farrelly Brothers signature blend of gross-out humor and heartfelt charm, with Ben Stiller’s lovably awkward Ted chasing after Cameron Diaz’s effortlessly charismatic Mary. If you like your rom-coms with a heavy dose of slapstick and absurdity—think Dumb and Dumber meets traditional love story—you’ll find a lot to enjoy here, even if it’s not exactly highbrow.

What really stands out is how the film rides the line between cringe and endearing, especially through its memorable supporting characters like Matt Dillon’s sleazy private eye. The tagline “Love is in the hair” hints at one of the film’s signature bits—equally ridiculous and iconic. The writing leans into the chaos of Ted’s misadventures, keeping the laughs coming while still rooting for his reunion with Mary. The Farrelly Brothers’ knack for mixing gross-out humor with genuine emotion is in full effect, making it more than just a string of gags.

That said, heads up for anyone sensitive to animal harm triggers: the film includes scenes involving animal abuse and death, which might catch some viewers off guard amid the comedy. If those are on your list, be cautious, as these moments stand out in an otherwise lighthearted romp.
emailReview:
There’s Something About Mary is a late-90s rom-com classic that perfectly balances outrageous slapstick with genuine charm, anchored by Ben Stiller’s awkwardly endearing performance and Cameron Diaz’s magnetic presence.

Be prepared for: animal abuse, animal death, and gross-out physical humor that might surprise you in this otherwise lighthearted comedy.

name: Déjà Vu
overview: Called in to recover evidence in the aftermath of a horrific explosion on a New Orleans ferry, Federal agent Doug Carlin gets pulled away from the scene and taken to a top-secret government lab that uses a time-shifting surveillance device to help prevent crime.

name: Elf
overview: When young Buddy falls into Santa's gift sack on Christmas Eve, he's transported back to the North Pole and raised as a toy-making elf by Santa's helpers. But as he grows into adulthood, he can't shake the nagging feeling that he doesn't belong. Buddy vows to visit Manhattan and find his real dad, a workaholic publisher.

name: The Lobster
overview: In a dystopian near future, single people, according to the laws of The City, are taken to The Hotel, where they are obliged to find a romantic partner in forty-five days or are transformed into beasts and sent off into The Woods.
review:
The Lobster is a darkly absurdist take on the dystopian romantic comedy, blending deadpan humor with unsettling world-building in a way that fans of Yorgos Lanthimos’s signature style will appreciate. It’s like Black Mirror meets a twisted dating game, where the stakes are literally life or death—and your potential soulmate or your new animal form. Colin Farrell anchors the film with a stoic charm as David, navigating this bizarre society’s rules with a mix of desperation and dry wit. It’s not your typical love story, but it’s definitely one you won’t forget.

What really stands out here is the film’s relentless commitment to its off-kilter premise, using minimalist dialogue and deadpan performances to heighten the absurdity. The Hotel’s cold, clinical environment contrasts sharply with the wild, almost lawless Woods, creating a visual metaphor for society’s pressure to conform versus the freedom (and danger) of rebellion. Themes of loneliness, conformity, and the absurdity of social rituals pulse beneath the surface, all wrapped in Lanthimos’s trademark unsettling atmosphere. Rachel Weisz and Olivia Colman add memorable, quirky supporting turns that enrich this unconventional narrative.

Heads up for animal lovers: the film features multiple instances of animal death and abuse, including the deaths of a dog, a horse, and a cat, as well as other unsettling animal-related content. Those sensitive to these types of triggers—or to the film’s body horror and psychological manipulation—should tread cautiously. The Lobster isn’t just a weird love story; it’s a sharp, sometimes harsh critique of societal norms that doesn’t shy away from discomfort.
emailReview:
The Lobster blends deadpan humor with a chillingly absurd dystopian world where love comes with a bizarre and brutal twist, anchored by Colin Farrell’s stoic charm and a cold, clinical atmosphere that stays with you long after the credits roll.

Be prepared for: multiple animal deaths including a dog, horse, and cat, unsettling animal abuse, body horror, and psychological manipulation.

name: Blade
overview: When Blade's mother was bitten by a vampire during pregnancy, she did not know that she gave her son a special gift while dying—all the good vampire attributes in combination with the best human skills. Blade and his mentor battle an evil vampire rebel who plans to take over the outdated vampire council, capture Blade and resurrect a voracious blood god.
tagline: Against an army of Immortals, one warrior must draw first blood.
review:
Blade is a slick, darkly stylish vampire action flick that helped pioneer the modern superhero genre before it was cool. Wesley Snipes as the titular half-vampire, half-human vampire hunter gives the film its cool, brooding edge, making this feel like a cross between a gritty comic book adaptation and a '90s action thriller. Fans of cult classics like The Crow or even later vampire fare like Underworld will find Blade’s blend of horror and martial arts pretty satisfying, though it leans harder into the pulpy action than the scares.

What really stands out here is the mix of supernatural world-building with street-level grit—Blade’s origin story, where his mom’s vamp bite gifts him unique powers, sets up a classic underdog warrior tale. The villain, Deacon Frost, plotting to overthrow the vampire council and unleash an ancient blood god, adds a cool mythological flavor that gives the stakes some heft. The film’s tone is ably supported by a moody score and shadowy visuals that echo its tagline: “Against an army of Immortals, one warrior must draw first blood.” Plus, Kris Kristofferson’s mentor character adds a grounded, rugged contrast to the slicker vampire chaos.

Heads up for animal-sensitive viewers: Blade features multiple instances of animal deaths and abuse, including dogs, cats, horses, and other creatures—not to mention some unsettling bug and spider appearances. If you keep those triggers on your radar, be prepared for some tough scenes involving animals.
emailReview:
Blade is a slick, darkly stylish vampire action flick with Wesley Snipes delivering a brooding, cool edge that blends gritty comic book vibes with '90s martial arts flair.

Be prepared for: multiple animal deaths including dogs, cats, and horses, unsettling bug and spider appearances, and intense scenes of animal abuse.

name: Forgetting Sarah Marshall
overview: When Sarah Marshall dumps aspiring musician Peter Bretter for rock star Aldous Snow, Peter's world comes crashing down. His best friend suggests that Peter should get away from everything and to fly off to Hawaii to escape all his problems. After arriving in Hawaii and meeting the beautiful Rachel Jansen, Peter is shocked to see not only Aldous Snow in Hawaii, but also Sarah Marshall.
tagline: You lose some, you get some.

writers: John Wagner, Carlos Ezquerra, Alex Garland
name: Dredd
overview: In the future, America is a dystopian wasteland. The latest scourge is Ma-Ma, a prostitute-turned-drug pusher with a dangerous new drug and aims to take over the city. The only possibility of stopping her is an elite group of urban police called Judges, who combine the duties of judge, jury and executioner to deliver a brutal brand of swift justice. But even the top-ranking Judge, Dredd, discovers that taking down Ma-Ma isn’t as easy as it seems in this explosive adaptation of the hugely popular comic series.

writers: Anne Fine, Randi Mayem Singer, Leslie Dixon
name: Mrs Doubtfire
overview: Loving but irresponsible dad Daniel Hillard, estranged from his exasperated spouse, is crushed by a court order allowing only weekly visits with his kids. When Daniel learns his ex needs a housekeeper, he gets the job -- disguised as an English nanny. Soon he becomes not only his children's best pal but the kind of parent he should have been from the start.
tagline: She makes dinner. She does windows. She reads bedtime stories. She's a blessing... in disguise.

name: The Intern
overview: 70-year-old widower Ben Whittaker has discovered that retirement isn't all it's cracked up to be. Seizing an opportunity to get back in the game, he becomes a senior intern at an online fashion site, founded and run by Jules Ostin.
review:
The Intern is a gently charming dramedy that leans heavily into feel-good vibes with a dash of workplace comedy. It’s the kind of movie that feels like a warm cup of tea—familiar, comforting, and just a bit predictable. Robert De Niro’s turn as the wise, good-natured senior intern Ben Whitaker anchors the film, while Anne Hathaway’s portrayal of the driven fashion entrepreneur Jules Ostin adds some modern hustle to the mix. If you like Nancy Meyers’ other work—think The Holiday or Something’s Gotta Give—this fits snugly in that world, though it doesn’t quite reach the same emotional heights.

What stands out is the film’s exploration of age and purpose, with the tagline “Experience never gets old” hitting the core theme. Ben’s journey from retirement doldrums to proving his worth in a digital startup is sweet if somewhat safe, avoiding big risks in favor of gentle lessons about friendship, mentoring, and work-life balance. The chemistry between De Niro and Hathaway is pleasant but feels a little surface-level, with the script opting for easy laughs and heartfelt moments rather than anything too sharp or subversive. Visually, it’s glossy and clean, the kind of sleek office setting that’s Instagram-ready, which suits the fashion-website backdrop well.

Heads up for those sensitive to animal-related content: the film includes a number of upsetting moments involving pets and other animals, including some deaths, so be heavily warned if that’s on your list. There’s also an incident of sexual assault mentioned, plus some scenes involving bugs and spiders that might catch you off guard. If any of these are triggers for you, approach with caution.
emailReview:
The Intern is a gently charming dramedy with feel-good vibes and a warm, comforting tone, anchored by Robert De Niro’s wise, good-natured performance and Anne Hathaway’s modern hustle.

Be prepared for: multiple pet deaths, a mention of sexual assault, and unsettling scenes involving bugs and spiders.

name: Phone Booth
overview: A slick New York publicist who picks up a ringing receiver in a phone booth is told that if he hangs up, he'll be killed... and the little red light from a laser rifle sight is proof that the caller isn't kidding.
tagline: No options. No lies. No fear. No deals. Just keep talking.

writers: Stephen Chin, Todd Phillips, Jason Smilovic, Guy Lawson
name: War Dogs
overview: Based on the true story of two young men, David Packouz and Efraim Diveroli, who won a $300 million contract from the Pentagon to arm America's allies in Afghanistan.

name: Seven Psychopaths
overview: A struggling screenwriter inadvertently becomes entangled in the Los Angeles criminal underworld after his oddball friends kidnap a gangster's beloved Shih Tzu.
tagline: They won't take any shih tzu.

name: The Invisible Man
overview: When Cecilia's abusive ex takes his own life and leaves her his fortune, she suspects his death was a hoax. As a series of coincidences turn lethal, Cecilia works to prove that she is being hunted by someone nobody can see.
tagline: What you can't see can hurt you.
review:
The Invisible Man (2020) is a tense, modern take on the classic horror trope, blending psychological thriller with high-stakes suspense. Elisabeth Moss delivers a powerhouse performance as Cecilia, whose paranoia and trauma feel raw and immediate, elevating what could have been a standard ghost story into something much more gripping. Fans of films like *Hush* or *Get Out* will appreciate its sharp focus on gaslighting and abuse, while horror buffs will recognize the clever use of invisibility as a metaphor for unseen trauma. It’s not just about scares—though those are plentiful—but about the way trauma invisibly follows you, long after the abuser is gone.

Leigh Whannell’s direction leans heavily into atmosphere, using tight framing and an eerie, almost clinical score to keep viewers on edge. The tagline, “What you can’t see can hurt you,” nails the film’s core tension perfectly. The synopsis hints at an abuser who fakes his own death to continue tormenting Cecilia, and the film never lets you forget how isolating and terrifying that kind of stalking and gaslighting can be. The inclusion of mannequins in both the protagonist’s and antagonist’s homes adds a haunting, surreal touch that amplifies the feeling of being watched and manipulated. Plus, the film’s use of natural settings like the ocean and the Golden Gate Bridge grounds the story in a recognizable reality, contrasting with the supernatural premise.

Those who pin the stalking, gaslighting, and PTSD triggers should be cautious—these themes are front and center and handled with unflinching intensity. The film also contains multiple jump scares, blood and gore, domestic violence, and scenes of choking and struggle to breathe that are quite graphic. Animal lovers should note the presence of a Doberman named Zeus who is sad and abandoned at various points, though he is never harmed and survives the story. There are also some very intense scenes involving restraint, hospitalization, and self-harm that may be difficult for some viewers. Overall, *The Invisible Man* is a well-crafted horror thriller that doesn’t shy away from the darkness lurking within abuse and trauma.
emailReview: The Invisible Man (2020) twists the classic horror trope into a tense psychological thriller, with Elisabeth Moss delivering a powerhouse performance that makes the unseen feel viscerally threatening and emotionally raw. Be prepared for: graphic choking and struggle to breathe, intense scenes of restraint and self-harm, domestic violence, and the haunting presence of mannequins creating an eerie atmosphere.

name: Dirty Dancing
overview: Expecting the usual tedium that accompanies a summer in the Catskills with her family, 17-year-old Frances 'Baby' Houseman is surprised to find herself stepping into the shoes of a professional hoofer—and unexpectedly falling in love.
tagline: First dance. First love. The time of your life.

name: Valkyrie
overview: Wounded in Africa during World War II, Nazi Col. Claus von Stauffenberg returns to his native Germany and joins the Resistance in a daring plan to create a shadow government and assassinate Adolf Hitler. When events unfold so that he becomes a central player, he finds himself tasked with both leading the coup and personally killing the Führer.

writers: Dan O'Bannon, Ronald Shusett, Fede Alvarez, Rodo Sayagues
name: Alien: Romulus
overview: While scavenging the deep ends of a derelict space station, a group of young space colonizers come face to face with the most terrifying life form in the universe.
tagline: In space, no one can hear you.
review:
Alien: Romulus dives back into the claustrophobic, pulse-pounding sci-fi horror that fans of the franchise expect, but with a fresh cast of young space colonizers who stumble upon one of the universe’s most iconic nightmares. Directed by Fede Álvarez, known for upping the tension in horror classics, this 2024 entry feels like Alien meets a gritty survival thriller—lean, tense, and often brutal. It’s not quite the next-level reinvention some might hope for, but it’s a solid addition elevated by a cast that includes Cailee Spaeny and Isabela Merced, who bring a gritty realism to their roles amidst the eerie derelict station.

What stands out most is how the film leans into the eerie atmosphere and suspense rather than just jump scares, playing with the isolating tagline "In space, no one can hear you" to full effect. The writing by Álvarez and Rodo Sayagues keeps things tight, focusing on the dread of what’s lurking rather than over-explaining. The visuals are appropriately grim and claustrophobic, with the derelict space station setting feeling like a character itself—dark, decaying, and full of secrets. There’s a memorable sequence involving a rat that’s both unsettling and crucial to the theme of experimentation and body horror, which adds a fresh layer of discomfort.

Those who pin the animal harm trigger should be cautious here—there’s a particularly graphic scene involving a rat that dies and is then subjected to painful, disturbing procedures. If that’s on your list, be heavily warned. Beyond that, the film hits many of the usual Alien franchise beats, so fans of tense, atmospheric sci-fi horror with a dash of body horror will find plenty to chew on.
emailReview:
Alien: Romulus delivers lean, claustrophobic sci-fi horror with a gritty cast and an eerie, decaying space station that feels like its own menacing character.

Be prepared for: graphic rat death, disturbing animal experimentation, body horror, and intense isolation-driven suspense.

writers: André Bijelic, Vincenzo Natali, Graeme Manson
name: Cube
overview: A group of strangers find themselves trapped in a maze-like prison. It soon becomes clear that each of them possesses the peculiar skills necessary to escape, if they don't wind up dead first.
tagline: Don't look for a reason... Look for a way out.

writers: Patrick Aison, Dan Trachtenberg, Jim Thomas, John Thomas
name: Prey
overview: When danger threatens her camp, the fierce and highly skilled Comanche warrior Naru sets out to protect her people. But the prey she stalks turns out to be a highly evolved alien predator with a technically advanced arsenal.
tagline: They hunt to live. It lives to hunt.
review:
Prey is a thrilling sci-fi action flick that flips the Predator franchise on its head by setting the hunt in 1719 among the Comanche people. Amber Midthunder’s fierce portrayal of Naru, a skilled warrior defending her tribe, grounds this tense cat-and-mouse game with real heart and grit. It’s like Predator meets a period Western, with a fresh cultural lens and a tighter, leaner story that feels both respectful and exciting. If you’ve ever wanted a sci-fi action movie that respects Indigenous voices while delivering pulpy thrills, this one’s a solid pick.

What really stands out here is the way the film balances its high-stakes alien hunt with a deeply felt connection to nature and survival. The tagline, “They hunt to live. It lives to hunt,” nails the primal stakes at play. The visuals lean into the wilderness setting beautifully, with the alien’s technically advanced arsenal contrasting sharply against Naru’s traditional skills and environment. Dan Trachtenberg keeps the pace taut, and the writing by Patrick Aison and Trachtenberg smartly avoids over-explaining, letting tension and atmosphere do the heavy lifting.

One heads-up: animal harm is a significant part of the story’s tension, with multiple animals—dogs, horses, cats, and others—dying or suffering, which could be upsetting for sensitive viewers. Alongside that, spiders, snakes, and bugs make appearances that might trigger arachnophobia or entomophobia. If animal deaths and creepy crawlies are on your watchlist, be heavily warned.
emailReview:
Prey reinvents the Predator saga with a crisp, tense wilderness hunt set in 1719 and anchored by Amber Midthunder’s fierce performance as a Comanche warrior.

Be prepared for: multiple animal deaths including dogs and horses, spider and snake encounters, and unsettling scenes involving bugs.

name: The Fountain
overview: Spanning over one thousand years, and three parallel stories, The Fountain is a story of love, death, spirituality, and the fragility of our existence in this world.

name: Ghost
overview: Sam Wheat is a banker, Molly Jensen is an artist, and the two are madly in love. However, when Sam is murdered by his friend and corrupt business partner Carl Bruner over a shady business deal, he is left to roam the earth as a powerless spirit. When he learns of Carl's betrayal, Sam must seek the help of psychic Oda Mae Brown to set things right and protect Molly from Carl and his goons.
tagline: Before Sam was murdered, he told Molly he'd love and protect her forever.

name: Closer
overview: Two couples disintegrate when they begin destructive adulterous affairs with each other.

writers: Kirk DeMicco, Chris Sanders, John Cleese
name: The Croods
overview: The Croods is a prehistoric comedy adventure that follows the world's first family as they embark on a journey of a lifetime when the cave that has always shielded them from danger is destroyed. Traveling across a spectacular landscape, the Croods discover an incredible new world filled with fantastic creatures -- and their outlook is changed forever.

name: Everest
overview: Inspired by the incredible events surrounding a treacherous attempt to reach the summit of the world's highest mountain, "Everest" documents the awe-inspiring journey of two different expeditions challenged beyond their limits by one of the fiercest snowstorms ever encountered by mankind. Their mettle tested by the harshest of elements found on the planet, the climbers will face nearly impossible obstacles as a lifelong obsession becomes a breathtaking struggle for survival.

name: Shakespeare in Love
overview: Young Shakespeare is forced to stage his latest comedy, "Romeo and Ethel, the Pirate's Daughter," before it's even written. When a lovely noblewoman auditions for a role, they fall into forbidden love -- and his play finds a new life (and title). As their relationship progresses, Shakespeare's comedy soon transforms into tragedy.

name: Rocky Balboa
overview: When he loses a highly publicized virtual boxing match to ex-champ Rocky Balboa, reigning heavyweight titleholder, Mason Dixon retaliates by challenging Rocky to a nationally televised, 10-round exhibition bout. To the surprise of his son and friends, Rocky agrees to come out of retirement and face an opponent who's faster, stronger and thirty years his junior.

writers: George Clooney, Grant Heslov, Beau Willimon
name: The Ides of March
overview: Dirty tricks stand to soil an ambitious young press spokesman's idealism in a cutthroat presidential campaign where 'victory' is relative.

name: Basic Instinct
overview: A police detective is in charge of the investigation of a brutal murder, in which a beautiful and seductive woman could be involved.
tagline: A brutal murder. A brilliant killer. A cop who can't resist the danger.

writers: Eddie Murphy, David Sheffield, Barry W. Blaustein
name: Coming to America
overview: An African prince decides it’s time for him to find a princess... and his mission leads him and his most loyal friend to Queens, New York. In disguise as an impoverished immigrant, the pampered prince quickly finds himself a new job, new friends, new digs, new enemies and lots of trouble.
tagline: This summer, Prince Akeem discovers America.

name: Enchanted
overview: The beautiful princess Giselle is banished by an evil queen from her magical, musical animated land and finds herself in the gritty reality of the streets of modern-day Manhattan. Shocked by this strange new environment that doesn't operate on a "happily ever after" basis, Giselle is now adrift in a chaotic world badly in need of enchantment. But when Giselle begins to fall in love with a charmingly flawed divorce lawyer who has come to her aid - even though she is already promised to a perfect fairy tale prince back home - she has to wonder: Can a storybook view of romance survive in the real world?
tagline: The real world and the animated world collide.

name: American Made
overview: The true story of pilot Barry Seal, who transported contraband for the CIA and the Medellin cartel in the 1980s.
tagline: It's not a felony if you're doing it for the good guys.

writers: Peter Lord, Nick Park, Karey Kirkpatrick, Mark Burton, John O'Farrell
name: Chicken Run
overview: Having been hopelessly repressed and facing eventual certain death at the British chicken farm where they are held, Ginger the chicken along with the help of Rocky the American rooster decide to rebel and lead their fellow chickens in a great escape from the murderous farmers Mr. and Mrs. Tweedy and their farm of doom.
tagline: There's nothing more determined than poultry with a plan.

writers: Mel Brooks, Thomas Meehan, Ronny Graham
name: Spaceballs
overview: When the nefarious Dark Helmet hatches a plan to snatch Princess Vespa and steal her planet's air, space-bum-for-hire Lone Starr and his clueless sidekick fly to the rescue. Along the way, they meet Yogurt, who puts Lone Starr wise to the power of "The Schwartz." Can he master it in time to save the day?
tagline: May the schwartz be with you.
review:
Spaceballs is the kind of goofy sci-fi parody that feels like Mel Brooks riffing on Star Wars with a heavy dose of Saturday morning cartoon silliness. It’s a wild ride of absurd characters and goofy dialogue, anchored by Rick Moranis’s delightfully hammy Dark Helmet and John Candy’s lovable half-man, half-dog sidekick Barf. While it doesn’t quite reach the comedic heights of Brooks’s Blazing Saddles or Young Frankenstein, it’s a pretty standard but enjoyable spoof that fans of 80s comedy and space operas will appreciate for its wink-wink, nudge-nudge humor.

What stands out here is the way the film leans into slapstick and meta-jokes — the tagline “May the schwartz be with you” sets the tone for a movie that’s happy to poke fun at itself and the genre. Mel Brooks’s dual role as both the bumbling President Skroob and wise Yogurt adds a nice layer of ridiculousness, and the concept of “The Schwartz” as a parody of the Force is a clever touch. The writing doesn’t take itself seriously for a second, which is both its charm and its limitation; if you’re after sharp satire, this might feel a bit too broad, but it’s perfect if you just want a silly sci-fi romp.

Heads up if you’re sensitive to animal deaths or gore — Spaceballs has quite a few moments where animals meet unfortunate ends, including dogs, cats, horses, and more. There’s also finger and toe mutilation, sexual assault, and other heavier content tucked beneath the goofy exterior. If you’re keeping an eye on triggers, those who pin animal harm and bodily injury should definitely be cautious going in.
emailReview:
Spaceballs is a goofy sci-fi parody packed with Rick Moranis’s hammy Dark Helmet and John Candy’s lovable half-man, half-dog sidekick, delivering a wild ride of absurd characters and wink-wink humor.

Be prepared for: multiple animal deaths including dogs and horses, finger and toe mutilation, and a surprising touch of sexual assault beneath the silliness.

writers: Jonathan Aibel, Glenn Berger, Ethan Reiff, Cyrus Voris
name: Kung Fu Panda 3
overview: Continuing his "legendary adventures of awesomeness", Po must face two hugely epic, but different threats: one supernatural and the other a little closer to his home.

name: Sing
overview: A koala named Buster recruits his best friend to help him drum up business for his theater by hosting a singing competition.

name: Desperado
overview: El Mariachi plunges headfirst into the dark border underworld when he follows a trail of blood to the last of the infamous Mexican drug lords, Bucho, for an action-packed, bullet-riddled showdown. With the help of his friend and a beautiful bookstore owner, El Mariachi tracks Bucho, takes on his army of desperados, and leaves his own trail of blood.
tagline: He came back to settle the score with someone. Anyone. EVERYONE.

name: The Danish Girl
overview: When Gerda Wegener asks her husband Einar to fill in as a portrait model, Einar discovers the person she's meant to be and begins living her life as Lili Elbe. Having realized her true self and with Gerda's love and support, Lili embarks on a groundbreaking journey as a transgender pioneer.
tagline: Find the courage to be yourself.

name: Melancholia
overview: Two sisters find their already strained relationship challenged as a mysterious new planet threatens to collide with Earth.

name: Side Effects
overview: A woman turns to prescription medication as a way of handling her anxiety concerning her husband's upcoming release from prison.
tagline: One pill can change your life.

writers: Nick Hornby, Peter Hedges, Chris Weitz, Paul Weitz
name: About a Boy
overview: Will Freeman is a hip Londoner who one day realizes that his friends are all involved with the responsibilities of married life, which leaves him alone in the cold. Passing himself off as a single father, he starts to meet a string of single mums, confident in his ability to leave them behind when they start to ask for a commitment. But Will's hope of continued bachelorhood is interrupted when he meets 12-year old Marcus, in many ways his complete opposite.
tagline: Growing up has nothing to do with age.

name: The Master
overview: Freddie, a volatile, heavy-drinking veteran who suffers from post-traumatic stress disorder, finds some semblance of a family when he stumbles onto the ship of Lancaster Dodd, the charismatic leader of a new "religion" he forms after World War II.

writers: Matthew Michael Carnahan, Matthew Sand, David Barstow, David Rohde, Stephanie Saul
name: Deepwater Horizon
overview: A story set on the offshore drilling rig Deepwater Horizon, which exploded during April 2010 and created the worst oil spill in U.S. history.
tagline: When faced with our darkest hour, hope is not a tactic.
review:
Deepwater Horizon is a tense, gripping disaster drama that leans hard into the harrowing true story of the 2010 oil rig explosion and its aftermath. Directed by Peter Berg and anchored by Mark Wahlberg’s steady presence, it fits comfortably alongside other real-life catastrophe movies like Sully or Everest. While it doesn’t reinvent the genre, it delivers enough edge-of-your-seat moments and emotional weight to rise above your typical action-thriller based on a true event.

What stands out here is the film’s unflinching depiction of chaos and heroism in the face of imminent disaster. The tagline, "When faced with our darkest hour, hope is not a tactic," underscores a theme of grit and survival against overwhelming odds. The ensemble cast, including Kurt Russell and John Malkovich, help flesh out the human side of this industrial nightmare, while the visuals and sound design plunge you into the claustrophobic, fiery inferno of the rig itself. It’s a grim reminder of the real lives behind the headlines and environmental catastrophe.

Heads up to those who pin the “someone is burned alive,” “a kid dies,” and “a dog dies” triggers—this movie doesn’t shy away from showing the brutal consequences of the explosion. There are also jump scares, flashing lights, and moments of intense panic that could unsettle sensitive viewers. If you’re looking for a straightforward disaster flick that respects its real-world source material without sugarcoating the trauma, this one fits the bill.
emailReview:
Deepwater Horizon delivers a gripping, unflinching look at heroism amid a fiery disaster, anchored by Mark Wahlberg’s steady presence and intense, immersive visuals that pull you into the chaos.

Be prepared for: someone burned alive, a kid dying, a dog dying, intense panic, and jump scares.

name: Three Kings
overview: A group of American soldiers stationed in Iraq at the end of the Gulf War find a map they believe will take them to a huge cache of stolen Kuwaiti gold hidden near their base, and they embark on a secret mission that's destined to change everything.
review:
Three Kings is a war adventure with a sharp satirical edge—part treasure hunt, part dark comedy, part political commentary—set against the chaotic backdrop of the Gulf War’s aftermath. David O. Russell’s 1999 film stands out from typical war movies by blending slick action with biting humor and moral ambiguity, making it feel like Ocean’s Eleven meets Full Metal Jacket. George Clooney, Mark Wahlberg, and Ice Cube lead a charismatic cast that balances bravado with vulnerability, giving the film a kinetic energy that keeps it engaging even as it questions the glory and cost of war.

The film’s tagline, “It’s good to be king,” hints at the power dynamics and greed that drive the story, and the plot’s premise—a secret mission to find stolen Kuwaiti gold—sets up a narrative that’s as much about personal survival and camaraderie as it is about political critique. The writing by Russell and John Ridley layers sharp dialogue and memorable set pieces with moments of genuine emotional weight, all underscored by a stylish visual approach that captures the desert landscape’s harsh beauty and the absurdity of the soldiers’ situation. It’s a film that doesn’t just lean into genre conventions—it twists them, offering both thrills and thoughtful reflection.

Heads-up for animal lovers: Three Kings features several distressing scenes involving animals, including dog fighting, animal abuse, and the deaths of a dog and a horse. If those are triggers on your list, be cautious—these elements are quite prominent and hard to overlook amid the film’s broader chaos.
emailReview:
Three Kings is a sharp satirical war adventure that blends slick action with biting humor and moral complexity, anchored by charismatic performances from George Clooney, Mark Wahlberg, and Ice Cube.

Be prepared for: dog fighting, animal abuse, the deaths of a dog and a horse, and the gritty realities of wartime violence.

name: Sicario: Day of the Soldado
overview: Agent Matt Graver teams up with operative Alejandro Gillick to prevent Mexican drug cartels from smuggling terrorists across the United States border.
tagline: Some missions need a hitman...others need a soldier.

name: Definitely, Maybe
overview: When Will decides to tell his daughter the story of how he met her mother, he discovers that a second look at the past might also give him a second chance at the future.

name: Allied
overview: In 1942, an intelligence officer in North Africa encounters a female French Resistance fighter on a deadly mission behind enemy lines. When they reunite in London, their relationship is tested by the pressures of war.

name: Four Weddings and a Funeral
overview: Over the course of five social occasions, a committed bachelor must consider the notion that he may have discovered love.
tagline: Five good reasons to stay single.
review:
Four Weddings and a Funeral is the quintessential 90s British rom-com that’s as charming as it is sharp-witted. If you’re into Richard Curtis’s brand of humor—think Love Actually with a bit more heart and less holiday chaos—you’ll find plenty to love here. Hugh Grant’s lovably awkward Charles anchors the film with his bumbling bachelor vibe, while Andie MacDowell’s Carrie brings a breezy American sensibility that spices up the classic “will they or won’t they” dance. It’s a movie that feels like a warm hug from a friend who’s just as cynical about love as they are hopeful.

What really sets this film apart is how it balances the highs of weddings—joyful, chaotic, and full of awkward encounters—with the sober, poignant moments of loss and reflection hinted at in the title’s “funeral.” The writing sparkles with clever dialogue and memorable one-liners, and the ensemble cast, including Kristin Scott Thomas and John Hannah, rounds out a believable group of friends whose lives intertwine in ways both funny and bittersweet. Director Mike Newell keeps the tone buoyant without glossing over the emotional stakes, making the tagline “Five good reasons to stay single” feel playfully ironic rather than cynical.

Heads up if you’re sensitive to animal-related content: the film contains multiple scenes involving the death or distress of various animals, including dogs, horses, and cats, which might catch you off guard. Those who pin the “animal dies” or “animals abused” triggers should be cautious going in, as these moments are woven into the story’s quieter, more somber beats. Otherwise, Four Weddings and a Funeral remains a delightful, if occasionally tear-jerking, romp through love’s unpredictable terrain.
emailReview:
Four Weddings and a Funeral charms with its sharp wit, heartfelt moments, and Hugh Grant’s perfectly awkward lead performance that balances joy and sorrow in a distinctly British rom-com style.

Be prepared for: multiple scenes of animal deaths and distress involving dogs, horses, and cats, as well as moments of quiet emotional grief.

primaryTitle: Bad Times at the El Royale
Title_IMDb_Link: Bad Times at the El Royale
name: Bad Times At El Royale
overview: Lake Tahoe, 1969. Seven strangers, each one with a secret to bury, meet at El Royale, a decadent motel with a dark past. In the course of a fateful night, everyone will have one last shot at redemption.
tagline: Seven strangers. Seven secrets. All roads lead here.
review:
Bad Times at the El Royale is a slick, stylish neo-noir thriller that feels like a Tarantino flick crashing into a ’60s motel soap opera. Drew Goddard’s direction leans heavily into mood and mystery, with a twisty plot that keeps you guessing about the true nature of each of the seven strangers. It’s not quite as sharp or memorable as some of the better ensemble thrillers in recent years, but it’s elevated by strong performances—Jeff Bridges and Cynthia Erivo especially stand out—and a pulsing, retro soundtrack that perfectly nails the era.

What sticks with you is the way the film slowly unpacks its characters’ dark pasts, weaving in themes of redemption and deception under the shadow of a creepy, almost haunted motel. The tagline “Seven strangers. Seven secrets. All roads lead here.” is spot-on—the motel itself almost feels like a character, steeped in decay and danger. The mix of psychological games, violence, and moments of eerie calm keeps the tone uneven but fascinating, even if the pacing stumbles a bit in the middle.

Heads up for those sensitive to animal-related content: this one is stuffed with multiple instances of animal harm and death, including dogs, cats, and horses. If the idea of animal abuse or death is a big red flag for you, this film will be tough to sit through. Also, there are plenty of creepy crawlies—bugs, spiders, and snakes make appearances—so if you’re on edge about critters, consider yourself warned.
emailReview:
Bad Times at the El Royale is a slick neo-noir thriller with strong performances from Jeff Bridges and Cynthia Erivo, wrapped in a moody, twisty plot set in a hauntingly atmospheric ’60s motel.

Be prepared for: multiple instances of animal harm including dogs, cats, and horses, unsettling insects like bugs and spiders, and tense psychological violence.

name: Spy Game
overview: On the day of his retirement, a veteran CIA agent learns that his former protégé has been arrested in China, is sentenced to die the next morning in Beijing, and that the CIA is considering letting that happen to avoid an international scandal.
tagline: It's not how you play the game. It's how the game plays you.

name: Escape from New York
altName: john carpenter’s escape from new york
overview: In a world ravaged by crime, the entire island of Manhattan has been converted into a walled prison where brutal prisoners roam free. After the US president crash-lands inside, war hero Snake Plissken has 24 hours to bring him back.
tagline: 1997. New York City is a walled, maximum security prison. Breaking out is impossible. Breaking in is insane.

writers: Juel Taylor, Sylvester Stallone, Sascha Penn, Cheo Hodari Coker, Steven Caple Jr.

overview: Between personal obligations and training for his next big fight against an opponent with ties to his family's past, Adonis Creed is up against the challenge of his life.
tagline: There's more to lose than a title.

name: State of Play
overview: Handsome, unflappable U.S. Congressman Stephen Collins is the future of his political party: an honorable appointee who serves as the chairman of a committee overseeing defense spending. All eyes are upon the rising star to be his party's contender for the upcoming presidential race. Until his research assistant/mistress is brutally murdered and buried secrets come tumbling out.

name: Love, Rosie
overview: Since the moment they met at age 5, Rosie and Alex have been best friends, facing the highs and lows of growing up side by side. A fleeting shared moment, one missed opportunity, and the decisions that follow send their lives in completely different directions. As each navigates the complexities of life, love, and everything in between, they always find their way back to each other - but is it just friendship, or something more?  Based on Cecelia Ahern's bestselling novel, LOVE, ROSIE is a heart-warming, modern comedy-of-errors posing the ultimate question: do we really only get one shot at true love?

writers: David Benioff, Susanne Bier, Anders Thomas Jensen
name: Brothers
overview: When his helicopter goes down during his fourth tour of duty in Afghanistan, Marine Sam Cahill is presumed dead. Back home, brother Tommy  steps in to look over Sam’s wife, Grace, and two children. Sam’s surprise homecoming triggers domestic mayhem.
tagline: There are two sides to every family.

writers: Antonio Campos, Paulo Campos, Donald Ray Pollock
name: The Devil All the Time
overview: In the 1960s after World War II in Southern Ohio, bizarre, compelling and mentally disturbed people suffer from the war's psychological damages.
tagline: Everyone ends up in the same damned place.

name: Seven Years in Tibet
overview: Austrian mountaineer, Heinrich Harrer journeys to the Himalayas without his family to head an expedition in 1939. But when World War II breaks out, the arrogant Harrer falls into Allied forces' hands as a prisoner of war. He escapes with a fellow detainee and makes his way to Llaso, Tibet, where he meets the 14-year-old Dalai Lama, whose friendship ultimately transforms his outlook on life.

name: The Time Travelers Wife
overview: Due to a genetic disorder, handsome librarian Henry DeTamble involuntarily zips through time, appearing at various moments in the life of his true love, the beautiful artist Clare Abshire.

name: Remember Me
overview: Still reeling from a heartbreaking family event and his parents' subsequent divorce, Tyler Hawkins discovers a fresh lease on life when he meets Ally Craig, a gregarious beauty who witnessed her mother's death. But as the couple draws closer, the fallout from their separate tragedies jeopardizes their love.

writers: Clayton Frohman, Edward Zwick, Nechama Tec
name: Defiance
overview: Based on a true story, during World War II, four Jewish brothers escape their Nazi-occupied homeland of West Belarus in Poland and join the Soviet partisans to combat the Nazis. The brothers begin the rescue of roughly 1,200 Jews still trapped in the ghettos of Poland.
tagline: Freedom begins with an act of defiance

name: Never Let Me Go
overview: As children, Kathy, Ruth, and Tommy spend their childhood at an idyllic and secluded English boarding school. As they grow into adults, they must come to terms with the complexity and strength of their love for one another while also preparing for the haunting reality awaiting them.
tagline: These students have everything they need. Except time.

overview: 17 year-old Ree Dolly sets out to track down her father, who put their house up for his bail bond and then disappeared. If she fails, Ree and her family will be turned out into the Ozark woods. Challenging her outlaw kin's code of silence and risking her life, Ree hacks through the lies, evasions and threats offered up by her relatives and begins to piece together the truth.

name: Margin Call
overview: A thriller that revolves around the key people at an investment bank over a 24-hour period during the early stages of the financial crisis.
tagline: Be first. Be smarter. Or cheat.

name: It's Kind of a Funny Story

tagline: Get ready to root for the bad guy.

tagline: Give a father no options and you leave him no choice.

tagline: Based on the inspirational best seller.

overview:
South Korean monster film, directed and co-written by Bong Joon Ho.

A teenage girl is captured by a giant mutated squid-like creature that appears from Seoul's Han River after toxic waste was dumped in it, prompting her family into a frantic search for her.
tagline: Man has made his newest predator.

name: The Dreamers
overview: A young American studying in Paris in 1968 strikes up a friendship with a French brother and sister.

name: T2 Trainspotting
overview: After 20 years abroad, Mark Renton returns to Scotland and reunites with his old friends Sick Boy, Spud and Begbie.
tagline: Face your past. Choose your future.
