name: The Hand That Rocks the Cradle
overview: A suburban family chooses seemingly sweet Peyton Flanders as their newborn's nanny. Only much later does the infant's mother, Claire Bartel, realize Peyton's true intentions -- to destroy Claire and replace her in the family. The nail-biting suspense builds quickly in this chilling psychological thriller about deception and bitter revenge.
tagline: Trust is her weapon. Innocence her opportunity. Revenge her only desire.
review:
The Hand That Rocks the Cradle is a quintessential early '90s psychological thriller that still manages to keep you on edge. With its suburban setting and creeping sense of dread, it feels like a precursor to the wave of nanny-centric thrillers that followed, but with a sharper edge. Rebecca De Mornay’s chilling turn as Peyton Flanders—who’s equal parts sweet and sinister—anchors the film, making it more than just a standard domestic suspense flick. If you like your thrillers with a dose of creeping paranoia and a villain you love to hate, this one’s a solid pick.

The film’s tagline—“Trust is her weapon. Innocence her opportunity. Revenge her only desire.”—perfectly sums up the core tension. Curtis Hanson’s direction leans into the slow burn of Peyton’s infiltration into the Bartel family, building a tight, claustrophobic atmosphere. The writing by Amanda Silver does a nice job of balancing the thriller elements with moments that feel genuinely unsettling rather than just jump-scare fodder. Plus, the performances from Annabella Sciorra and Julianne Moore add depth to what could have been a pretty straightforward “crazy nanny” story. It’s the kind of movie that plays on fears of betrayal and invasion of the domestic sphere, which still resonates today.

Trigger-wise, be warned if animal harm or death is on your list—this one includes multiple upsetting scenes involving pets and other animals, which could be a real gut punch. There’s also some gaslighting and general psychological abuse that ramps up the tension, so if you’re sensitive to those themes, proceed with caution. The combination of these triggers adds a darker layer beneath the film’s glossy suburban surface.
emailReview:
A slow-burning psychological thriller with a chilling performance from Rebecca De Mornay, The Hand That Rocks the Cradle turns the nanny trope into a masterclass in creeping dread and domestic paranoia.

Be prepared for: multiple scenes of animal harm, psychological abuse, gaslighting, and a pervasive sense of betrayal that cuts deep.

name: Nothing to Lose
overview: Advertising executive Nick Beame learns that his wife is sleeping with his employer. In a state of despair, he encounters a bumbling thief whose attempted carjacking goes awry when Nick takes him on an involuntary joyride. Soon the betrayed businessman and the incompetent crook strike up a partnership and develop a robbery-revenge scheme. But it turns out that some other criminals in the area don't appreciate the competition.

name: The Old Man & the Gun
overview: The true story of Forrest Tucker, from his audacious escape from San Quentin at the age of 70 to an unprecedented string of heists that confounded authorities and enchanted the public. Wrapped up in the pursuit are a detective, who becomes captivated with Forrest’s commitment to his craft, and a woman, who loves him in spite of his chosen profession.

name: Ju-On: the Grudge
overview: A mysterious and vengeful spirit marks and pursues anybody who dares enter the house in which it resides.
tagline: When a grudge from the dead passes to the living, who is safe?
review:
Ju-On: The Grudge is a classic of Japanese horror that set the bar for supernatural curse stories in the early 2000s. It’s a grim, unsettling ghost tale where the dread doesn’t just come from jump scares but a creeping sense of inevitable doom once you cross into the haunted house. If you’re a fan of the slow-burn, atmospheric horror that made The Ring famous, this one’s right up your alley—though it leans heavily into a fragmented narrative structure that can be as disorienting as it is chilling.

Takashi Shimizu’s direction plays masterfully with silence and sudden bursts of terror, crafting a mood that sticks with you long after the credits roll. The story’s simple but effective: a malevolent spirit curses anyone who enters the house, and the ripple effects on various characters unfold in a non-linear way. The cast, including Megumi Okina and Misa Uehara, help ground the eerie proceedings with believable performances, but it’s really the atmosphere and the design of the ghostly apparitions that make this film memorable. The tagline, “When a grudge from the dead passes to the living, who is safe?” nails that inescapable tension.

Heads up to animal lovers and anyone sensitive to animal harm triggers: Ju-On features several distressing scenes involving animals, including dog fighting and abuse, which are integral to the story’s dark, cursed world. Those who pin animal harm should be cautious going in, as these moments are unsettling and can be hard to watch.
emailReview:
Ju-On: The Grudge is a masterclass in slow-building dread, blending eerie silence with sudden jolts to create a haunting atmosphere that lingers well beyond the final scene.

Be prepared for: dog fighting, animal abuse, intense supernatural menace, and a creeping sense of inevitable doom.

name: Saved
overview: Teenage Mary Cummings, who has "been Born Again her whole life," is about to enter her senior year at American Eagle Christian High School near Baltimore with her Fundamentalist Christian friends Hilary Faye and Veronica, the three of whom have formed a girl group called the Christian Jewels. Everything seems perfect—until Mary’s "perfect Christian boyfriend" Dean tells her, as they’re swimming underwater, that he thinks he's gay.

name: Company Men
overview: Bobby Walker lives the proverbial American dream: great job, beautiful family, shiny Porsche in the garage. When corporate downsizing leaves him and two co-workers jobless, the three men are forced to re-define their lives as men, husbands and fathers.

name: Tolkien
overview: England, early 20th century. The future writer and philologist John Ronald Reuel Tolkien (1892-1973) and three of his schoolmates create a strong bond between them as they share the same passion for literature and art, a true fellowship that strengthens as they grow up, but the outbreak of World War I threatens to shatter it.
tagline: A life of love, courage & fellowship.

writers: Jim Cox, Karey Kirkpatrick, Byron Simpson, Joe Ranft, Margery Sharp
name: The Rescuers Down Under
overview: A lawless poacher wants to capture a majestic and rare golden eagle, so he kidnaps the boy who knows where to find the bird. Not to worry -- the Rescue Aid Society's top agents, heroic mice Miss Bianca and Bernard, fly to Australia to save the day. Accompanying the fearless duo are bumbling albatross Wilbur and local field operative Jake the Kangaroo Rat.
tagline: Hang on for the most thrilling ride of your life!

directors: François Simard, Anouk Whissell, Yoann-Karl Whissell
name: Summer of 84
overview: Summer is usually a time for fun and games, but some teens get much more danger than they bargained for after beginning to suspect their neighbor is a serial murderer.
tagline: Every serial killer lives next door to someone

directors: Don Bluth, Gary Goldman, Dan Kuenster
writers: Don Bluth, Ken Cromar, Gary Goldman, Larry Leker, Linda Miller, Monica Parker, John Pomeroy, Guy Shulman, David J. Steinberg, David N. Weiss
name: All Dogs Go to Heaven
overview: When a casino owning dog named Charlie is murdered by his rival Carface, he finds himself in Heaven basically by default since all dogs go to heaven. However, since he wants to get back at his killer, he cons his way back to the living with the warning that doing that damns him to Hell. Once back, he teams with his old partner, Itchy to prep his retaliation. He also stumbles on to an orphan girl who can talk to the animals, thus allowing him to get the inside info on the races to ensure his wins to finance his plans. However, all the while, he is still haunted by nightmares on what's waiting for him on the other side unless he can prove that he is worthy of Heaven again.
tagline: But not all dogs stay there!
review:
All Dogs Go to Heaven is that Don Bluth classic that straddles the line between dark and charming in a way few animated films dare. At first glance, it feels like a blend of 1930s gangster flick meets a bittersweet fairy tale, with Burt Reynolds lending his gruff charisma to Charlie, the roguish canine antihero. It’s not your typical feel-good dog movie — it’s got edge, a moral complexity, and a surprisingly heavy dose of existential dread for a cartoon about dogs. Fans of more traditional family animations might find it a little rougher around the edges, but those who appreciate a story willing to get a little grim will dig it.

What really sticks with you is how the film doesn’t shy away from darker themes — from Charlie’s murder and resurrection to the gambling underworld and the looming threat of damnation. The writing balances sharp, witty dialogue with moments of genuine emotional weight, especially through Charlie’s relationship with Anne-Marie, the orphan girl who can talk to animals. The visuals and music capture that late-80s animation vibe with a moody palette and a jazzy score that perfectly matches the smoky, shadowy casino atmosphere. The tagline “But not all dogs stay there!” hints at the film’s take on redemption and the afterlife, which feels surprisingly mature and unsettling for its audience.

Heads up: this one’s heavy on triggers like animal abuse, child abuse, and gun violence, not to mention some pretty intense scenes involving drowning and death. Substance use — cigars, alcohol, and gambling addiction — is portrayed throughout, painting a world that’s rougher and less sanitized than most animated fare. Those who pin the dog death and animal abuse triggers should be especially cautious, as the film includes some genuinely upsetting moments that linger long after the credits roll.
emailReview:
All Dogs Go to Heaven blends 1930s gangster grit with bittersweet fairy tale charm, anchored by Burt Reynolds’ gruff turn as a canine antihero navigating a smoky, shadowy underworld.

Be prepared for: dog death, animal abuse, child abuse, gun violence, and drowning scenes.

name: Oddity
overview: After the brutal murder of her twin sister, Darcy goes after those responsible by using haunted items as her tools for revenge.

name: The Last Starfighter
overview: A video game expert Alex Rogan finds himself transported to another planet after conquering The Last Starfighter video game only to find out it was just a test. He was recruited to join the team of best Starfighters to defend their world from the attack.
tagline: Alex Rogan was a small town boy with big dreams. But in his wildest dreams, he never suspected that tonight he would become The Last Starfighter.

name: The Vast of Night
overview: At the dawn of the space-race, two radio-obsessed teens discover a strange frequency over the airwaves in what becomes the most important night of their lives and in the history of their small town.

name: Rumble in the Bronx
overview: Keong comes from Hong Kong to visit New York for his uncle's wedding. His uncle runs a market in the Bronx and Keong offers to help out while Uncle is on his honeymoon. During his stay in the Bronx, Keong befriends a neighbor kid and beats up some neighborhood thugs who cause problems at the market. One of those petty thugs in the local gang stumbles into a criminal situation way over his head.
tagline: No Fear. No Stuntman. No Equal.

writers: Francis Annan, L.H. Adams, Tim Jenkin, Karol Griffiths
name: Escape from Pretoria
overview: South Africa, 1978. Tim Jenkin and Stephen Lee, two white political activists from the African National Congress imprisoned by the apartheid regime, put a plan in motion to escape from the infamous Pretoria Prison…

writers: John A. Russo, George A. Romero
name: Night of the Living Dead
overview: In this remake of the original classic film, a group of people are trapped inside a farmhouse as legions of the walking dead try to get inside and use them for food.
tagline: There IS a fate worse than death.

name: The Stanford Prison Experiment
overview: This film is based on the actual events that took place in 1971 when Stanford professor Dr. Philip Zimbardo created what became one of the most shocking and famous social experiments of all time.

writers: Theodore Simonson, Kay Linaker, Irvine H. Millgate, Chuck Russell, Frank Darabont
name: The Blob
overview: Remake of the 1958 horror sci-fi about a deadly blob which is the spawn of a secret government germ warfare project which consumes everyone in its path. Teenagers try in vain to warn the townsfolk, who refuse to take them seriously, while government agents try to cover up the evidence and confine the creature.

name: Sea of Love
overview: Seen-it-all New York detective Frank Keller is unsettled - he has done twenty years on the force and could retire, and he hasn't come to terms with his wife leaving him for a colleague. Joining up with an officer from another part of town to investigate a series of murders linked by the lonely hearts columns he finds he is getting seriously and possibly dangerously involved with Helen, one of the main suspects.

writers: Reggie Rock Bythewood, Cheo Hodari Coker
name: Notorious
overview: NOTORIOUS is the story of Christopher Wallace. Through raw talent and sheer determination, Wallace transforms himself from Brooklyn street hustler (once selling crack to pregnant women) to one of the greatest rappers of all time; THE NOTORIOUS B.I.G. Follow his meteoric rise to fame and his refusal to succumb to expectations - redefining our notion of "The American Dream."

name: Inside
overview: Four months after the death of her husband, a woman on the brink of motherhood is tormented in her home by a strange woman who wants her unborn baby.

name: Marrowbone
overview: A young man and his three younger siblings are plagued by a sinister presence in the sprawling manor in which they live.
tagline: No one will ever separate us.

name: Dead Calm
overview: An Australian couple take a sailing trip in the Pacific to forget about a terrible accident. While on the open sea, in dead calm, they come across a ship with one survivor who is not at all what he seems.
tagline: High seas. Deep terror. Try to stay calm.

name: The Skeleton Twins
overview: Estranged twins Maggie and Milo coincidentally cheat death on the same day, prompting them to reunite and confront the reasons their lives went so wrong. As the twins' reunion reinvigorates them, they realize the key to fixing their lives may just lie in repairing their relationship.

name: Weird: The Al Yankovic Story
overview: Exploring every facet of ‘Weird Al’ Yankovic’s life, from his meteoric rise to fame with early hits like ‘Eat It’ and ‘Like a Surgeon’ to his torrid celebrity love affairs and famously depraved lifestyle, this biopic takes audiences on a truly unbelievable journey through Yankovic’s life and career, from gifted child prodigy to the greatest musical legend of all time.
tagline: The world belongs to the weird.

name: The Salvation
overview: In 1870s America, a peaceful American settler kills his family's murderer which unleashes the fury of a notorious gang leader. His cowardly fellow townspeople then betray him, forcing him to hunt down the outlaws alone.

writers: Nick Evans, Eric Roth, Richard LaGravenese
name: The Horse Whisperer
overview: Based on the novel by the same name from Nicholas Evans, the talented Robert Redford presents this meditative family drama set in the country side. Redford not only directs but also stars in the roll of a cowboy with a magical talent for healing.

name: Repo Man
overview: A down and out young punk gets a job working with a seasoned repo man, but what awaits him in his new career is a series of outlandish adventures revolving around aliens, the CIA, and a most wanted '64 Chevy.
tagline: It’s 4 a.m. Do you know where your car is?

name: Drop Dead Gorgeous
overview: In a small Minnesota town, the annual beauty pageant is being covered by a TV crew. Former winner Gladys Leeman wants to make sure her daughter follows in her footsteps; explosions, falling lights, and trailer fires prove that. As the Leemans are the richest family in town, the police are pretty relaxed about it all. Despite everything, main rival (but sweet) Amber Atkins won't give up without a fight.
tagline: The battle between the good and the bad is about to get ugly.

name: Camp X-Ray
overview: A young woman joins the military to be part of something bigger than herself and her small-town roots. Instead, she ends up as a new guard at Guantanamo Bay, where her mission is far from black and white. Surrounded by hostile jihadists and aggressive squadmates, she strikes up an unusual friendship with one of the detainees.

name: Freaks
overview: Kept locked inside the house by her father, 7-year-old Chloe lives in fear and fascination of the outside world, where Abnormals create a constant threat—or so she believes. When a mysterious stranger offers her a glimpse of what's really happening outside, Chloe soon finds that while the truth isn't so simple, the danger is very real.

name: Apt Pupil
overview: One day in 1984, Todd Bowden, a brilliant high school boy fascinated by the history of Nazism, stumbles across an old man whose appearance resembles that of Kurt Dussander, a wanted Nazi war criminal. A month later, Todd decides to knock on his door.
tagline: If you don't believe in the existence of evil, you've got a lot to learn

name: Summer of Sam
overview: Spike Lee's take on the "Son of Sam" murders in New York City during the summer of 1977 centering on the residents of an Italian-American South Bronx neighborhood who live in fear and distrust of one another.

While peering through the beautiful home's telescope one night, he spies a gorgeous blonde dancing in her window. But when he witnesses the girl's murder, it leads Scully through the netherworld of the adult entertainment industry on a search for answers -- with porn actress Holly Body as his guide.

overview: Nazi skinheads in Melbourne take out their anger on local Vietnamese, who are seen as threatening racial purity. Finally the Vietnamese have had enough and confront the skinheads in an all-out confrontation, sending the skinheads running. A woman who is prone to epileptic seizures joins the skins' merry band, and helps them on their run from justice, but is her affliction also a sign of impurity?

overview: A mentally disturbed man takes residence in a halfway house. His mind gradually slips back into the realm created by his illness, where he replays a key part of his childhood.
tagline: The only thing worse than losing your mind... is finding it again.

writers: Will De Los Santos, Creighton Vero
name: Spun
overview: Over the course of three days Ross, a college dropout addicted to crystal-meth, encounters a variety of oddball folks - including a stripper named Nikki and her boyfriend, the local meth producer, The Cook - but all he really wants to do is hook up with his old girlfriend, Amy.

name: Small Time Crooks
overview: A loser of a crook and his wife strike it rich when a botched bank job's cover business becomes a spectacular success.

name: Liberal Arts
overview: Newly single, 35, and uninspired by his job, Jesse Fisher worries that his best days are behind him. But no matter how much he buries his head in a book, life keeps pulling Jesse back. When his favorite college professor invites him to campus to speak at his retirement dinner, Jesse jumps at the chance. He is prepared for the nostalgia of the dining halls and dorm rooms, the parties and poetry seminars; what he doesn’t see coming is Zibby – a beautiful, precocious, classical-music-loving sophomore. Zibby awakens scary, exciting, long-dormant feelings of possibility and connection that Jesse thought he had buried forever.

writers: Anna Leonowens, Steve Meerson, Peter Krikes
name: Anna and the King
overview: The story of the romance between the King of Siam (now Thailand) and the widowed British school teacher Anna Leonowens during the 1860s. Anna teaches the children and becomes romanced by the King. She convinces him that a man can be loved by just one woman.

name: Young & Beautiful
overview: Isabelle, a 17-year-old student, loses her virginity during a quick holiday romance. When she returns home, she begins a secret life as a prostitute for a year.

name: Housebound
overview: When Kylie Bucknell is sentenced to home detention, she's forced to come to terms with her unsociable behaviour, her blabbering mother and a hostile spirit who seems less than happy about the new living arrangement.

writers: Nick Damici, Jim Mickle, Joe R. Lansdale
name: Cold In July
overview: While investigating noises in his house one balmy Texas night in 1989, Richard Dane puts a bullet in the brain of a low-life burglar. Although he’s hailed as a small-town hero, Dane soon finds himself fearing for his family’s safety when Freddy’s ex-con father rolls into town, hell-bent on revenge.
tagline: How many men can one bullet kill?

name: Mermaids
overview: Fifteen-year-old Charlotte Flax is tired of her wacky mom moving their family to a different town any time she feels it is necessary. When they move to a small Massachusetts town and Mrs. Flax begins dating a shopkeeper, Charlotte and her 9-year-old sister, Kate, hope that they can finally settle down. But when Charlotte's attraction to an older man gets in the way, the family must learn to accept each other for who they truly are.

name: Los ojos de Julia
overview: The story of a woman who is slowly losing her sight whilst trying to investigate the mysterious death of her twin sister.

writers: Steven Kampmann, William Porter, PJ Torokvei, Harold Ramis, Rodney Dangerfield, Greg Fields, Dennis Snee
name: Back to School
overview: Self-made millionaire Thornton Melon decides to get a better education and enrolls at his son Jason's college. While Jason tries to fit in with his fellow students, Thornton struggles to gain his son's respect, giving way to hilarious antics.

writers: Robert Mark Kamen, Mark Miller, Harvey Weitzman, Piero Tellini, Cesare Zavattini, Vittorio de Benedetti
name: A Walk in the Clouds
overview: World War II vet Paul Sutton falls for a pregnant and unwed woman who persuades him -- during their first encounter -- to pose as her husband so she can face her family.

writers: Lowell Ganz, Babaloo Mandel, Billie Letts
name: Where the Heart Is
overview: Novalee Nation is a 17-year-old Tennessee transient who has to grow up in a hurry when she's left pregnant and abandoned by her boyfriend on a roadside in Sequoyah, Okla., and takes refuge in the friendly aisles of Wal-Mart. In short order, some eccentric, kindly strangers "adopt" Novalee and her infant daughter, helping them buck the odds and build a new life.

name: Let Him Go
overview: A retired sheriff and his wife fight to rescue their grandson from a dangerous off-grid family upon the death of their son.

writers: Kôji Suzuki, Yoshihiro Nakamura, Ken'ichi Suzuki, Takashige Ichise, Hideo Nakata
name: Dark Water
overview: A woman in the midst of an unpleasant divorce moves to an eerie apartment building with her young daughter. The ceiling of their apartment has a dark and active leak.

name: Sharper
overview: A small, wealthy family in New York City gets progressively torn apart by secrets, lies, and the theft that orchestrates all of it.

name: The Tender Bar
overview: A young boy is seeking a replacement for his father, a New York City disc jockey who had vanished before his son spoke his first word. When he can’t find his father’s voice on the radio anymore, the boy turns in desperation to the bar on the corner, where he finds friendship from his Uncle Charlie and other adults, who take him to the beach, to ballgames, and ultimately into their circle.

name: Regarding Henry
overview: After being shot, a lawyer loses his memory and must relearn speech and mobility, but he has a loving family to support him.

name: L.A. Story
overview: With the help of a talking freeway billboard, a "wacky weatherman" tries to win the heart of an English newspaper reporter, who is struggling to make sense of the strange world of early-90s Los Angeles.

name: The Idiots
overview: With his first Dogma-95 film director Lars von Trier opens up a completely new film platform. With a mix of home-video and documentary styles the film tells the story of a group of young people who have decided to get to know their “inner-idiots” and thus not only facing and breaking their outer appearance but also their inner.

name: Metal Lords
overview: Follows two kids who want to start a heavy metal band in a high school, where only two people care about heavy metal, they also find a girl who is very good at cello. The three of them decide to settle their differences and work together, so they can win the Battle of the Bands.

name: Cronos
overview: Faced with his own mortality, an ingenious alchemist tried to perfect an invention that would provide him with the key to eternal life. It was called the Cronos device. When he died more than 400 years later, he took the secrets of this remarkable device to the grave with him. Now, an elderly antiques dealer has found the hellish machine hidden in a statue and learns about its incredible powers. The more he uses the device, the younger he becomes...but nothing comes without a price. Life after death is just the beginning as this nerve-shattering thriller unfolds and the fountain of youth turns bloody.

name: Celeste & Jesse Forever
overview: Celeste and Jesse met in high school and got married young. They laugh at the same jokes and finish each other’s sentences. They are forever linked in their friends’ minds as the perfect couple – she, a high-powered businesswoman and budding novelist; he, a free spirit who keeps things from getting boring. Their only problem is that they have decided to get divorced. Can their perfect relationship withstand this minor setback?

writers: Chad Kultgen, Jason Reitman, Erin Cressida Wilson
name: Men, Women & Children
overview: Follows the story of a group of high school teenagers and their parents as they attempt to navigate the many ways the internet has changed their relationships, their communication, their self-image, and their love lives.

name: Singles
overview: Romantic comedy about six of Seattle's young people, most of whom live in the same apartment building and whose lives revolve around the city's ever-expanding music scene. The interrelated stories about each character's progress through the singles scene are intriguing and often very funny, and the soundtrack is a grunge fanatic's dream, with the likes of Soundgarden, Pearl Jam and Mudhoney.

name: Harriet
overview: The extraordinary tale of Harriet Tubman's escape from slavery and transformation into one of America's greatest heroes. Her courage, ingenuity and tenacity freed hundreds of slaves and changed the course of history.

name: The Red Sea Diving Resort
overview: Sudan, East Africa, 1980. A team of Israeli Mossad agents plans to rescue and transfer thousands of Ethiopian Jews to Israel. To do so, and to avoid raising suspicions from the inquisitive and ruthless authorities, they establish as a cover a fake diving resort by the Red Sea.
tagline: In the 1980s one partnership saved thousands of lives

name: Powder
overview: Harassed by classmates who won't accept his shocking appearance, a shy young man known as "Powder" struggles to fit in. But the cruel taunts stop when Powder displays a mysterious power that allows him to do incredible things. This phenomenon changes the lives of all those around him in ways they never could have imagined.

writers: Jalmari Helander, Juuso Helander, Petri Jokiranta, Sami Parkkinen
name: Rare Exports: a Christmas Tale
overview: It's the eve of Christmas in northern Finland and an archaeological dig has just unearthed the real Santa Claus. But this particular Santa isn't the one you want coming to town. When all the local children begin mysteriously disappearing, young Pietari and his father Rauno, a reindeer hunter by trade, capture the mythological being and attempt to sell Santa to the misguided leader of the multinational corporation sponsoring the dig. Santa's elves, however, will stop at nothing to free their fearless leader from captivity.
tagline: This Christmas everyone will believe in Santa Claus

writers: Stephen Dyer, Jonah Lisa Dyer, Howard Gensler
name: Hysteria
overview: Two doctors in Victorian England use manual stimulation of female genitalia to cure their patients' ills, leading to the invention of the vibrator.

name: The Lady in the Van
overview: The true story of the relationship between Alan Bennett and the singular Miss Shepherd, a woman of uncertain origins who ‘temporarily’ parked her van in Bennett’s London driveway and proceeded to live there for 15 years.

name: Psycho II
overview: Norman Bates is declared sane and released from the facility in which he was being held, despite the complaints of Lila Loomis, sister of his most famous victim. Is he really cured, or will he kill again?

writers: H.P. Lovecraft, Brian Yuzna, Dennis Paoli, Stuart Gordon
name: From Beyond
overview: The Resonator, a powerful machine that can control the sixth sense, has killed its creator and sent his associate into an insane asylum. When a psychiatrist becomes determined to continue the experiment, she unwittingly opens the door to a hostile parallel universe.
review:
From Beyond is a classic slice of ’80s Lovecraftian horror that leans hard into the weird and the grotesque. Directed by Stuart Gordon and anchored by Jeffrey Combs’ memorable turn as the obsessed Crawford Tillinghast, it’s a trippy, unsettling blend of sci-fi and body horror that feels like a cross between Re-Animator and The Thing. If you dig practical effects that squirm and ooze in all the right ways, this one’s a wild ride—even if the story itself is pretty straightforward mad scientist fare.

What really sticks with you is the unsettling concept of the Resonator machine, which tears open the veil on unseen dimensions only to unleash monstrous entities. The tagline “Humans are such easy prey” nails the film’s grim worldview—there’s no heroic victory here, just creeping dread and a slow melt into chaos. The practical effects and creature designs are a highlight, complementing the claustrophobic atmosphere and the film’s fascination with sensory perception and reality’s fragility. The supporting cast, including Barbara Crampton and Ken Foree, adds solid texture, making the horror feel grounded even as the visuals get increasingly bizarre.

Heads up for anyone sensitive to animal harm—this one’s notorious for some pretty heavy animal death and abuse, including dogs, cats, and horses. Body horror fans will get their fill, but those who pin the animal harm and body horror triggers should definitely be cautious going in. There’s also a fair share of creepy crawlies (spiders, snakes, bugs) that might unsettle the arachnophobes and entomophobes among you.
emailReview:

review:
Grumpier Old Men is a charming, if predictable, comedy that leans heavily on the chemistry between Walter Matthau and Jack Lemmon as two curmudgeonly neighbors locked in a decades-long feud. It’s basically the lovechild of a small-town romantic comedy and a buddy rivalry flick, with a splash of fishing and old-school slapstick. Fans of the original Grumpy Old Men will appreciate the same grumpy humor and tender moments, though it doesn’t quite reach the heights of the first film’s sharp wit.

The highlight here is the delightful addition of Sophia Loren as the fiery Italian divorcée who shakes up the sleepy town and Max’s life. Her presence brings a fresh energy and a dash of sultry humor that livens up the otherwise familiar setup of family drama and romantic mishaps. The tagline “Still Yelling. Still Fighting. Still Ready for Love.” nails the tone—this movie knows it’s a bit silly but leans into the warmth of lifelong friendships and love’s persistence. Howard Deutch’s direction keeps it breezy and accessible, while the fishing and small-town backdrop add a cozy, if somewhat worn, charm.

Heads up for animal lovers: this one is heavily flagged for animal harm, including several instances of animal deaths and mistreatment. If you’re sensitive to scenes involving dogs, cats, or other animals being hurt or dying, this is a tough watch. The presence of dog fighting and other abuse-related triggers means it’s not just a passing mention but a significant part of the content to be mindful of.
emailReview:

review:
Signs is classic M. Night Shyamalan territory—an eerie, slow-burn sci-fi thriller that leans heavily into atmosphere and family drama. It’s pretty much a mix of Close Encounters meets a haunted farmhouse, with Mel Gibson anchoring the cast as a retired priest grappling with faith and fear. While it doesn’t quite reach the jaw-dropping twist heights of Shyamalan’s best work, it’s a solid, suspenseful ride that fans of thoughtful alien stories will appreciate.

What really sticks with you here is the way Shyamalan builds dread through the mundane—the quiet farm, the crop circles, and the family’s tight-knit dynamic. The tagline, “It’s not like they didn’t warn us,” feels like a cheeky nod to the slow reveal of something sinister lurking just beyond the fields. The film’s tension is supported by a subtle score and restrained visuals that avoid cheap jump scares in favor of creeping unease and emotional stakes. Plus, the performances—especially from Gibson and young Abigail Breslin—add a grounded humanity to the sci-fi premise.

Heads up for animal lovers: this one has a pretty heavy animal death component, including a dog, a horse, and a cat, along with some scenes involving bugs and spiders that might unsettle arachnophobes. If you keep “animal harm” or “pet death” on your trigger list, Signs is definitely one to eyeball carefully before diving in.
emailReview:
Signs is a quietly unsettling sci-fi thriller that blends family drama with creeping alien dread, anchored by strong performances from Mel Gibson and Abigail Breslin.

Be prepared for: dog death, horse death, cat death, unsettling scenes with bugs and spiders.

review:
The Proposal is a classic rom-com romp with Sandra Bullock’s sharp-edged, overbearing book editor Margaret Tate at the center, forced into a fake marriage with her put-upon assistant Andrew Paxton (Ryan Reynolds) to avoid deportation. It’s that “enemies-to-lovers” trope done with enough sass and chemistry to keep things lively, falling comfortably into the “When Harry Met Sally meets 2000s workplace comedy” category. Not as laugh-out-loud as some rom-coms but elevated by Bullock’s deadpan delivery and Reynolds’ charm, it’s a pretty solid entry in the genre.

What really stands out is the family dynamic and the setting—going from the cold, high-powered office world to the quirky, nature-surrounded Paxton household adds some nice texture to the story. The tagline “Here comes the bribe…” perfectly nails the cheeky tone, while the mix of awkward, slightly uncomfortable moments (hello, forced lap dance) and genuine warmth keeps the movie from feeling too formulaic. The scenes with the natural lakes and boating add a recurring, if mildly tense, backdrop given Margaret’s obvious fear of water, and there’s a fun bit of tension when she nearly drowns but manages to hold her own.

Heads up if you’re sensitive: there’s a handful of triggers including sexual objectification and a borderline sexual assault scene during the lap dance, plus some fairly frequent obscene language and gestures. The natural bodies of water show up enough that if you’re uneasy around lakes or swimming scenes, proceed with caution. Also, there’s a tense moment involving the dog getting snatched by an eagle, though it doesn’t end in tragedy. Finally, a family member’s death is mentioned but not depicted, which might come up unexpectedly for some.
emailReview:
Sandra Bullock and Ryan Reynolds light up this sassy enemies-to-lovers rom-com set between a high-powered office and a quirky lakeside family home, mixing deadpan humor with genuine warmth and a touch of tension.

name: Us
overview: Husband and wife Gabe and Adelaide Wilson take their kids to their beach house expecting to unplug and unwind with friends. But as night descends, their serenity turns to tension and chaos when some shocking visitors arrive uninvited.
review:
Jordan Peele’s *Us* is a wild, unsettling ride that blends social thriller with pure horror in a way that feels both familiar and fresh. If you dug *Get Out*’s sharp commentary and creeping dread, this one doubles down on the eerie doubles and doppelgängers, turning a family beach getaway into a nightmare of identity and survival. It’s less a straight-up horror movie and more a twisted allegory that leaves you thinking long after the credits roll—though it never loses sight of delivering some genuinely scary moments.

What really stands out here is Lupita Nyong’o’s powerhouse dual performance as Adelaide and her sinister double, Red. The film’s tagline, “Watch yourself,” perfectly captures the core theme: confronting the self and the shadow that lurks beneath. Peele’s writing is clever, weaving a story that’s as much about societal divides as it is about primal fear. The beach house setting and the sudden invasion by these “shocking visitors” escalate tension with a tight, claustrophobic pace. The unsettling visuals of the underground world and the eerie, almost ritualistic behavior of the doppelgängers add layers of mystery and horror that keep you hooked.

Heads up for those sensitive to animal distress: while no animal death is shown explicitly, there’s a disturbing undercurrent involving rabbits—caged, roaming, and implied to be a food source for the underground group. The brief, unsettling screams and imagery might catch some off guard. So if you pin the animal harm trigger, be cautious going in.
emailReview:
Jordan Peele’s *Us* delivers a chilling blend of social thriller and horror, anchored by Lupita Nyong’o’s stunning dual performance and a claustrophobic beach house setting that turns into a nightmare of identity and survival.

Be prepared for: implied animal cruelty involving rabbits, eerie doppelgänger violence, unsettling underground rituals, and intense psychological terror.

writers: Edward Kitsis, Adam Horowitz, Brian Klugman, Lee Sternthal, Steven Lisberger, Bonnie MacBird
name: Tron: Legacy
overview: Sam Flynn, the tech-savvy and daring son of Kevin Flynn, investigates his father's disappearance and is pulled into The Grid. With the help of a mysterious program named Quorra, Sam quests to stop evil dictator Clu from crossing into the real world.
review:
Tron: Legacy is a slick sci-fi adventure that leans heavily into its neon-soaked, digital playground aesthetic. Think Blade Runner meets The Matrix, but with a much cooler soundtrack and a lot more light cycles. It’s a sequel that knows its roots and doubles down on the visual spectacle, although the story sometimes feels like it’s coasting on style over substance. Fans of cyberpunk and high-concept action will appreciate the world-building, even if the emotional stakes don’t always land as hard as you'd hope.

What stands out most here is the dazzling visual design—Joseph Kosinski’s direction turns The Grid into a hypnotic digital realm where every frame is a feast of glowing lines and futuristic architecture. The tagline “The game has changed” is spot-on, as the film updates the original’s concept for a modern audience with impressive CGI and a pulsating electronic score that really drives the pace. Garrett Hedlund and Olivia Wilde bring enough charm to their roles to keep things engaging, while Jeff Bridges delivers a layered performance juggling the dual roles of Kevin Flynn and his digital doppelgänger Clu.

Heads up to anyone who’s sensitive to intense emotional moments and harsh visuals: this movie includes some significant character deaths (including a kid and a parent), as well as scenes of burning and mutilation. There are also jump scares, flashing lights, and a dog dying, so those prone to sensory overload or grief triggers should be cautious. Overall, it’s a thrilling ride through a digital dystopia—but not without a few tough scenes.
emailReview:
Tron: Legacy dazzles with its neon-lit digital world and pulsating electronic score, creating a cyberpunk playground that’s as stylish as it is immersive.

Be prepared for: a dog dying, intense character deaths including a child and parent, scenes of burning and mutilation, and jump scares with flashing lights.

name: Insidious
overview: A family discovers that dark spirits have invaded their home after their son inexplicably falls into an endless sleep. When they reach out to a professional for help, they learn things are a lot more personal than they thought.
tagline: It's not the house that's haunted.
review:
Insidious is a classic haunted-house horror film with a twist — the real terror isn’t tied to the house but something far more personal and insidious, as the tagline promises. Directed by James Wan and written by Leigh Whannell, it feels like a blend of Poltergeist’s family drama and The Conjuring’s supernatural dread, but with a sharper focus on the astral plane and possession myths. It’s a pretty airtight horror package, elevated by a strong cast including Patrick Wilson and Rose Byrne, and Lin Shaye’s memorable turn as the psychic Elise adds a welcome dose of creepy charm.

What really sticks with you is how Insidious builds tension not just through jump scares, but through its unsettling atmosphere and clever use of silence and shadows. The idea of a child slipping into an “endless sleep” and the family’s desperate attempts to reach him taps into primal fears, while the film’s exploration of dark spirits invading more than just physical space adds layers to the usual haunted house trope. It’s also worth noting the tight pacing and the way it leans into classic horror motifs without feeling overly derivative.

That said, if you’re sensitive to animal harm triggers, be warned: this one doesn’t hold back on animal deaths and abuse, which show up repeatedly and can be quite distressing. Also, there are plenty of creepy crawlies like spiders and bugs, plus some unsettling body horror moments. If those themes are on your list, prepare accordingly.
emailReview:
Insidious delivers a masterclass in haunted-house horror with a chilling atmosphere, standout performances, and a fresh spin on possession lore that lingers long after the credits roll.

Be prepared for: repeated animal deaths and abuse, unsettling body horror, and creepy crawlies like spiders and bugs.

name: The Book of Eli
overview: A post-apocalyptic tale, in which a lone man fights his way across America in order to protect a sacred book that holds the secrets to saving humankind.
tagline: Some will kill to have it. He will kill to protect it.
review:
The Book of Eli is a grim, gritty post-apocalyptic action drama that leans heavily on its spiritual undertones and Denzel Washington’s quietly commanding presence. It’s like Mad Max meets The Road, but with a biblical twist—where the survival of mankind hinges on a mysterious sacred book. While it sometimes dips into familiar genre tropes, the film stands out for its brooding atmosphere and the moral weight it tries to carry, even if it doesn’t always fully deliver on its ambitious promise.

What’s most worth noting here is the way the movie balances its bleak world-building with moments of genuine reflection. The tagline, “Some will kill to have it. He will kill to protect it,” perfectly sums up the relentless tension that underpins the story, as Eli treks across a ravaged America to safeguard knowledge that could save humanity. The Hughes brothers direct with a stylish eye for desolate landscapes and brutal encounters, and Gary Whitta’s script leans into themes of faith, hope, and redemption without becoming preachy. Plus, Gary Oldman’s menacing villain adds a sharp edge to the stakes.

Heads up for those sensitive to animal harm and death—there’s a fair bit of that, including a dog and other animals meeting grim fates, along with some jump scares that might catch you off guard. If spiders, snakes, or bugs are on your list, be aware they show up too. The story also includes some heavier emotional blows like parental death and suicide, so it’s not exactly light fare for anyone looking for a breezy watch.
emailReview:
The Book of Eli offers a grim and gritty post-apocalyptic journey anchored by Denzel Washington’s quietly commanding presence and Gary Oldman’s chilling villain, all wrapped in a brooding atmosphere that blends faith and survival.

Be prepared for: dog death, snake and spider encounters, animal harm, parental death, and suicide.

writers: Caspian Tredwell-Owen, Alex Kurtzman, Roberto Orci
name: The Island
overview: In 2019, Lincoln Six-Echo is a resident of a seemingly "Utopian" but contained facility. Like all of the inhabitants of this carefully-controlled environment, Lincoln hopes to be chosen to go to The Island — reportedly the last uncontaminated location on the planet. But Lincoln soon discovers that everything about his existence is a lie.
review:
Michael Bay’s 2005 sci-fi thriller *The Island* is a slick, high-concept action flick that feels like *Logan’s Run* meets *Gattaca* with a dash of *The Truman Show* paranoia. It’s got that glossy, over-the-top Bay aesthetic—fast cuts, explosions, and plenty of chase sequences—but beneath the bombast is a decent premise about identity and control. Ewan McGregor and Scarlett Johansson lead as clones trapped in a manufactured utopia, and while the story isn’t breaking new ground, it rides the wave of early-2000s dystopian sci-fi with enough style to keep things moving. It’s not as deep as some of its peers, but it’s definitely elevated by McGregor’s earnestness and Johansson’s charm.

What stands out most is the film’s exploration of the illusion of freedom—“Your time will come...” isn’t just a tagline, it’s the chilling promise of a fate these clones desperately try to escape. The set design nails that sterile, too-perfect vibe of the “facility,” and the contrast when the outside world finally crashes in is jarring and effective. The script leans heavily on conspiracy thriller tropes and, yes, some classic Michael Bay explosions, but there’s a pulse beneath the spectacle that questions what it means to be human. The supporting cast, including Sean Bean as the morally ambiguous scientist, add texture, even if some characters feel a bit undercooked.

Heads up for those sensitive to multiple forms of violence and distressing imagery: the movie includes jump scares, scenes of people being burned alive, and finger/toe mutilation. Animal lovers should also be cautious as there’s a dog death. Plus, there are moments of claustrophobia and some intense blood and gore that might catch you off guard. It’s one of those flashy thrillers that doesn’t shy away from throwing everything but the kitchen sink at you—and that includes a few heavy triggers.
emailReview:
Michael Bay’s *The Island* delivers slick, high-octane sci-fi thrills with a glossy aesthetic and standout performances from Ewan McGregor and Scarlett Johansson, all wrapped in a shiny dystopian package that questions freedom and identity.

Be prepared for: a dog death, scenes of burning alive, finger and toe mutilation, intense blood and gore, and moments of claustrophobia.

name: The Transporter
overview: Former Special Forces officer, Frank Martin will deliver anything to anyone for the right price, and his no-questions-asked policy puts him in high demand. But when he realizes his latest cargo is alive, it sets in motion a dangerous chain of events. The bound and gagged Lai is being smuggled to France by a shady American businessman, and Frank works to save her as his own illegal activities are uncovered by a French detective.

name: Contagion
overview: As an epidemic of a lethal airborne virus - that kills within days - rapidly grows, the worldwide medical community races to find a cure and control the panic that spreads faster than the virus itself.
review:
Contagion is a tense, no-frills medical thriller that feels like a documentary version of a pandemic horror flick — think Outbreak meets a very serious episode of a global news special. Steven Soderbergh’s direction keeps things clinical and urgent without slipping into melodrama, while Scott Z. Burns’ script smartly captures the chaos of a worldwide health crisis. It’s not a wild ride, but it’s gripping in a subtle, realistic way that’s aged especially well in the years since its release.

What stands out most here is how the film juggles multiple storylines — from public health officials like Kate Winslet’s Erin Mears to conspiracy theorists like Jude Law’s Alan Krumwiede — showing different facets of fear and misinformation as the virus spreads. The tagline “Nothing spreads like fear” feels spot on, highlighting how panic often outpaces the virus itself. The cast is strong across the board, with Matt Damon and Marion Cotillard adding emotional depth amid the procedural grind. The film’s restrained score and clinical visuals underscore the bleakness and inevitability of an outbreak, making it feel eerily plausible.

Those sensitive to animal-related content should be cautious: Contagion includes multiple instances of animal deaths and distress, including pets and wildlife, which might catch viewers off guard. If animal triggers are high on your list, be prepared for some tough scenes.
emailReview:
Contagion is a clinically precise and quietly gripping pandemic thriller that balances multiple storylines with a sharp focus on fear and misinformation, anchored by strong performances from Kate Winslet, Jude Law, and Matt Damon.

Be prepared for: multiple animal deaths including pets, wildlife distress, and emotionally charged scenes of loss.

name: Bridesmaids
overview: Annie's life is a mess. But when she finds out her lifetime best friend is engaged, she simply must serve as Lillian's maid of honor. Though lovelorn and broke, Annie bluffs her way through the expensive and bizarre rituals. With one chance to get it perfect, she’ll show Lillian and her bridesmaids just how far you’ll go for someone you love.
review:
Bridesmaids is a riotous comedy that manages to blend raunchy humor with genuinely heartfelt moments, landing somewhere between classic wedding chaos flicks and female buddy comedies like Bridesmaids feels like a sharper, wittier take on the genre that leans heavily on Kristen Wiig’s neurotic charm and Melissa McCarthy’s scene-stealing antics. It’s not just another bridal party disaster movie — it’s a messy, relatable dive into friendship, jealousy, and the brutal economics of adult life, all wrapped up in absurd set pieces and sharp dialogue.

What really elevates Bridesmaids is its mix of outrageous situations with a surprisingly tender core. The tagline, “Save the date,” plays into the film’s obsession with the high stakes of wedding rituals, which become a battleground for Annie’s personal struggles and loyalties. The writing by Wiig and Annie Mumolo is clever and self-aware, balancing slapstick with moments of vulnerability that keep it from feeling like just a string of gags. Plus, Paul Feig’s direction keeps the pace brisk and the tone just the right side of frenetic, ensuring the chaos never overwhelms the emotional beats.

Heads up for those sensitive to animal-related content and certain intense themes: the film includes the death of a dog and other animal-related distress, as well as mentions and depictions of sexual assault, domestic violence, and various forms of bodily harm. There are also flashing lights and some anxiety-inducing scenarios, so if any of those are on your radar, brace yourself accordingly.
emailReview:
Bridesmaids is a riotous comedy that pairs Kristen Wiig’s neurotic charm with Melissa McCarthy’s unforgettable antics, delivering sharp dialogue and absurd set pieces that make wedding chaos feel both hilarious and heartbreakingly real.

Be prepared for: a dog’s death, sexual assault references, domestic violence, bodily harm, and flashing lights.

writers: Peter Gaulke, Gerry Swallow, Jim Hecht, Michael J. Wilson
name: Ice Age: The Meltdown
overview: Diego, Manny and Sid return in this sequel to the hit animated movie Ice Age. This time around, the deep freeze is over, and the ice-covered earth is starting to melt, which will destroy the trio's cherished valley. The impending disaster prompts them to reunite and warn all the other beasts about the desperate situation.

name: Panic Room
overview: Trapped in their New York brownstone's panic room, a hidden chamber built as a sanctuary in the event of break-ins, newly divorced Meg Altman and her young daughter Sarah play a deadly game of cat-and-mouse with three intruders - Burnham, Raoul and Junior - during a brutal home invasion. But the room itself is the focal point because what the intruders really want is inside it.
tagline: It was supposed to be the safest room in the house.

writers: George Gallo, Michael Barrie, Jim Mulholland, Doug Richardson
name: Bad Boys
overview: Marcus Burnett is a hen-pecked family man. Mike Lowry is a foot-loose and fancy free ladies' man. Both are Miami policemen, and both have 72 hours to reclaim a consignment of drugs stolen from under their station's nose. To complicate matters, in order to get the assistance of the sole witness to a murder, they have to pretend to be each other.

writers: Matt Greenberg, Scott Alexander, Larry Karaszewski, Stephen King
overview: A man who specializes in debunking paranormal occurrences checks into the fabled room 1408 in the Dolphin Hotel. Soon after settling in, he confronts genuine terror.
tagline: The Dolphin Hotel invites you to stay in any of its stunning rooms. Except one.

writers: Thomas Harris, David Mamet, Steven Zaillian
name: Hannibal
overview: After having successfully eluded the authorities for years, Hannibal peacefully lives in Italy in disguise as an art scholar. Trouble strikes again when he's discovered leaving a deserving few dead in the process. He returns to America to make contact with now disgraced Agent Clarice Starling, who is suffering the wrath of a malicious FBI rival as well as the media.
tagline: His genius undeniable. His evil unspeakable. His name...Hannibal.
review:
Hannibal is the slick, stylish follow-up to The Silence of the Lambs that leans into its dark, operatic horror with Ridley Scott’s signature visual panache. It’s part psychological thriller, part macabre crime drama, and it rides heavily on Anthony Hopkins’ magnetic return as Hannibal Lecter — equal parts cultured predator and chilling enigma. If you’re a fan of the first film or the wave of early-2000s cerebral thrillers, this one’s a rich, if sometimes overindulgent, feast of tension and twisted elegance.

What stands out here is the way the film balances Hannibal’s polished European exile with his brutal, remorseless nature — the tagline “His genius undeniable. His evil unspeakable.” really nails that duality. Julianne Moore steps into Clarice Starling’s shoes with a fresh take amid a story that juggles FBI politics, media pressures, and a sadistic new antagonist played by Gary Oldman. The screenplay by David Mamet and Steven Zaillian brings sharp dialogue and layered character drama, even if the plot occasionally gets lost in its own stylish complexity. Visually, the film is drenched in moody, often haunting compositions, which complement its suspenseful and gruesome beats.

Be heavily warned if animal harm or death is a serious trigger for you. This movie features multiple instances of animal suffering and death, including dogs, horses, cats, and more, alongside unsettling imagery involving bugs, snakes, and spiders. Those sensitive to these kinds of scenes should approach with caution.
emailReview:
Hannibal is a darkly elegant thriller that combines Ridley Scott’s lush visuals with Anthony Hopkins’ magnetic, chilling return as the cultured yet brutal Hannibal Lecter, creating a tension-filled feast for fans of cerebral horror.

Be prepared for: multiple horrific animal deaths including dogs and horses, unsettling insect and snake imagery, and intense scenes involving spiders.

name: Nope
overview: Residents in a lonely gulch of inland California bear witness to an uncanny, chilling discovery.

name: Sinister
overview: Found footage helps a true-crime novelist realize how and why a family was murdered in his new home, though his discoveries put his entire family in the path of a supernatural entity.
tagline: Once you see him, nothing can save you.

name: It Follows
overview: After carefree teenager Jay  sleeps with her new boyfriend, Hugh, for the first time, she learns that she is the latest recipient of a fatal curse that is passed from victim to victim via sexual intercourse. Death, Jay learns, will creep inexorably toward her as either a friend or a stranger. Jay's friends don't believe her seemingly paranoid ravings, until they too begin to see the phantom assassins and band together to help her flee or defend herself.
tagline: It doesn't think. It doesn't feel. It doesn't give up.

writers: Jeff Nathanson, Irene Mecchi, Jonathan Roberts, Linda Woolverton
name: The Lion King
overview: Simba idolizes his father, King Mufasa, and takes to heart his own royal destiny. But not everyone in the kingdom celebrates the new cub's arrival. Scar, Mufasa's brother—and former heir to the throne—has plans of his own. The battle for Pride Rock is ravaged with betrayal, tragedy and drama, ultimately resulting in Simba's exile. With help from a curious pair of newfound friends, Simba will have to figure out how to grow up and take back what is rightfully his.

writers: J.M. Barrie, James V. Hart, Nick Castle, Malia Scotch Marmo
name: Hook
overview: The boy who wasn't supposed grow up—Peter Pan—does just that, becoming a soulless corporate lawyer whose workaholism could cost him his wife and kids. During his trip to see Granny Wendy in London, the vengeful Capt. Hook kidnaps Peter's kids and forces Peter to return to Neverland.
tagline: To live would be an awfully big adventure.

writers: Joe Russo, Ande Parks, Anthony Russo, Fernando León González
name: Extraction
overview: Tyler Rake, a fearless mercenary who offers his services on the black market, embarks on a dangerous mission when he is hired to rescue the kidnapped son of a Mumbai crime lord…
tagline: When the mission ends, redemption begins

writers: Helen Fielding, Andrew Davies, Richard Curtis
name: Bridget Joness Diary
overview: A chaotic Bridget Jones meets a snobbish lawyer, and he soon enters her world of imperfections.
tagline: All women keep score... Only the great ones put it in writing.

name: Chappie
overview: Every child comes into the world full of promise, and none more so than Chappie: he is gifted, special, a prodigy. Like any child, Chappie will come under the influence of his surroundings—some good, some bad—and he will rely on his heart and soul to find his way in the world and become his own man. But there's one thing that makes Chappie different from any one else: he is a robot.
tagline: I am consciousness. I am alive. I am Chappie.

writers: Peter Steinfeld, Allan Loeb, Ben Mezrich
overview: Ben Campbell is a young, highly intelligent, student at M.I.T. in Boston who strives to succeed. Wanting a scholarship to transfer to Harvard School of Medicine with the desire to become a doctor, Ben learns that he cannot afford the $300,000 for the four to five years of schooling as he comes from a poor, working-class background. But one evening, Ben is introduced by his unorthodox math professor Micky Rosa into a small but secretive club of five. Students Jill, Choi, Kianna, and Fisher, who are being trained by Professor Rosa of the skill of card counting at blackjack.
tagline: They proved the Vegas Blackjack System was beatable...by beating the hell out of it.

writers: Oliver Butcher, Stephen Cornwell, Didier Van Cauwelaert
name: Unknown
overview: A man awakens from a coma, only to discover that someone has taken on his identity and that no one, (not even his wife), believes him. With the help of a young woman, he sets out to prove who he is.

name: Disturbia
overview: Kale is a 17-year-old placed under house arrest after punching his teacher. He is confined to his house, and decides to use his free time spying on his neighbors. Things start to get weird when guests enter the Turner's house and don't come back out. Kale and his friends, Ronnie and Ashley, start to grow more and more interested in what is actually happening within the house of Robert Turner.
tagline: Every killer lives next door to someone.

name: The Babadook
overview: A single mother, plagued by the violent death of her husband, battles with her son's fear of a monster lurking in the house, but soon discovers a sinister presence all around her.
tagline: If it's in a word, or it's in a look, you can't get rid of...
review:
The Babadook is a psychological horror film that stands out as a deeply unsettling exploration of grief and trauma rather than a typical monster movie. It feels like a blend of The Ring’s creeping dread and a character study on PTSD, elevated by Essie Davis’s haunting performance as Amelia Vanek. Unlike jump-scare-heavy horror flicks, this one uses its supernatural elements to probe the mental and emotional breakdown of a mother struggling with loss and an autistic-coded son who’s just trying to survive. It’s not just scary—it’s heartbreakingly real in its depiction of grief’s monstrous hold.

What really lingers here is Jennifer Kent’s tight script and the film’s atmospheric visuals, which turn the mundane domestic space into a claustrophobic, nightmarish trap. The tagline “If it’s in a word, or it’s in a look, you can’t get rid of...” perfectly sums up the way the Babadook represents an inescapable, festering presence—grief and trauma made flesh. The film’s use of sound design and sudden loud noises amplifies tension without relying on cheap thrills, while its hallucinatory sequences blur reality and madness in a way that keeps you off balance. The relationship between Amelia and her son Samuel is raw and complicated, peeling back layers of love, resentment, and misunderstanding in a way horror rarely attempts.

Heads up: The Babadook is heavy on child abuse and abusive parent dynamics, with Amelia’s struggle manifesting as emotional and physical violence that escalates disturbingly. Those sensitive to depictions of mental illness, PTSD, and the mistreatment of neurodivergent children (Samuel is heavily autism-coded) should be cautious. The film also features intense jump scares, loud bangs, and some particularly distressing animal harm, including a dog’s death. If you’re triggered by stalking, possession, or a blurring of reality that can feel disorienting, this one demands a careful approach.
emailReview:
The Babadook is a haunting psychological horror that masterfully blends creeping dread with a raw, heartbreaking look at grief and trauma, anchored by Essie Davis’s unforgettable performance.

Be prepared for: a dog’s death, intense child abuse, emotional and physical violence, stalking, and disorienting hallucinatory sequences.

writers: Katie Dippold, Paul Feig, Ivan Reitman, Dan Aykroyd, Harold Ramis
name: Ghostbusters
overview: Following a ghost invasion of Manhattan, paranormal enthusiasts Erin Gilbert and Abby Yates, nuclear engineer Jillian Holtzmann, and subway worker Patty Tolan band together to stop the otherworldly threat.

name: Warm Bodies
overview: After a zombie becomes involved with the girlfriend of one of his victims, their romance sets in motion a sequence of events that might transform the entire lifeless world.
tagline: He's still dead, but he's getting warmer.

writers: Timothy Dowling, William Blake Herron, Paul Rudd, David Wain, Ken Marino
name: Role Models
overview: Two salesmen trash a company truck on an energy drink-fueled bender. Upon their arrest, the court gives them a choice: do hard time or spend 150 service hours with a mentorship program. After one day with the kids, however, jail doesn't look half bad.
tagline: They're about to get more than they plea-bargained for.

name: Bolt
overview: Bolt is the star of the biggest show in Hollywood. The only problem is, he thinks it's real. After he's accidentally shipped to New York City and separated from Penny, his beloved co-star and owner, Bolt must harness all his "super powers" to find a way home.

writers: James McCausland, George Miller, Byron Kennedy
name: Mad Max
overview: Taking place in a dystopian Australia in the near future, Mad Max tells the story of a highway patrolman cruising the squalid back roads that have become the breeding ground of criminals foraging for gasoline and scraps. After some grisly events at the hands of a motorcycle gang, Max sets out across the barren wastelands in search of revenge.
tagline: The maximum force of the future.

name: The Fall Guy
overview: Fresh off an almost career-ending accident, stuntman Colt Seavers has to track down a missing movie star, solve a conspiracy and try to win back the love of his life while still doing his day job.

name: Lemony Snicket's A Series of Unfortunate Events
cleanNameArticles: lemony snickets a series of unfortunate events
overview: Three wealthy children's parents are killed in a fire. When they are sent to a distant relative, they find out that he is plotting to kill them and seize their fortune.  This movie is extremely alarming, an expression which here means "a thrilling misadventure involving three ingenious orphans and a villainous actor named Count Olaf (Jim Carrey) who wants their enormous fortune."  It includes a suspicious fire, delicious pasta, Jim Carrey, poorly behaved looches, Billy Connolly, an incredibly deadly viper, Meryl Streep, and the voice of an imposter named Jude Law.

name: Ready or Not
overview: A bride's wedding night takes a sinister turn when her eccentric new in-laws force her to take part in a terrifying game.
tagline: A killer game of hide and seek.
review:
This was such a wild ride. Great horror, sprinkled with just the right amount of comedy, and an absolutely commanding, vocal-cord-killing performance by Samara Weaving in the lead. 

If you pinned triggers for screaming, restraining, blood/gore, choking, or gun violence, you may need to avoid this one, as it will be tough to avoid the rampant displays of them during the entirety of the film. 

Otherwise, add this one to your respective Halloween rotations (or just when you need to see pandemonium and chaos related to wedding themes).
emailReview:
Samara Weaving delivers a show-stopping, scream-filled performance in this wild horror-comedy that perfectly blends chaos with darkly funny wedding madness.

Be prepared for: intense screaming, graphic blood and gore, choking scenes, gun violence, and physical restraint.

writers: Richard Wenk, Michael Sloan, Richard Lindheim
name: The Equalizer 2
overview: Robert McCall, who serves an unflinching justice for the exploited and oppressed, embarks on a relentless, globe-trotting quest for vengeance when his former partner is murdered.
review:
The Equalizer 2 is a by-the-numbers action thriller that leans hard on Denzel Washington’s steady charisma to keep the wheels turning. Directed by Antoine Fuqua, it’s a globe-trotting revenge saga where Robert McCall trades his quiet life for a relentless pursuit of justice after his former partner’s murder. It’s not reinventing the wheel if you’ve seen the first Equalizer or similar vigilante flicks, but fans of the genre will appreciate the muscular fight scenes and Washington’s measured intensity. It’s a solid, if somewhat predictable, entry in the revenge thriller canon.

What stands out here is the film’s commitment to its tagline, “There is no equal,” which feels less like a boast and more like a straightforward statement of purpose. The writing by Richard Wenk keeps the plot moving briskly, even if it doesn’t stray far from genre conventions. There’s a certain melancholy woven into McCall’s quest, especially in how the film handles loyalty and loss, but the real draw is the action set pieces that blend grit with style. The supporting cast, including Pedro Pascal as the betrayed partner, adds some flavor, though the story revolves firmly around Washington’s McCall.

Be heavily warned if animal harm is on your list—The Equalizer 2 doesn’t shy away from showing multiple animals in distress or worse, including dogs, cats, and horses. This is a rare action film where the animal death triggers are surprisingly prominent, so anyone sensitive to that should proceed with caution. Also, spiders, snakes, and bugs make appearances that might unsettle some viewers. If you’re sensitive to animal suffering or death, this one’s going to be tough to watch.
emailReview:
Denzel Washington’s steady charisma powers this globe-trotting revenge thriller, where gritty action scenes meet a melancholy undercurrent of loyalty and loss.

Be prepared for: multiple animal deaths including dogs, cats, and horses, unsettling spider encounters, and scenes involving snakes and bugs.

writers: Rhett Reese, Paul Wernick, Dave Callaham
name: Zombieland: Double Tap
overview: Columbus, Tallahassee, Wichita, and Little Rock move to the American heartland as they face off against evolved zombies, fellow survivors, and the growing pains of the snarky makeshift family.
review:
Zombieland: Double Tap is a snarky, zombie-apocalypse comedy that tries to recapture the goofy charm of the original but leans a bit heavily on familiar gags. It’s like Shaun of the Dead meets a buddy road trip, but with more evolved zombies and the awkward dynamics of a makeshift family trying to survive in the heartland. Woody Harrelson and Jesse Eisenberg bring back their usual banter, and Abigail Breslin’s Little Rock adds some tension to the group, but it’s not quite as fresh or funny as the 2009 classic. Still, it’s a decent time if you’re craving a mix of gore, laughs, and some borderline dysfunctional family drama.

What stands out is the way the film juggles its genre tropes—there’s plenty of zombie mayhem with the “double tap” rule still in play, but also some surprisingly tender moments about the group’s evolving relationships. The new characters, like Zoey Deutch’s Madison, shake up the dynamic (sometimes for better, sometimes for worse), and the heartland setting gives the usual chaos a slightly different vibe. The writing leans into self-aware humor, but it’s a mixed bag; you’ll get some solid one-liners amid the predictable jokes. Ruben Fleischer’s direction keeps the pace brisk, and the action sequences deliver the expected mix of blood and carnage.

Heads up for those sensitive to violence and death: this one doesn’t hold back on gore, jump scares, or brutal moments like burning alive and mutilation. There are also some tough emotional punches with the death of a child and a dog, so if those hits pack a punch for you, be prepared. Flashing images and shaky cam might also be a headache if you’re prone to sensory overload. It’s a wild ride with plenty of carnage, so proceed with caution if any of those triggers are on your list.
emailReview:
Zombieland: Double Tap serves up snarky zombie chaos with a side of dysfunctional family drama, mixing gore and laughs in a heartland setting that adds a fresh twist to the apocalypse road trip.

Be prepared for: brutal burning alive scenes, graphic mutilation, the death of a dog and a child, and intense jump scares.

writers: Kurt Johnstad, Antony Johnston, Sam Hart
name: Atomic Blonde
overview: An undercover MI6 agent is sent to Berlin during the Cold War to investigate the murder of a fellow agent and recover a missing list of double agents.

name: Cruel Intentions
overview: Slaking a thirst for dangerous games, Kathryn challenges her stepbrother, Sebastian, to deflower their headmaster's daughter before the summer ends. If he succeeds, the prize is the chance to bed Kathryn. But if he loses, Kathryn will claim his most prized possession.
tagline: In the game of seduction, there is only one rule: Never fall in love.

writers: Danny McBride, Len Wiseman, Kevin Grevioux
name: Underworld: Evolution
overview: As the war between the vampires and the Lycans rages on, Selene, a former member of the Death Dealers (an elite vampire special forces unit that hunts werewolves), and Michael, the werewolf hybrid, work together in an effort to unlock the secrets of their respective bloodlines.
tagline: A new race. A new battle. A new hero...
review:
Underworld: Evolution doubles down on its dark, gothic vampire-versus-werewolf saga with a glossy, if occasionally convoluted, blend of action and myth-building. Fans of the first film will find more of the same sleek, stylized combat and brooding atmosphere, though this sequel leans harder into its sprawling supernatural family drama. It’s like Blade meets Twilight but with a heavier dose of gothic noir and less of the teen romance—Kate Beckinsale’s Selene remains the franchise’s cool, lethal anchor amid the chaos.

What stands out here is the way the film dives deeper into the lore of the Corvinus bloodline, giving the vampire-werewolf feud a more epic, almost Shakespearean weight, especially with Derek Jacobi’s Alexander Corvinus adding gravitas to the mix. The writing leans into big, operatic reveals and alliances, while Len Wiseman’s direction keeps the visuals slick and moody, perfectly capturing that shadowy underworld vibe. While the plot sometimes feels like it’s juggling too many threads, the chemistry between Beckinsale and Scott Speedman helps hold it all together, and the action sequences remain satisfyingly brutal and kinetic.

Those who pin the animal harm and death triggers should be cautious here—there are multiple instances of animal cruelty, including dog fighting and the deaths of various animals such as horses and cats, which might be tough for sensitive viewers. The film doesn’t shy away from showing these moments on screen, so if that’s on your list, brace yourself.
emailReview:
Underworld: Evolution amps up its stylish, gothic vampire-versus-werewolf saga with sleek action and a brooding, myth-heavy atmosphere anchored by Kate Beckinsale’s cool, lethal Selene.

Be prepared for: graphic dog fighting, multiple animal deaths including horses and cats, and intense supernatural violence.

name: Unstoppable
overview: A runaway train, transporting deadly, toxic chemicals, is barreling down on Stanton, Pennsylvania,  and proves to be unstoppable until a veteran engineer and young conductor risk their lives to try and stop it with a switch engine.

writers: Alexis Nolent, Luc Jacamon, Andrew Kevin Walker
name: The Killer
overview: After a fateful near-miss, an assassin battles his employers, and himself, on an international manhunt he insists isn't personal.
review:
David Fincher’s *The Killer* is a sleek, brooding thriller that’s as much about internal turmoil as it is about international espionage. Michael Fassbender delivers a typically intense, restrained performance as the assassin wrestling with his own code amid a deadly game of cat and mouse. If you liked the cold precision of Fincher’s earlier work like *Se7en* or *Gone Girl*, this fits right in with that dark, meticulous vibe—though it’s a bit leaner on emotional complexity and more focused on style and atmosphere.

What stands out here is the tagline, “Execution is everything,” which is less a clever slogan and more a thematic through-line. The film makes you think about the nature of professionalism, loyalty, and self-destruction. The sparse dialogue and muted score keep the tension tight, while the international manhunt plotline is a familiar but effective framework to showcase the assassin’s internal battle. Tilda Swinton’s presence as “The Expert” adds an icy counterpoint that complements Fassbender’s brooding silence, giving the film a subtle, almost hypnotic rhythm.

Heads up for sensitive viewers: this one leans heavily into animal death—dogs, cats, horses, and more make appearances in the grim tally of casualties. Plus, there’s a fair dose of creepy-crawly stuff (spiders, bugs, snakes) that might unsettle some. If animals or creepy critters are on your “avoid” list, be warned that this movie doesn’t shy away from those darker elements.
emailReview:
David Fincher’s *The Killer* is a sleek, brooding thriller that pairs Michael Fassbender’s intense, restrained assassin with Tilda Swinton’s icy presence, creating a hypnotic tension wrapped in cold precision and dark atmosphere.

Be prepared for: multiple animal deaths including dogs, cats, and horses, unsettling scenes with spiders and snakes, and a steady undercurrent of professional self-destruction.

When French animal-control officer Capitaine Chantel DuBois picks up their scent, Alex and company are forced to hide out in a traveling circus.
tagline: They have one shot to get back home.
