overview: An advice columnist, Andie Anderson, tries pushing the boundaries of what she can write about in her new piece about how to get a man to leave you in 10 days. Her editor, Lana, loves it, and Andie goes off to find a man she can use for the experiment. Enter executive Ben Berry, who is so confident in his romantic prowess that he thinks he can make any woman fall in love with him in 10 days. When Andie and Ben meet, their plans backfire.
tagline: One of them is lying. So is the other.
review:
How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days is a quintessential early-2000s rom-com that leans hard into the genre’s classic battle-of-the-sexes setup but adds a clever twist: both leads are secretly trying to dupe each other. Kate Hudson and Matthew McConaughey bring their usual charm, with Hudson’s Andie Anderson playing a mischievous advice columnist and McConaughey’s Ben Berry as the cocky executive who thinks he can win any woman’s heart in ten days. It’s not as sharp as it tries to be, but the chemistry between the leads keeps it from feeling like a total rerun of rom-com tropes.

What really stands out is the film’s self-awareness—Andie’s article about how to drive a guy away is both the plot and the punchline, poking fun at the ridiculousness of dating games. Donald Petrie’s direction keeps things breezy, with a solid supporting cast including Kathryn Hahn adding some welcome sidekick energy. The tagline “One of them is lying. So is the other.” nails the premise, setting up a fun cat-and-mouse dynamic that’s more about laughs than deep emotional stakes. The movie doesn’t reinvent the wheel, but it’s an enjoyable ride for fans of lighthearted romantic mischief.

Heads up for animal lovers: despite being mostly a rom-com, the film has a surprisingly heavy load of animal-related triggers. If you’re sensitive to pet deaths or scenes involving animal harm, especially dogs, cats, or horses, be prepared for some upsetting moments. Bugs and spiders also make appearances, so those with those triggers should be cautious going in.
emailReview:
This early-2000s rom-com charms with Kate Hudson and Matthew McConaughey’s playful chemistry and a delightfully self-aware take on dating games that keeps things light and fun.

Be prepared for: dog death, cat death, horse death, bug scenes, spider scenes.

name: Resident Evil
overview:
First film in the Resident Evil live action film franchise.

When a virus leaks from a top-secret facility, turning all resident researchers into ravenous zombies and their lab animals into mutated hounds from hell, the government sends in an elite military task force to contain the outbreak.
tagline: A secret experiment. A deadly virus. A fatal mistake.

name: Olympus Has Fallen
overview: When the White House (Secret Service Code: "Olympus") is captured by a terrorist mastermind and the President is kidnapped, disgraced former Presidential guard Mike Banning finds himself trapped within the building. As the national security team scrambles to respond, they are forced to rely on Banning's inside knowledge to help retake the White House, save the President and avert an even bigger disaster.
tagline: When our flag falls our nation will rise.
review:
Olympus Has Fallen is classic early-2010s action fare, dialing up the intensity with a patriotic flair that feels like Die Hard meets White House political thriller. Gerard Butler’s Mike Banning is your quintessential tough-guy hero—disgraced but ready to save the day—with Aaron Eckhart’s President adding some gravitas to the hostage stakes. If you’re into high-stakes siege movies where tension and gunfire never let up, this one’s a solid pick, though it leans heavily into familiar tropes without much subtlety.

What stands out here is the claustrophobic setting of the White House under siege, which director Antoine Fuqua uses to good effect, keeping the pace brisk and the action tight. The tagline, “When our flag falls our nation will rise,” nails the film’s clear-cut patriotism and the theme of personal redemption woven through Banning’s journey. The writing plays it straightforward, but the film’s real muscle is in the set pieces and the gritty, relentless visuals. It’s not reinventing the genre, but it delivers the goods with enough flair to satisfy action junkies.

Heads up to those sensitive to animal harm, as the movie includes a difficult scene involving a dog being shot—definitely one of the tougher moments here. The stakes get grim with several death scenes, including a child’s, and the action sequences are peppered with brutal violence, including strangulation and knife fights. If jump scares or flashing lights bother you, those are also present. So, anyone with triggers around gun violence, death (especially kids and animals), or intense physical harm should tread carefully.
emailReview:
Olympus Has Fallen packs classic early-2010s action thrills with Gerard Butler’s tough-guy charm and a white-knuckle siege atmosphere that keeps the tension cranked from start to finish.

Be prepared for: a dog being shot, child death, brutal strangulation, knife fights, and intense gun violence.

writers: Jeff Wadlow, Mark Millar, John Romita Jr.
name: Kick-Ass 2
overview: After Kick-Ass’ insane bravery inspires a new wave of self-made masked crusaders, he joins a patrol led by the Colonel Stars and Stripes. When these amateur superheroes are hunted down by Red Mist — reborn as The Mother Fucker — only the blade-wielding Hit-Girl can prevent their annihilation.
review:
Kick-Ass 2 tries to recapture the wild, hyper-violent energy of its predecessor but lands somewhere between a crowd-pleasing superhero romp and a messy, overstuffed sequel. It’s got that irreverent teen-vigilante vibe fans of the first movie will recognize, but with Jeff Wadlow stepping in as director and writer, the tone shifts a bit—less fresh and a bit more chaotic. The cast, led by Aaron Taylor-Johnson’s earnest Kick-Ass and Chloë Grace Moretz’s razor-sharp Hit-Girl, still delivers punchy performances, and Jim Carrey’s turn as the Colonel Stars and Stripes adds an oddball flair, but the story leans heavily on familiar tropes without the same spark.

What stands out here is the attempt to expand the universe with a growing army of amateur heroes and a nastier villain in The Mother Fucker, played by Christopher Mintz-Plasse. The tagline, “You Can’t Fight Your Destiny,” feels like a nod to the inevitable escalation of chaos as these masked crusaders clash. The film leans hard into comic-book violence and dark humor, with Hit-Girl's blade work providing the most visceral thrills. Still, the tone sometimes feels uneven, juggling camp and brutality without fully committing to either, which leaves it a bit less memorable than the original.

Heads up if you’re sensitive to animal-related content—this movie is loaded with it. Be heavily warned if triggers like animal death, abuse, or fighting are on your list, as several pets and other creatures meet grim fates. On top of that, the usual fare of intense violence and some unsettling imagery might catch you off guard. Fans of dark superhero flicks with a rough edge will find much to chew on, but don’t expect a clean or gentle ride.
emailReview:
Kick-Ass 2 cranks up the comic-book chaos with razor-sharp performances and a twisted sense of humor, even if the tone stumbles between camp and brutality.

Be prepared for: graphic animal deaths, pet abuse, intense superhero violence, and grim fight scenes involving creatures.

name: Glass
overview: In a series of escalating encounters, former security guard David Dunn uses his supernatural abilities to track Kevin Wendell Crumb, a disturbed man who has twenty-four personalities. Meanwhile, the shadowy presence of Elijah Price emerges as an orchestrator who holds secrets critical to both men.
tagline: You cannot contain what you are.

writers: Catherine Johnson, Melvin Frank, Sheldon Keller, Denis Norden
name: Mamma Mia
overview: An independent, single mother who owns a small hotel on a Greek island is about to marry off the spirited young daughter she's raised alone. But, the daughter has secretly invited three of her mother's ex-lovers in the hopes of finding her biological father.
tagline: A mother. A daughter. Three possible fathers. A trip down the aisle you'll never forget.
review:
Mamma Mia is the kind of sun-soaked, ABBA-fueled musical that either sweeps you off your feet or leaves you rolling your eyes at the campy cheesiness—and I’m firmly in the former camp. This 2008 rom-com musical feels like a breezy mash-up of classic wedding chaos meets nostalgic jukebox fun, anchored by a spirited cast led by Meryl Streep and Amanda Seyfried. If you like your musicals with a side of Greek island charm and a plot that’s basically a rom-com Rubik’s cube, this one’s going to hit the right notes.

What stands out is the infectious energy that the film rides on, thanks in no small part to Phyllida Lloyd’s direction and Catherine Johnson’s lively script. The story’s simple but effective: a young bride-to-be invites her mom’s three exes to her wedding, hoping to figure out which one is her dad. Between the sunlit scenery, the memorable ABBA numbers, and the ensemble’s playful chemistry—especially Brosnan, Firth, and Skarsgård as the potential dads—the movie leans into its silliness while still delivering some unexpectedly sweet moments about family and identity. Plus, the supporting characters like Christine Baranski’s Tanya add a fun layer of sass and sparkle.

Heads up for those who pin the “there’s ghosts” trigger—there’s a brief, lighthearted ghostly moment that might catch some folks off guard. It’s nothing heavy, more of a quirky aside than a spooky element. Otherwise, Mamma Mia is pretty gentle fare in terms of content, so it’s mostly about whether you can handle the endless ABBA singalongs and the inevitable wedding-day whirlwind.
emailReview:
Mamma Mia is a sun-soaked, ABBA-fueled romp filled with infectious energy, charming Greek island vibes, and a cast that sparkles with playful chemistry.

Be prepared for: a brief lighthearted ghost moment, wedding chaos, and plenty of nostalgic musical numbers.

writers: Andrew Stanton, Mark Andrews, Michael Chabon, Edgar Rice Burroughs
name: John Carter
overview: John Carter is a war-weary, former military captain who's inexplicably transported to the mysterious and exotic planet of Barsoom (Mars) and reluctantly becomes embroiled in an epic conflict. It's a world on the brink of collapse, and Carter rediscovers his humanity when he realizes the survival of Barsoom and its people rests in his hands.

writers: Brian Helgeland, Ethan Reiff, Cyrus Voris
name: Robin Hood
overview: When soldier Robin happens upon the dying Robert of Loxley, he promises to return the man's sword to his family in Nottingham. There, he assumes Robert's identity; romances his widow, Marion; and draws the ire of the town's sheriff and King John's henchman, Godfrey.
tagline: Rise and rise again, until lambs become lions

name: The Village
overview: When a willful young man tries to venture beyond his sequestered Pennsylvania hamlet, his actions set off a chain of chilling incidents that will alter the community forever.
review:
M. Night Shyamalan’s *The Village* is a moody, atmospheric thriller that leans heavily into its claustrophobic, rural setting and slow-burn tension. It’s not quite the twisty masterpiece many hoped for back in 2004, but it’s a visually striking meditation on fear, control, and the cost of isolation. Think *The Lottery* meets *The Crucible* with a dash of *The Wicker Man*—it’s a cultish community with dark secrets, and fans of quiet, unsettling mystery will find plenty to chew on here, even if the payoff feels a bit divisive.

What stands out is the deliberate world-building: a secluded Pennsylvania hamlet that bans all contact with the outside world, built to protect itself from an unspecified threat. Bryce Dallas Howard’s Ivy Walker, a blind woman who embodies both vulnerability and resilience, anchors the story alongside Joaquin Phoenix’s restless Lucius Hunt, whose curiosity sets the plot in motion. The film’s tagline, “There is no turning back,” feels like a promise—and a warning—that once you step beyond the village’s boundaries, everything changes. Shyamalan’s signature style shines in the eerie silence, the haunting score, and the way the community’s secrets unravel slowly but surely. The film plays with genre conventions, mixing elements of suspense, horror, and drama, though it occasionally gets bogged down in exposition.

Trigger-wise, this one leans heavily on violence and death—there are multiple off-screen family deaths, some on-screen stabbings, and a major character’s painful death after a fall into a pit. There’s also a fair amount of blood and gore, including skinned animals shown on screen, and a few jump scares that punctuate the tension. The film includes mentions of sexual violence and intense emotional distress, though these are mostly in voiceover rather than depicted visually. Those who pin violent deaths, blood/gore, jump scares, or heavy emotional trauma should be cautious going in. On the upside, animals are safe from harm on screen, so no worries there.
emailReview:
M. Night Shyamalan’s *The Village* crafts a moody, claustrophobic atmosphere with strong performances that pull you deep into a rural world cloaked in secrets and slow-burning dread.

Be prepared for: on-screen stabbings, a major fall leading to a painful death, skinned animals, jump scares, and intense emotional distress.

name: Saw II
overview: When a new murder victim is discovered with all the signs of Jigsaw's hand, Detective Eric Matthews begins a full investigation and apprehends Jigsaw with little effort. But for Jigsaw, getting caught is just another part of his plan. Eight more of his victims are already fighting for their lives and now it's time for Matthews to join the game.
tagline: Oh yes... There will be blood.

name: Focus
overview: Nicky, an accomplished con artist, gets romantically involved with his disciple Jess but later ends their relationship. Years later, she returns as a femme fatale to spoil his plans.

writers: George Gallo, Marianne Wibberley, Cormac Wibberley, Ron Shelton, Jerry Stahl
name: Bad Boys II
overview: Detectives Marcus Burnett and Mike Lowrey of the Miami Narcotics Task Force are tasked with stopping the flow of the drug Ecstasy into Miami. They track the drugs to the whacked-out Cuban drug lord Johnny Tapia, who is also involved in a bloody war with Russian and Haitian mobsters.
tagline: If you can't stand the heat, get out of Miami.

name: American Pie 2
overview: After a year apart - attending different schools, meeting different people - the guys rent a beach house and vow to make this the best summer ever. As it turns out, whether that will happen or not has a lot to do with the girls. Between the wild parties, outrageous revelations and yes, a trip to band camp, they discover that times change and people change, but in the end, it's all about sticking together.
tagline: This summer it's all about sticking together.

name: Ad Astra
overview: The near future, a time when both hope and hardships drive humanity to look to the stars and beyond. While a mysterious phenomenon menaces to destroy life on planet Earth, astronaut Roy McBride undertakes a mission across the immensity of space and its many perils to uncover the truth about a lost expedition that decades before boldly faced emptiness and silence in search of the unknown.
tagline: The answers we seek are just outside our reach.

writers: Amanda Brown, Karen McCullah, Kirsten Smith
name: Legally Blonde
overview: Elle Woods has it all. She's the president of her sorority, a Hawaiian Tropic girl, Miss June in her campus calendar, and, above all, a natural blonde. She dates the cutest fraternity boy on campus and wants nothing more than to be Mrs. Warner Huntington III. But, there's just one thing stopping Warner from popping the question: Elle is too blonde.
tagline: Boldly going where no blonde has gone.

writers: David Franzoni, Peter Craig, David Scarpa
name: Gladiator II
overview: Years after witnessing the death of the revered hero Maximus at the hands of his uncle, Lucius is forced to enter the Colosseum after his home is conquered by the tyrannical Emperors who now lead Rome with an iron fist. With rage in his heart and the future of the Empire at stake, Lucius must look to his past to find strength and honor to return the glory of Rome to its people.
review:
Gladiator II tries to capture the epic sweep and gritty intensity of its predecessor, but it’s a mixed bag. The film leans hard into classic sword-and-sandals tropes—betrayal, revenge, and the fight for Rome’s soul—while adding a fresh face in Paul Mescal as Lucius. Think Gladiator meets a more modern political thriller, with Denzel Washington and Pedro Pascal rounding out a solid cast that brings some gravitas to what could’ve been a by-the-numbers sequel. It’s not quite the slam dunk everyone expected, but it’s certainly entertaining and offers a few moments of genuine emotional weight.

What stands out most here is the film’s commitment to atmosphere and spectacle. Ridley Scott’s direction leans into the grime and grandeur of ancient Rome, balanced with some surprisingly intimate character work around Lucius’ internal struggles. The tagline, “Prepare to be entertained,” fits—the movie doesn’t shy away from brutal gladiatorial combat or political intrigue, and the score punctuates these highs and lows pretty well. Fans of the original will appreciate how the story picks up years later, confronting legacy and honor amid the chaos of new tyrants, though some plot beats feel a bit predictable.

Heads up for anyone sensitive to animal-related content—this one is heavy on animal harm and death, including horses, dogs, cats, and other creatures. There’s also some unsettling animal abuse and dog fighting depicted. Plus, if you’re creeped out by spiders, snakes, or bugs, be warned those show up too. It’s a blood-soaked saga not just for people, it seems.
emailReview:
Gladiator II brings gritty spectacle and political intrigue to ancient Rome with strong performances from Paul Mescal, Denzel Washington, and Pedro Pascal, mixing epic battles with surprisingly intimate character moments.

Be prepared for: graphic animal harm and deaths including horses and dogs, dog fighting, and unsettling scenes with spiders, snakes, and bugs.

writers: Marianne Wibberley, Cormac Wibberley, Gregory Poirier, Ted Elliott, Terry Rossio, Jim Kouf, Oren Aviv, Charles Segars
name: National Treasure: Book of Secrets
overview: Benjamin Franklin Gates and Dr. Abigail Chase re-team with Riley Poole and, now armed with a stack of long-lost pages from John Wilkes Booth’s diary, Ben must follow a clue left there to prove his ancestor’s innocence in the assassination of Abraham Lincoln.
tagline: The greatest adventure history has ever revealed.

writers: Joe Russo, Christopher Markus, Stephen McFeely, Mark Greaney
name: The Gray Man
overview: When a shadowy CIA agent uncovers damning agency secrets, he's hunted across the globe by a sociopathic rogue operative who's put a bounty on his head.

name: Silent Hill
overview: In search for answers, a mother travels to the enigmatic town of Silent Hill when her daughter begins to suffer recurring nightmares related to the place. It doesn't take long for her to discover its home to beings as equally haunting as the town itself.

name: Don Jon
overview: A New Jersey guy dedicated to his family, friends, and church, develops unrealistic expectations from watching porn and works to find happiness and intimacy with his potential true love.

writers: Chris Morgan, Drew Pearce, Gary Scott Thompson
name: Fast & Furious Presents: Hobbs & Shaw
cleanNameArticles: fast and furious presents hobbs and shaw
overview: Ever since US Diplomatic Security Service Agent Hobbs and lawless outcast Shaw first faced off, they just have traded smack talk and body blows. But when cyber-genetically enhanced anarchist Brixton's ruthless actions threaten the future of humanity, they join forces to defeat him.

writers: Michael Berg, Jason Fuchs, Lori Forte
name: Ice Age: Continental Drift
overview: Manny, Diego, and Sid embark upon another adventure after their continent is set adrift. Using an iceberg as a ship, they encounter sea creatures and battle pirates as they explore a new world.
tagline: The end of the world is just the tip of the iceberg.

primaryTitle: The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian
writers: Andrew Adamson, Christopher Markus, Stephen McFeely, C.S. Lewis
Title_IMDb_Link: The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian
name: The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian
overview: One year after their incredible adventures in the Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe, Peter, Edmund, Lucy and Susan Pevensie return to Narnia to aid a young prince whose life has been threatened by the evil King Miraz. Now, with the help of a colorful cast of new characters, including Trufflehunter the badger and Nikabrik the dwarf, the Pevensie clan embarks on an incredible quest to ensure that Narnia is returned to its rightful heir.
tagline: Everything you know is about to change forever.
review:
The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian steps back into the magical world with a darker, more battle-driven tone than its predecessor, leaning into epic fantasy adventure territory. It’s less about discovery and wonder, more about reclaiming a kingdom, which makes it feel a bit like The Lord of the Rings meets a coming-of-age saga. While it doesn’t quite capture the fresh charm of The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe, it still delivers a solid sequel for fans craving more Narnian lore and sword-swinging action.

What stands out here is the way the film juggles its large cast and introduces new fantastical creatures like Trufflehunter the badger and Nikabrik the dwarf, adding layers of complexity and intrigue. The tagline, “Everything you know is about to change forever,” rings true as the Pevensies face a new threat in King Miraz and navigate shifting alliances. Andrew Adamson’s direction keeps the pace brisk, and the blend of practical and CGI effects holds up well, even if the story occasionally leans on familiar fantasy tropes without much subversion.

Heads up for folks sensitive to animal-related content—this film is packed with it. There are multiple instances of animals dying, including a dog, horse, cat, and even a dragon, alongside scenes of animal abuse and suffering. Those who pin the “animal harm” or “non-human character dies” triggers should be cautious, as these moments are woven into the story’s darker, more violent turns. Plus, if bugs, spiders, or snakes make you uneasy, they show up too.
emailReview:
Prince Caspian dives into darker, battle-driven fantasy with a strong ensemble cast and a mix of practical and CGI effects that bring both new creatures and familiar Narnian magic to life.

Be prepared for: multiple animal deaths including a dog and dragon, animal abuse, and unsettling appearances by bugs, spiders, and snakes.

writers: Tom J. Astle, Matt Ember, Mel Brooks, Buck Henry
name: Get Smart
overview: When the identities of secret agents from Control are compromised, the Chief promotes hapless but eager analyst Maxwell Smart and teams him with stylish, capable Agent 99, the only spy whose cover remains intact. Can they work together to thwart the evil plans of KAOS and its crafty operative?

writers: Josh Goldsmith, Cathy Yuspa, Diane Drake
name: What Women Want
overview: Advertising executive Nick Marshall is as cocky as they come, but what happens to a chauvinistic guy when he can suddenly hear what women are thinking? Nick gets passed over for a promotion, but after an accident enables him to hear women's thoughts, he puts his newfound talent to work against Darcy, his new boss, who seems to be infatuated with him.
tagline: He has the power to hear everything women are thinking. Finally... a man is listening.

writers: Cinco Paul, Ken Daurio, Brian Lynch
name: The Secret Life of Pets
overview: The quiet life of a terrier named Max is upended when his owner takes in Duke, a stray whom Max instantly dislikes.
tagline: Ever wonder what your pets do when you're not home?

name: Space Jam
overview: Swackhammer, an evil alien theme park owner, needs a new attraction at Moron Mountain. When his gang, the Nerdlucks, heads to Earth to kidnap Bugs Bunny and the Looney Tunes, Bugs challenges them to a basketball game to determine their fate. The aliens agree, but they steal the powers of NBA basketball players, including Larry Bird and Charles Barkley -- so Bugs gets some help from superstar Michael Jordan.

primaryTitle: Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny
writers: Jez Butterworth, John-Henry Butterworth, David Koepp, James Mangold, George Lucas, Philip Kaufman

name: Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny
cleanNameArticles: indiana jones and the dial of destiny
overview:
Fifth film in the Indiana Jones franchise.

Finding himself in a new era, and approaching retirement, Indy wrestles with fitting into a world that seems to have outgrown him. But as the tentacles of an all-too-familiar evil return in the form of an old rival, Indy must don his hat and pick up his whip once more to make sure an ancient and powerful artifact doesn't fall into the wrong hands.
tagline: A legend will face his destiny.

name: Smile
overview:
Feature length remake of the 2020 Horror Short film, Laura Hasn’t Slept, also written/directed by Parker Finn.

After witnessing a bizarre, traumatic incident involving a patient, Dr. Rose Cotter starts experiencing frightening occurrences that she can't explain.
tagline: Once you see it, it's too late.

name: Air Force One
overview: Russian terrorists conspire to hijack the aircraft with the president and his family on board. The commander in chief finds himself facing an impossible predicament: give in to the terrorists and sacrifice his family, or risk everything to uphold his principles - and the integrity of the nation.
tagline: The fate of the nation rests on the courage of one man.

name: Secret Window
overview: Mort Rainey, a writer just emerging from a painful divorce with his ex-wife, is stalked at his remote lake house by a psychotic stranger and would-be scribe who claims Rainey swiped his best story idea. But as Rainey endeavors to prove his innocence, he begins to question his own sanity.
tagline: The most important part of a story is the ending.

name: X
overview: In 1979, a group of young filmmakers set out to make an adult film in rural Texas, but when their reclusive, elderly hosts catch them in the act, the cast find themselves fighting for their lives.
tagline: Dying to show you a good time.
review:
X is a grim, grindhouse-tinged horror that feels like a twisted mash-up of The Texas Chainsaw Massacre and Boogie Nights, with a dash of ’70s sleaze. Ti West leans hard into the slow-burn tension before unleashing some genuinely brutal horror moments, making it a standout in the recent wave of retro-inspired slashers. Mia Goth’s dual role as Maxine and Pearl is a highlight, delivering both vulnerability and menace with chilling precision. While it’s not exactly subtle, the film’s blend of dark humor and ruthless violence elevates it above your average backwoods horror flick.

What really sticks with you about X is how it uses its tagline—“Dying to show you a good time”—as both a cheeky wink and a grim promise. The setup of young filmmakers trying to shoot an adult film in rural Texas feels like a fresh twist on the “outsiders in a hostile environment” trope, and the tension ratchets up as their reclusive hosts reveal deadly intentions. The vintage aesthetic and synth-heavy score add to the creeping dread, while the performances keep the stakes feeling real. It’s a brutal, unapologetic film that doesn’t shy away from gore or discomfort, making its commentary on exploitation and ambition all the more biting.

Be heavily warned if animal harm is on your list—this one features multiple upsetting scenes involving pets and wildlife, including death and abuse that are hard to shake. Spider, snake, and bug phobias will also flare up, and there’s some body horror that’s rough around the edges. Plus, the film doesn’t hold back on disturbing imagery and uncomfortable power dynamics, so those sensitive to those elements should approach with caution.
emailReview:
X is a grim, grindhouse-tinged horror with a ’70s sleaze vibe, anchored by Mia Goth’s chilling dual performance and a slow-burn tension that explodes into brutal violence.

Be prepared for: multiple upsetting animal deaths and abuse, spider and snake phobias, rough body horror, and disturbing power dynamics.

name: Tomorrow Never Dies
overview: A deranged media mogul is staging international incidents to pit the world’s superpowers against each other. Now 007 must take on this evil mastermind in an adrenaline-charged battle to end his reign of terror and prevent global pandemonium.
tagline: Yesterday is a memory. Today is history. Tomorrow is in the hands of one man.

writers: Fede Alvarez, Rodo Sayagues, Sam Raimi
name: Evil Dead
overview:
Remake of the 1981 Sam Raimi classic.

Mia, a young woman struggling with sobriety, heads to a remote cabin with a group of friends where the discovery of a Book of the Dead unwittingly summon up dormant demons which possess the youngsters one-by-one.
tagline: The most terrifying film you will ever experience.
review:
Evil Dead (2013) is a brutal, relentless horror remake that leans fully into the gore and terror without much of the camp that made the original ’81 Sam Raimi classic a cult hit. If you’re a fan of modern, ultra-violent supernatural horror like *The Babadook* meets *Hereditary* on steroids, this one’s a wild ride—no punches pulled, no mercy given. Jane Levy’s Mia anchors the film as a heroin addict trying to get clean in a remote cabin, which quickly turns into a nightmare of demonic possession and grisly mayhem. It’s not as sly or funny as the original, but Fede Álvarez’s direction keeps the tension taut and the scares frequent.

What’s most striking here is how the film marries raw, visceral body horror with the psychological torment of addiction and withdrawal. The tagline, “The most terrifying film you will ever experience,” isn’t hyperbole: the movie definitely lives up to that promise with some truly harrowing scenes of possession, brutal violence, and graphic mutilation. The use of shaky cam throughout adds to the disorienting, claustrophobic feel, pulling you right into Mia’s spiraling hell. The practical effects and gore are impressively unapologetic, with plenty of sickening close-ups, from severed limbs to grotesque possession-induced self-harm. The film doesn’t shy away from pushing boundaries, whether it’s with shocking sexual assault, animal cruelty, or relentless jump scares.

That said, this is not a horror movie for the faint of heart or those sensitive to extreme content. Those who pin the sexual assault, graphic gore, and possession triggers should be very cautious. The film also features intense scenes of restraint, choking, self-harm, and animal death, including multiple dead cats shown in disturbing detail. There’s also heavy use of loud noises, flashing lights, and shaky cam, which could be overwhelming for some. If you’re looking for a relentless, unapologetically grim horror experience, *Evil Dead* delivers—but it’s a brutal one.
emailReview:
Evil Dead (2013) is an unflinching, ultra-violent horror remake that ditches camp for raw, relentless terror anchored by Jane Levy’s gripping portrayal of addiction and possession.

Be prepared for: graphic mutilation, disturbing animal deaths including multiple cats, shocking sexual assault, and intense scenes of self-harm and choking.

name: The Girl On the Train
overview: Rachel Watson, devastated by her recent divorce, spends her daily commute fantasizing about the seemingly perfect couple who live in a house that her train passes every day, until one morning she sees something shocking happen there and becomes entangled in the mystery that unfolds.
tagline: What you see can hurt you.

name: Idiocracy
overview: To test its top-secret Human Hibernation Project, the Pentagon picks the most average Americans it can find - an Army private and a prostitute - and sends them to the year 2505 after a series of freak events. But when they arrive, they find a civilization so dumbed-down that they're the smartest people around.
tagline: In the future, intelligence is extinct.

writers: Dan Hernandez, Benji Samit, Rob Letterman, Derek Connolly, Nicole Perlman, Satoshi Tajiri, Ken Sugimori, Jun'ichi Masuda, Hiroyuki Jinnai
name: Pokémon Detective Pikachu
overview: In a world where people collect pocket-size monsters (Pokémon) to do battle, a boy comes across an intelligent monster who seeks to be a detective.

writers: Peter Craig, Joe Carnahan, Chris Bremner, George Gallo
name: Bad Boys for Life
overview: Marcus and Mike are forced to confront new threats, career changes, and midlife crises as they join the newly created elite team AMMO of the Miami police department to take down the ruthless Armando Armas, the vicious leader of a Miami drug cartel.

writers: David Morrell, Kevin Jarre, Sylvester Stallone, James Cameron
name: Rambo: First Blood Part II
overview: John Rambo is released from prison by the government for a top-secret covert mission to the last place on Earth he'd want to return - the jungles of Vietnam.
tagline: No man, no law, no war can stop him.
review:
Rambo: First Blood Part II is the quintessential ’80s action sequel, cranking up the intensity and patriotism to full volume. If you liked the original’s gritty, somewhat somber tone, this one trades subtlety for straight-up explosive showdowns and one-man-army bravado. It’s basically Rambo meets Rambo, but with bigger explosions and a more pronounced “war hero” vibe. Fans of vintage action flicks and Stallone’s muscle-bound persona will find plenty to chew on here, even if the plot is pretty by-the-numbers.

What stands out is the film’s unapologetic embrace of Cold War-era machismo, with Stallone’s John Rambo sent back to the hostile jungles of Vietnam on a covert mission that’s as much about revenge as it is rescue. The tagline, “No man, no law, no war can stop him,” nails the tone perfectly—this is Rambo at his most unstoppable. The supporting cast, including Richard Crenna as the grizzled Colonel Trautman, adds some grounding, but ultimately it’s the relentless action sequences and the pulsing, tense score that drive the movie forward. Director George P. Cosmatos keeps the pace brisk, and the screenplay (with input from James Cameron, no less) balances the spectacle with just enough character moments to keep it from feeling like a mindless shoot-’em-up.

Heads up for animal lovers: this one doesn’t shy away from some tough stuff involving animals, including dog fighting and the death of pets and other creatures. If you have triggers around animal harm or death, be warned that there are multiple scenes where this comes into play and can be pretty upsetting. The jungle setting also brings in a handful of creepy crawlies and dangerous wildlife, so anyone sensitive to snakes, spiders, or other critters should tread carefully.
emailReview:
Rambo: First Blood Part II turns up the volume on ’80s action with Stallone’s muscle-bound Rambo unstoppable in explosive jungle showdowns and high-octane patriotism.

Be prepared for: dog fighting, death of pets, snake encounters, spider scenes, and intense animal harm.

primaryTitle: Zack and Miri Make a Porno
Title_IMDb_Link: Zack and Miri Make a Porno
name: Zack and Miri Make a Porno
cleanNameArticles: zack and miri make a porno
overview: Lifelong platonic friends Zack and Miri look to solve their respective cash-flow problems by making an adult film together. As the cameras roll, however, the duo begin to sense that they may have more feelings for each other than they previously thought.
tagline: What would you do to get out of debt?

name: Road Trip
overview: After a student at the University of Ithaca films his one-night stand with a beautiful sorority girl, he discovers one of his friends has accidentally mailed the homemade sex tape to his girlfriend in Austin. In a frenzy, he must borrow a car and hit the road in a desperate bid to intercept the tape.
tagline: The greatest college tradition of all.
review:
Road Trip is the kind of late-'90s/early-2000s college comedy that’s equal parts raunchy and ridiculous, riding the wave of frat-house farce but with a little more charm thanks to Todd Phillips’ knack for zany setups. Think American Pie meets The Hangover’s earlier, more innocent cousin. Breckin Meyer leads a solid ensemble cast, including Seann William Scott and Amy Smart, through a madcap race to stop a sex tape disaster that’s both embarrassing and hilarious in equal measure. It’s not exactly high art, but it’s got enough goofy energy and memorable moments to earn its place among the cult classics of its era.

What really stands out is the film’s commitment to the absurdity of its premise — a desperate cross-country chase sparked by a tragically misplaced homemade tape. The writing leans heavily into the awkwardness of early-2000s college life, and the dialogue is peppered with that era’s brand of crude humor, which might feel dated or tame depending on your taste. The tagline, “The greatest college tradition of all,” nails the tone perfectly: this is a film that revels in the chaos and stupidity of youth. And while the story is pretty straightforward, the chemistry among the cast brings a little life to the predictable beats.

Be warned if you’re sensitive to animal-related content: this movie has a heavy dose of animal harm, including the death of multiple animals (dogs, cats, horses), scenes of abuse, and even dog fighting. These elements are surprisingly prominent and might catch viewers off guard amid the comedy. If animal safety is a big concern for you, this one comes with a serious caution.
emailReview:
Road Trip delivers a goofy, chaotic blast of early-2000s college comedy with a cast that turns frat-house farce into a surprisingly charming romp.

Be prepared for: multiple animal deaths including dogs and horses, scenes of animal abuse, and dog fighting.

name: The Perfect Storm
overview: In October 1991, a confluence of weather conditions combined to form a killer storm in the North Atlantic. Caught in the storm was the sword-fishing boat Andrea Gail. Magnificent foreshadowing and anticipation fill this true-life drama while minute details of the fishing boats, their gear and the weather are juxtaposed with the sea adventure.

writers: Pat Casey, Josh Miller, Yuji Naka, Naoto Ohshima, Hirokazu Yasuhara
name: Sonic the Hedgehog
overview: Powered with incredible speed, Sonic The Hedgehog embraces his new home on Earth. That is, until Sonic sparks the attention of super-uncool evil genius Dr. Robotnik. Now it’s super-villain vs. super-sonic in an all-out race across the globe to stop Robotnik from using Sonic’s unique power for world domination.
tagline: A whole new speed of hero.
review:
Sonic the Hedgehog is a family-friendly live-action adventure comedy that feels like a mash-up of classic buddy movies and video game nostalgia. It’s got the speedy, quirky energy of the original Sega game, wrapped up in a bright, goofy package that leans heavily on Jim Carrey’s manic charm as the villainous Dr. Robotnik. While it doesn’t break much new ground, it’s a solid crowd-pleaser that’s more enjoyable than your average video game adaptation—fans of lighthearted action and goofy humor will find plenty to like here.

The real highlight is the chemistry between Sonic (voiced by Ben Schwartz) and his human sidekick Tom (James Marsden), which helps ground the film’s more outlandish moments. The story’s straightforward: Sonic finds a home on Earth and must stop Robotnik’s world domination plans, but the film’s upbeat tone and colorful visuals keep things moving fast—just like Sonic himself. The tagline, “A whole new speed of hero,” fits the film’s energetic vibe, and the humor leans into slapstick and pop culture references, which might not be everyone’s cup of tea but generally lands well.

Heads up to those sensitive to death and intense moments: Sonic includes multiple instances of character deaths (including a kid and a parent), and there are a few jump scares and scenes involving fire that could be unsettling. Additionally, there’s some mild gore and gun violence sprinkled throughout, so if those are on your list, be prepared. Despite its family-friendly facade, it’s not entirely free of darker beats.
emailReview:
Sonic the Hedgehog zips through a bright, goofy adventure packed with Jim Carrey’s manic villainy and a charming buddy dynamic that keeps the energy buzzing.

Be prepared for: character deaths including a kid and a parent, jump scares, scenes with fire, mild gore, and gun violence.

writers: Mark L. Smith, Joseph Kosinski, Michael Crichton, Anne-Marie Martin
name: Twisters
overview: As storm season intensifies, the paths of former storm chaser Kate Carter and reckless social-media superstar Tyler Owens collide when terrifying phenomena never seen before are unleashed. The pair and their competing teams find themselves squarely in the paths of multiple storm systems converging over central Oklahoma in the fight of their lives.

writers: John Carpenter, Debra Hill, Jeff Fradley, Danny McBride, David Gordon Green
name: Halloween
overview: Laurie Strode comes to her final confrontation with Michael Myers, the masked figure who has haunted her since she narrowly escaped his killing spree on Halloween night four decades ago.
tagline: You don't believe in the Boogeyman? You should.
review:
Halloween (2018) is a solid return to form for the slasher genre, blending old-school chills with a modern sensibility. Jamie Lee Curtis is back as Laurie Strode, facing off against Michael Myers in what’s billed as their final showdown. It’s kind of like John Carpenter’s original meets a contemporary thriller — familiar enough to please fans but with enough fresh tension to avoid feeling like a retread. If you’re into haunted survivor stories and relentless masked killers, this one hits the mark without reinventing the wheel.

What stands out here is the way the film leans into Laurie’s trauma, aging her into a battle-hardened warrior rather than just a scream queen. The writing by David Gordon Green and Danny McBride gives her more depth than your typical horror protagonist, and the tension is amped up by a creeping score and some tight, claustrophobic visuals. The tagline, “You don’t believe in the Boogeyman? You should,” nails the persistent dread that runs through the film. There’s a real sense of legacy and reckoning, which elevates it above your average slasher fare.

Heads up for animal lovers: this one is heavy on animal-related content that might be upsetting. There are multiple instances of animal deaths, including a dog, a horse, and a cat, plus some animal abuse and even dog fighting. If those kinds of scenes are on your no-watch list, prepare yourself accordingly.
emailReview:
Halloween (2018) is a tense, atmospheric slasher that balances vintage chills with fresh emotional depth, anchored by Jamie Lee Curtis’s fierce return as a trauma-hardened Laurie Strode.

Be prepared for: multiple animal deaths including dog, horse, and cat, animal abuse, and dog fighting.

name: The Mechanic
overview: Arthur Bishop is a 'mechanic' - an elite assassin with a strict code and unique talent for cleanly eliminating targets. It's a job that requires professional perfection and total detachment, and Bishop is the best in the business. But when he is ordered to take out his mentor and close friend Harry, Bishop is anything but detached.
tagline: Someone has to fix the problems.

name: Carry-On
overview: An airport security officer races to outsmart a mysterious traveler forcing him to let a dangerous item slip onto a Christmas Eve flight.
tagline: Every holiday season, millions travel safely by air. This Christmas will be different.
review:
Carry-On lands squarely in the high-stakes thriller zone, with Taron Egerton stepping up as a sharp, resourceful airport security officer caught in a tense Christmas Eve game of cat and mouse. It’s got that familiar pulse of a Jaume Collet-Serra film—think non-stop momentum and claustrophobic tension—mixed with a holiday backdrop that injects a fresh twist into the genre. Jason Bateman’s mysterious traveler adds a layer of menace that keeps things unpredictable, even if the premise doesn’t exactly reinvent the wheel.

What makes Carry-On work is its slick pacing and the way it leans into the anxiety of modern air travel, amplified by the looming holiday rush. The script by T.J. Fixman keeps the stakes personal and immediate, and the confined airport setting is used to good effect, cranking up the pressure as the clock ticks down to takeoff. Sofia Carson and Danielle Deadwyler provide solid support, rounding out a cast that grounds the film’s more outlandish thriller beats in believable human reactions. The tagline—“Every holiday season, millions travel safely by air. This Christmas will be different.”—really nails that uneasy blend of everyday normalcy and looming disaster.

On the trigger front, Carry-On is surprisingly light. Despite the tense setup, there are no animal deaths or harm, and definitely no dragons or bugs creeping around to freak you out. So if you’re sensitive to violence or suspense, be aware this movie leans into those, but it won’t blindside you with unexpected cruelty toward animals or weird fantasy elements.
emailReview:
Carry-On delivers a taut holiday thriller with Taron Egerton’s sharp performance and a claustrophobic airport setting that keeps the tension cranked to the max.

Be prepared for: tense suspense, intense airport security confrontations, and escalating violence in confined spaces.

tagline: Walk down the right back alley in Sin City and you can find anything...

writers: Danny McBride, Dirk Blackman, Howard McCain, Len Wiseman, Robert Orr, Kevin Grevioux
name: Underworld: Rise of the Lycans
overview: A prequel to the first two Underworld films, this fantasy explains the origins of the feud between the Vampires and the Lycans. Aided by his secret love, Sonja, courageous Lucian leads the Lycans in battle against brutal Vampire king Viktor. Determined to break the king's enslavement of his people, Lucian faces off against the Death Dealer army in a bid for Lycan independence.

writers: Zak Penn, Adam Leff, Shane Black, David Arnott
name: Last Action Hero
overview: Danny is obsessed with a fictional movie character action hero Jack Slater. When a magical ticket transports him into Jack's latest adventure, Danny finds himself in a world where movie magic and reality collide. Now it's up to Danny to save the life of his hero and new friend.
review:
Last Action Hero is a 90s action-comedy mashup that tries to have its cake and eat it too—part meta satire, part Arnold Schwarzenegger musclefest. It’s a curious beast, feeling like Die Hard meets The Purple Rose of Cairo, with a dash of Shane Black’s snark in the mix. While it doesn’t quite hit the heights of classic Schwarzenegger action flicks, its playful breaking of the fourth wall and the fish-out-of-water story give it enough charm to remain a cult favorite rather than just a forgotten blockbuster.

What really stands out is the concept itself: a kid literally stepping into the movie world of his favorite hero, Jack Slater. This lets the film toy with genre tropes and poke fun at action clichés while still delivering the expected explosions and one-liners. The tagline, “This isn’t the movies anymore,” perfectly captures the film’s self-aware tone, even if the blend of fantasy and action occasionally feels uneven. The writing teams Shane Black and Zak Penn bring their trademark sharpness, though the film’s ambition sometimes outpaces its execution. Still, Arnold’s larger-than-life presence keeps it grounded in that classic action vibe, and Austin O’Brien’s wide-eyed Danny adds a kid-friendly heart to the chaos.

Heads up for animal-sensitive viewers: Last Action Hero is notorious on DoesTheDogDie for multiple animal-related triggers—including the death of a dog, cat, horse, and other animals, along with scenes of animal abuse and dog fighting. If you’re on the lookout for those, this movie has more of that than your average 90s action flick, so proceed with caution.
emailReview:
Last Action Hero is a quirky 90s action-comedy that combines Arnold Schwarzenegger's muscle with sharp meta satire and playful genre-bending, making it a cult classic with a kid-friendly heart and plenty of snark.

Be prepared for: dog fighting, multiple animal deaths including a dog, cat, and horse, and scenes of animal abuse.

directors: Eric Darnell, Tim Johnson, Lawrence Guterman
writers: Todd Alcott, Chris Weitz, Paul Weitz
name: Antz
overview: A neurotic worker ant in love with a rebellious princess rises to unlikely stardom when he switches places with a soldier. Signing up to march in a parade, he ends up under the command of a bloodthirsty general. But he's actually been enlisted to fight against a termite army.
tagline: See the world from a whole new perspective.

name: Crimson Peak
overview: In the aftermath of a family tragedy, an aspiring author is torn between love for her childhood friend and the temptation of a mysterious outsider. Trying to escape the ghosts of her past, she is swept away to a house that breathes, bleeds… and remembers.
tagline: Love makes monsters of us all.

name: Annabelle Creation
overview: Several years after the tragic death of their little girl, a doll maker and his wife welcome a nun and several girls from a shuttered orphanage into their home, soon becoming the target of the doll maker's possessed creation—Annabelle.
tagline: You don't know the real story.

name: Evil Dead Rise
overview: A reunion between two estranged sisters gets cut short by the rise of flesh-possessing demons, thrusting them into a primal battle for survival as they face the most nightmarish version of family imaginable.

writers: Rob McKittrick, Mark Steilen, Russell Adams
name: Tag
overview: For one month every year, five highly competitive friends hit the ground running in a no-holds-barred game of tag they’ve been playing since the first grade. This year, the game coincides with the wedding of their only undefeated player, which should finally make him an easy target. But he knows they’re coming...and he’s ready.
tagline: We don't stop playing because we grow old, we grow old because we stop playing.
review:
Tag is a surprisingly entertaining comedy-thriller hybrid that leans into the absurdity of a lifelong game of tag played with almost militaristic intensity. It’s like The Hangover meets a low-stakes Mission: Impossible, with a crew of competitive grown-ups refusing to let go of childhood rituals. The cast—Ed Helms, Jon Hamm, Jeremy Renner, Jake Johnson, and Hannibal Buress—bring a solid mix of charm and goofiness that keeps the movie from ever feeling too silly or too serious, striking a nice balance that fans of buddy comedies will appreciate.

What stands out is how the premise—a no-holds-barred tag game during one frenetic month each year—transforms into a full-on chase caper with surprisingly creative set pieces. The tagline, “We don't stop playing because we grow old, we grow old because we stop playing,” nails the theme of friendship and refusing to grow up. The wedding of the undefeated player adds a nice ticking clock element, and the film manages to stay fresh by subverting the standard sports or competition movie tropes with its sheer ridiculousness and heart.

Heads up for those sensitive to animal death and some darker moments: the film includes a dog dying, a child dying, and even someone being burned alive—definitely not what you’d expect from a comedy about tag. Plus, there are jump scares and flashing lights that might catch you off guard. So if you’re skittish about those heavier triggers, tread carefully. Otherwise, it’s a wild, surprisingly heartfelt ride about friendship, competition, and never quite growing up.
emailReview:
Tag turns a simple childhood game into a high-octane comedy-thriller with a stellar cast that balances goofiness and charm, making the absurdity of lifelong competition oddly touching and entertaining.

Be prepared for: a dog dying, a child dying, someone burned alive, jump scares, and flashing lights.

name: Triple Frontier
overview: Struggling to make ends meet, former special ops soldiers reunite for a high-stakes heist: stealing $75 million from a South American drug lord.

name: Blended
overview: After a bad blind date, a man and woman find themselves stuck together at a resort for families, where their attractions grows as their respective kids benefit from the burgeoning relationship.
tagline: Single dad, no clue. Single mom, flying solo.

writers: John Long, Michael France, Sylvester Stallone
name: Cliffhanger
overview: A year after losing his friend in a tragic 4,000-foot fall, former ranger Gabe Walker and his partner, Hal, are called to return to the same peak to rescue a group of stranded climbers, only to learn the climbers are actually thieving hijackers who are looking for boxes full of money.
review:
Cliffhanger is peak early-90s action thriller—a Sylvester Stallone-led adrenaline rush that feels like Die Hard meets vertical rock climbing. It’s loud, brash, and unapologetically cheesy, but that’s part of the charm. Director Renny Harlin knows how to stage jaw-dropping set pieces, and Stallone’s gruff, rugged presence anchors what could otherwise be a standard “mountain hostage” flick. Fans of high-stakes, physical action with a hint of brooding guilt will find a lot to like here, even if it doesn’t reinvent the genre.

What really stands out are the vertigo-inducing visuals and the tight pacing. The tagline, “Hang on,” isn’t just a cute pun—it sums up the tension of the film’s main premise, with every climb and rescue attempt ratcheting up the stakes. The twist that the stranded climbers are actually hijackers looking for a fortune adds a nice layer of deceit and danger, mixing survival with classic heist elements. The cast, including John Lithgow as the sinister villain Qualen and Michael Rooker as Stallone’s loyal partner Hal, bring solid performances that keep the story engaging beyond the physical spectacle.

Those who pin the “someone falls to their death” trigger should brace themselves, as the film opens with a devastating fatal fall that haunts the protagonist. Additionally, be warned if gun violence, animal death, or jump scares are on your list—there’s no shortage of bullets flying, a dog dying, and sudden moments meant to startle. Burning alive and finger mutilation are also present, which might be a bit much for sensitive viewers. In short, Cliffhanger delivers on its promise of high-altitude thrills but comes with a fair share of heavy content.
emailReview:
Cliffhanger is a loud, brash early-90s action thriller that combines vertigo-inducing mountain climbs with a gritty heist twist, anchored by Sylvester Stallone’s rugged charm and some truly jaw-dropping set pieces.

Be prepared for: fatal falls, gun violence, a dog dying, burning alive, and finger mutilation.

name: Nerve
overview: Industrious high school senior, Vee Delmonico, has had it with living life on the sidelines. When pressured by friends to join the popular online game Nerve, Vee decides to sign up for just one dare in what seems like harmless fun. But as she finds herself caught up in the thrill of the adrenaline-fueled competition partnered with a mysterious stranger, the game begins to take a sinister turn with increasingly dangerous acts, leading her into a high stakes finale that will determine her entire future.

primaryTitle: Harold & Kumar Escape from Guantanamo Bay
Title_IMDb_Link: Harold & Kumar Escape from Guantanamo Bay
name: Harold & Kumar Escape From Guantanamo Bay

cleanNameArticles: harold and kumar escape from guantanamo bay
overview: Having satisfied their urge for White Castle, Harold and Kumar jump on a plane to catch up with Harold's love interest, who's headed for the Netherlands. But the pair must change their plans when Kumar is accused of being a terrorist. Rob Corddry also stars in this wild comedy sequel that follows the hapless stoners' misadventures as they try to avoid being captured by the Department of Homeland Security.
tagline: This time they're running from the joint.
review:
Harold & Kumar Escape From Guantanamo Bay is a wild, ridiculous stoner comedy that doubles down on the absurdity and social satire of its predecessor. If you dug the first Harold & Kumar’s mix of buddy hijinks and sharp cultural riffs, this sequel cranks it up by tossing the duo into an over-the-top manhunt with Homeland Security. It’s like a less polished, raunchier version of a road trip comedy meets a political farce—equal parts goofy and pointed, though not always as tight as it could be.

The film shines when it leans into its outrageous scenarios and the chemistry between John Cho and Kal Penn, who keep the jokes flying even as the plot barrels into some pretty outlandish territory. The tagline, “This time they’re running from the joint,” sets the tone for a sequel that’s unapologetically silly but still manages to poke fun at post-9/11 paranoia and racial profiling. Rob Corddry’s presence adds a nice dose of manic energy, and Neil Patrick Harris continues to steal scenes with his self-aware cameo. While the humor can be hit-or-miss, the movie’s willingness to push boundaries and its blend of slapstick with social commentary make it a memorable ride.

Heads up to anyone sensitive to animal-related content: this one packs a punch with multiple instances of animal harm, including dog fighting, rabbits being hurt, and pets dying. The animal triggers are heavy enough that if you cringe at scenes involving animal suffering, you’ll want to brace yourself here.
emailReview:
Harold & Kumar Escape From Guantanamo Bay is a raunchy, over-the-top stoner comedy that blends buddy hijinks with sharp social satire, boosted by the lively chemistry of John Cho and Kal Penn and a manic Rob Corddry.

Be prepared for: dog fighting, rabbits being hurt, pets dying, and scenes of animal suffering that hit hard amid the chaos.

name: Life As We Know It
overview: After a disastrous first date for caterer Holly and network sports director Messer, all they have in common is a dislike for each other and their love for their goddaughter Sophie. But when they suddenly become all Sophie has in this world, Holly and Messer must set their differences aside. Juggling careers and social calendars, they'll have to find common ground while living under the same roof.
tagline: A comedy about taking it one step at a time.

name: Antichrist
overview: A grieving couple retreats to their cabin 'Eden' in the woods, hoping to repair their broken hearts and troubled marriage. But nature takes its course and things go from bad to worse.
review:
Lars von Trier’s *Antichrist* is a grim, unflinching dive into grief and chaos that feels like a brutal art-horror cocktail—think *The Evil Dead* meets psychological nightmare, but with a heavy dose of existential dread. It’s not for the faint of heart or those expecting a traditional horror flick. Willem Dafoe and Charlotte Gainsbourg anchor the film with raw performances that make you squirm and sympathize simultaneously, even as the story spirals into madness. This one’s definitely a wild ride, elevated by von Trier’s stark visuals and his willingness to go places most directors wouldn’t dare.

What stands out most is the film’s use of nature as an almost malevolent force—as the tagline “Chaos reigns” suggests, the woods around their cabin are not just a backdrop but a character in itself. The film explores grief, trauma, and the breakdown of a relationship with a brutal honesty that’s as poetic as it is disturbing. The sparse dialogue and haunting score amplify the sense of dread, making every frame feel heavy with meaning. It’s a tough watch, but the way it leans into genre conventions only to twist them into something deeply unsettling feels very von Trier.

Be heavily warned if animal harm or death is on your list—*Antichrist* features multiple instances of animal suffering and death, including dogs, horses, cats, and more, with some scenes reportedly involving real harm during filming. Anyone sensitive to animal abuse or death should approach with extreme caution.
emailReview:
Lars von Trier’s *Antichrist* is a harrowing art-horror experience that blends raw, unflinching performances with a malevolent natural world that feels almost alive in its cruelty.

Be prepared for: graphic animal deaths including dogs and horses, intense scenes of animal abuse, and a psychological descent into madness that spares no brutality.

name: Homefront
overview: Phil Broker, a retired DEA agent, leads a quiet life with his daughter Maddy, until a school bullying incident draws them into a conflict with Morgan “Gator” Bodine, a local crime boss.
tagline: How far would you go to protect your home?

tagline: Some games you play. Some you survive.

name: J. Edgar
overview: As the face of law enforcement in the United States for almost 50 years, J. Edgar Hoover was feared and admired, reviled and revered. But behind closed doors, he held secrets that would have destroyed his image, his career, and his life.

writers: Scott Kosar, Ray Wright, George A. Romero
name: The Crazies
overview: Four friends find themselves trapped in their small hometown after they discover their friends and neighbors going quickly and horrifically insane.

name: A Haunting in Venice

name: Step Up
overview: Everyone deserves a chance to follow their dreams, but some people only get one shot. Tyler Gage is a rebel from the wrong side of Baltimore's tracks and the only thing that stands between him and an unfulfilled life are his dreams of one day making it out of there. Nora is a privileged ballet dancer attending Baltimore's ultra-elite Maryland School of the Arts
tagline: Every second chance begins with a first step.

writers: Tom Clancy, Paul Attanasio, Daniel Pyne
name: The Sum of All Fears
overview: When the president of Russia suddenly dies, a man whose politics are virtually unknown succeeds him. The change in political leaders sparks paranoia among American CIA officials, so CIA director Bill Cabot recruits a young analyst to supply insight and advice on the situation. Then the unthinkable happens: a nuclear bomb explodes in a U.S. city, and America is quick to blame the Russians.

name: A Walk Among the Tombstones
overview: Private investigator Matthew Scudder is hired by a drug kingpin to find out who kidnapped and murdered his wife.
tagline: Some people are afraid of all the wrong things.

name: Skeleton Key
overview: A hospice nurse working at a spooky New Orleans plantation home finds herself entangled in a mystery involving the house's dark past.

name: Marie Antoinette
overview: The retelling of France's iconic but ill-fated queen, Marie Antoinette. From her betrothal and marriage to Louis XVI at 15 to her reign as queen at 19 and ultimately the fall of Versailles.

name: Rat Race
overview: In an ensemble film about easy money, greed, manipulation and bad driving, a Las Vegas casino tycoon entertains his wealthiest high rollers -- a group that will bet on anything -- by pitting six ordinary people against each other in a wild dash for $2 million jammed into a locker hundreds of miles away. The tycoon and his wealthy friends monitor each racer's every move to keep track of their favorites. The only rule in this race is that there are no rules.

name: Safe
overview: After a former elite agent rescues a 12-year-old Chinese girl who's been abducted, they find themselves in the middle of a standoff between Triads, the Russian Mafia and high-level corrupt New York City politicians and police.

name: Premium Rush
overview: In Manhattan, a bike messenger picks up an envelope that attracts the interest of a dirty cop, who pursues the cyclist throughout the city.

writers: Pat Proft, David Zucker, Robert LoCash, Jim Abrahams, Jerry Zucker
name: Naked Gun 33⅓: The Final Insult
overview: Frank Drebin is persuaded out of retirement to go undercover in a state prison. There he is to find out what top terrorist, Rocco, has planned for when he escapes. Frank's wife, Jane, is desperate for a baby.. this adds to Frank's problems. A host of celebrities at the Academy awards ceremony are humiliated by Frank as he blunders his way trying to foil Rocco.
review:
Naked Gun 33⅓: The Final Insult sticks to the classic slapstick formula that made the original films cult favorites, but it doesn’t quite hit the same high notes. Leslie Nielsen’s deadpan Lt. Frank Drebin remains the comedic anchor here, bumbling through an absurd undercover prison mission and a chaotic Academy Awards setting. If you’re a fan of the original Naked Gun movies or the Airplane!-style spoofs from the Zucker, Abrahams, and Zucker team, this one feels like a familiar if slightly tired reunion. It’s got the goofy gags and celebrity cameos, but some of the jokes land with less punch than you might hope.

What stands out is the film’s willingness to throw everything at the wall—prison shenanigans, terrorist plots, desperate attempts at baby-making, and a parade of slapstick humiliation at Hollywood’s biggest night. The tagline, “Mostly all new jokes,” is a cheeky nod to the franchise’s self-awareness, but the writing leans heavily on familiar tropes, and the humor sometimes feels more nostalgic than fresh. Still, Leslie Nielsen’s timing and the sheer ridiculousness of Frank Drebin’s antics keep it watchable. The blend of spoof and physical comedy delivers enough laughs to satisfy fans of the genre, even if it isn’t quite the “final insult” the title suggests.

Heads up for anyone sensitive to animal-related content: several animals meet unfortunate fates here, including a pigeon caught in a fan and other pet casualties, though the scenes are handled with cartoonish restraint and no graphic gore. There’s also some mild body horror, moments of choking, and a handful of creepy crawlies like spiders and snakes. If you’re triggered by animal harm or the presence of bugs, this one might be a rougher watch than expected.
emailReview:
Naked Gun 33⅓: The Final Insult delivers Leslie Nielsen’s classic deadpan comedy amid chaotic prison antics and a slapstick-filled Hollywood spoof, mixing nostalgia with absurd physical humor.

Be prepared for: cartoonish animal harm including a pigeon caught in a fan, mild body horror, choking scenes, and creepy crawlies like spiders and snakes.

name: Pet Sematary
overview: Dr. Louis Creed's family moves into the country house of their dreams and discover a pet cemetery at the back of their property. The cursed burial ground deep in the woods brings the dead back to life -- with "minor" problems. At first, only the family's cat makes the return trip, but an accident forces a heartbroken father to contemplate the unthinkable.

writers: Richard Maibaum, Tom Mankiewicz, Ian Fleming
name: Diamonds Are Forever
overview: Diamonds are stolen only to be sold again in the international market. James Bond infiltrates a smuggling mission to find out who's guilty. The mission takes him to Las Vegas where Bond meets his archenemy Blofeld.
tagline: The man who made 007 a household number.

writers: Tom J. Astle, Matt Ember, Adam Rex

name: The Craft
overview: A Catholic school newcomer falls in with a clique of teen witches who wield their powers against all who dare to cross them -- be they teachers, rivals or meddlesome parents.
review:
The Craft is a quintessential ’90s teen witch flick that’s equal parts moody high school drama and supernatural revenge fantasy. It’s like Heathers meets Buffy the Vampire Slayer with a dash of Salem witch trial vibes—dark, stylish, and a little campy. Robin Tunney leads a memorable cast, including a scene-stealing Fairuza Balk as the dangerously intense Nancy, giving the film an edge that’s kept it a cult classic decades later. While it leans into familiar tropes of outsider angst and teenage power struggles, the witchcraft angle adds a deliciously wicked twist.

What really stands out is how the film balances its eerie, mystical elements with the raw emotional turmoil of adolescence. The tagline “Welcome to the witching hour” nails it—there’s a constant tension between empowerment and the consequences of wielding that power recklessly. The Catholic school setting amps up the stakes, making the girls’ rebellion against authority both literal and symbolic. The writing doesn’t shy away from the darkness lurking beneath teenage envy and friendship, and the ’90s aesthetic, from wardrobe to soundtrack, adds a nostalgic charm that feels just right.

Heads up for anyone sensitive to emotional manipulation—gaslighting plays a noticeable role in the story, as the characters navigate trust and betrayal within their coven. It’s subtle but unsettling, so those who pin the gaslighting trigger should be cautious going in.
emailReview:
The Craft is a darkly stylish ’90s teen witch flick where moody high school drama meets supernatural revenge, anchored by Robin Tunney and a scene-stealing Fairuza Balk as the dangerously intense Nancy.

Be prepared for: emotional manipulation through gaslighting, tense scenes of teenage betrayal, and a haunting Catholic school backdrop that amps up the witchy rebellion.

overview: The Grinch hatches a scheme to ruin Christmas when the residents of Whoville plan their annual holiday celebration.

review:
The 2018 animated *The Grinch* leans into the holiday heist genre with a glossy, family-friendly sheen that feels like *How the Grinch Stole Christmas* meets a kid-friendly caper flick. Benedict Cumberbatch’s grumpy green voice work keeps the character lively, but the film doesn’t quite reach the mischievous heights of Jim Carrey’s live-action turn or the original Dr. Seuss special. It’s a pretty standard retelling, buoyed by a bright visual style and a few genuinely funny moments, though it sometimes plays it safe with its heartwarming message.

What stands out here is the film’s focus on the “heist before Christmas” angle, giving the Grinch’s sabotage a bit more narrative weight than just grumpy holiday stealing. The voice cast is solid, with Rashida Jones and Cameron Seely adding charm as the Whos, and Pharrell Williams’ narration adds a playful touch. The animation is crisp and colorful, leaning into the whimsical, snowy world of Whoville, but the story doesn’t stray far from familiar territory. It’s the kind of movie that feels cozy and predictable in equal measure—perfect for a casual holiday watch but unlikely to become a seasonal classic.

Heads up for animal lovers: this one’s notorious for its animal-related triggers. There’s a surprising amount of animal harm and death, including dogs, cats, horses, and even a dragon, plus some unsettling moments with spiders and snakes. If you’re sensitive to that sort of thing—or anything from animal abuse to pet deaths—you’ll want to proceed with caution.
emailReview:
The 2018 animated *The Grinch* offers a glossy, kid-friendly holiday heist with lively voice work and bright, whimsical animation, though it plays its heartwarming message a bit safe.

writers: Brian Lynch, Ken Daurio, Cinco Paul
name: The Secret Life of Pets 2
overview: Max the terrier must cope with some major life changes when his owner gets married and has a baby. When the family takes a trip to the countryside, nervous Max has numerous run-ins with canine-intolerant cows, hostile foxes and a scary turkey. Luckily for Max, he soon catches a break when he meets Rooster, a gruff farm dog who tries to cure the lovable pooch of his neuroses.
review:
The Secret Life of Pets 2 sticks close to the formula of its predecessor: a family-friendly animated romp with plenty of animal antics and goofy heart. It’s not reinventing the wheel here, but fans of the first film will appreciate the familiar mix of humor and mild adventure. The countryside setting and the introduction of Rooster, a tough farm dog, give it a bit of a “buddy road trip” vibe, which adds some fresh energy to the franchise’s usual city-bound chaos. It’s not as sharp or surprising as something like Zootopia, but it delivers what it promises—a lighthearted, visually bright comedy with a solid voice cast including Patton Oswalt and Kevin Hart.

What stands out most is how the film leans into Max’s anxieties as a way to explore themes of change and growing up, which is a nice touch for a kids’ movie. The tagline “They still have their secrets” hints at the pets’ hidden inner lives, and the screenplay by Brian Lynch makes good use of that to sneak in some genuine warmth beneath the punchlines and slapstick. The encounters with hostile farm animals and the gruff mentorship from Rooster provide a fun, if predictable, narrative arc. Visually, it’s polished and colorful, continuing the franchise’s knack for making fur and feathers feel delightfully fluffy and expressive.

Heads up for sensitive viewers: this one has a surprisingly heavy dose of animal death and abuse—dog fighting is depicted, along with the deaths of a dog, cat, horse, and even a dragon (in a fantasy sequence). Those who pin the animal harm or death triggers should be cautious going in, as these moments, while cartoonish, could be upsetting.
emailReview:
The Secret Life of Pets 2 keeps its bright, fluffy animation and humor while adding a countryside buddy-trip vibe that freshens up the familiar city chaos.

Be prepared for: dog fighting, the deaths of a dog, cat, horse, and even a dragon in a fantasy sequence.

name: IF

name: Revenge
overview: Jen's romantic getaway with her wealthy (married) boyfriend is disrupted when his friends arrive for an impromptu hunting trip. Tension mounts at the house until the situation culminates in an unexpected way.
tagline: Why do women always have to put up a fight?
review:
Revenge is a slick, brutal entry in the “female revenge thriller” subgenre that feels like a hyper-stylized mashup of Kill Bill’s relentless fury and The Strangers’ tense isolation. Matilda Lutz turns in a fierce performance as Jen, whose romantic trip swiftly spirals into a savage fight for survival—this isn’t your average getaway gone wrong. Coralie Fargeat’s sharp direction elevates the film beyond typical exploitation fare, mixing gorgeous visuals with a darkly feminist edge that challenges the usual victim narrative.

What really stands out here is how the movie leans into genre conventions only to twist them upside down. The tagline, “Why do women always have to put up a fight?” hints at that subversion, and the story delivers with inventive, often shocking moments that keep you on edge. The tension mounting among the men on a hunting trip turns into something far more primal and unsettling, and the film’s vivid, almost operatic violence feels like a comment on power and control rather than gratuitous gore. Plus, the use of the natural environment and the eerie atmosphere add a layer of dread that’s as much about the wilderness as it is about human cruelty.

If you’re sensitive to animal harm or death, be warned: this one doesn’t shy away from showing violence against animals, which is central enough to the story that it’s impossible to miss. Those who pin the “animal harm” and “animal death” triggers should approach with caution, as well as anyone put off by the presence of bugs and snakes that add to the film’s unsettling mood. Revenge is definitely not for the faint of heart, but if you’re up for a wild, uncompromising ride, it’s a tough one to forget.
emailReview:
Revenge is a fierce, hyper-stylized thriller that blends Kill Bill’s relentless energy with The Strangers’ eerie isolation, anchored by Matilda Lutz’s unforgettable performance and Coralie Fargeat’s sharp, darkly feminist direction.

Be prepared for: graphic animal violence, snake attacks, bug infestations, and intense survival brutality.

primaryTitle: Scouts Guide to the Zombie Apocalypse
writers: Carrie Lee Wilson, Emi Mochizuki, Christopher Landon, Lona Williams
Title_IMDb_Link: Scouts Guide to the Zombie Apocalypse
name: Scouts Guide to the Zombie Apocalypse
cleanNameArticles: scouts guide to the zombie apocalypse
overview: Three scouts and lifelong friends join forces with one badass cocktail waitress to become the world’s most unlikely team of heroes.  When their peaceful town is ravaged by a zombie invasion, they’ll fight for the badge of a lifetime and put their scouting skills to the test to save mankind from the undead.
review:
Scouts Guide to the Zombie Apocalypse is a cheeky, raunchy horror-comedy that feels like a mashup of Superbad meets Night of the Living Dead, with a generous splash of teen slapstick. It’s the kind of flick where scouts trade badges for baseball bats and cocktail waitresses turn into badass zombie slayers. Not exactly high art, but it earns points for its goofy charm and solid chemistry among the leads, especially Tye Sheridan and Sarah Dumont. If you’re into zombie flicks that don’t take themselves too seriously, this one’s a wild ride, though it’s not as sharp or funny as some of the genre’s best.

What stands out is how the film leans hard into its absurd premise: three scouts using their outdoorsy skills to fend off a full-blown zombie apocalypse. Director Christopher Landon, known for blending horror with humor, leans into the chaos with plenty of over-the-top gore, jump scares, and juvenile jokes. The tagline “Always bring protection” nails the film’s tongue-in-cheek tone. While it doesn’t reinvent the zombie wheel, the mix of teenage antics and undead carnage keeps things entertaining enough.

Heads up for anyone sensitive to graphic content: Scouts Guide to the Zombie Apocalypse is heavy on blood and gore, jump scares, and some pretty brutal moments like people getting burned alive and finger mutilations. Animal lovers, beware—a dog dies, and there’s general animal harm. Also, there are flashing lights, shaky cam, and a few other unsettling moments that might catch you off guard. If any of that’s on your list, proceed with caution.
emailReview:
Scouts Guide to the Zombie Apocalypse blends raunchy teen comedy with gory zombie chaos, delivering goofy charm and solid lead chemistry in a wild, blood-soaked romp.

Be prepared for: graphic animal harm including a dog dying, brutal finger mutilations, people burned alive, and plenty of jump scares.

name: Watcher
overview: Julia — a young actress who just moved to town with her husband — notices a mysterious stranger watching her from across the street.
