And Mary, who's found an entire network of loving, supportive men, just needs to find one who's straight.
tagline: Are you the exception... or are you the rule?

writers: Ewan Leslie, Karen McCullah, Kirsten Smith
name: She's the Man
overview: Viola Johnson is in a real jam. Complications threaten her scheme to pose as her twin brother, Sebastian, and take his place at a new boarding school. She falls in love with her handsome roommate, Duke, who loves beautiful Olivia, who has fallen for Sebastian! As if that were not enough, Viola's twin returns from London ahead of schedule but has no idea that his sister has already replaced him on campus.

writers: Maya Forbes, Wallace Wolodarsky, Rob Letterman, Jonathan Aibel, Glenn Berger, Conrad Vernon
name: Monsters Vs Aliens
overview: When Susan Murphy is unwittingly clobbered by a meteor full of outer space gunk on her wedding day, she mysteriously grows to 49-feet-11-inches. The military jumps into action and captures Susan, secreting her away to a covert government compound. She is renamed Ginormica and placed in confinement with a ragtag group of Monsters...
tagline: Saving the day the monster way.

name: Need for Speed
overview: The film revolves around a local street-racer who partners with a rich and arrogant business associate, only to find himself framed by his colleague and sent to prison. After he gets out, he joins a New York-to-Los Angeles race to get revenge. But when the ex-partner learns of the scheme, he puts a massive bounty on the racer's head, forcing him to run a cross-country gauntlet of illegal racers in all manner of supercharged vehicles.
tagline: For honor. For love. For redemption.

writers: David Twohy, Jim Wheat, Ken Wheat
name: Riddick
overview: Betrayed by his own kind and left for dead on a desolate planet, Riddick fights for survival against alien predators and becomes more powerful and dangerous than ever before. Soon bounty hunters from throughout the galaxy descend on Riddick only to find themselves pawns in his greater scheme for revenge. With his enemies right where he wants them, Riddick unleashes a vicious attack of vengeance before returning to his home planet of Furya to save it from destruction.

name: The Punisher
overview: When undercover FBI agent Frank Castle's wife and son are slaughtered, he becomes 'the Punisher' -- a ruthless vigilante willing to go to any length to avenge his family.
tagline: There is no justice, there is only revenge.

name: Pitch Perfect 2
overview: The Bellas are back, and they are better than ever. After being humiliated in front of none other than the President of the United States of America, the Bellas are taken out of the Aca-Circuit. In order to clear their name, and regain their status, the Bellas take on a seemingly impossible task: winning an international competition no American team has ever won. In order to accomplish this monumental task, they need to strengthen the bonds of friendship and sisterhood and blow away the competition with their amazing aca-magic! With all new friends and old rivals tagging along for the trip, the Bellas can hopefully accomplish their dreams.
review:
Pitch Perfect 2 is the kind of loud, colorful musical comedy sequel that knows exactly what it is and leans hard into it. Picking up after the Bellas’ humiliating presidential mishap, this one cranks up the stakes with an international competition no American team has ever won. If you liked the first movie’s mix of goofy humor and catchy a cappella, this sequel delivers more of the same — though it doesn’t quite hit the same fresh notes as the original. Fans of ensemble comedies like *Glee* or *Bring It On* will find plenty to enjoy, especially with Rebel Wilson’s Fat Amy stealing scenes as usual.

What stands out here is the film’s relentless energy and the way it uses music as a glue for friendship and sisterhood — the tagline “We’re back pitches” says it all. Anna Kendrick’s Beca is still the group’s heart, and the addition of new characters like Hailee Steinfeld’s Emily adds some fresh dynamics, even if the story follows familiar underdog tropes. Elizabeth Banks directs with a light touch, keeping the vibe fun and upbeat. The writing by Kay Cannon keeps the jokes coming, though it leans on fat jokes and some cringe-worthy bits that might not land for everyone.

On the trigger front, be heavily warned if you’re sensitive to the death of animals or children, as both occur in the story. There are also jump scares and scenes involving fire or burning, which might catch you off guard in an otherwise comedic romp. If you’re watching with an eye out for animal harm or emotional triggers around loss, this one has a few moments that may sting amid the laughs and tunes.
emailReview:
Pitch Perfect 2 bursts with energetic musical numbers and Rebel Wilson’s Fat Amy stealing scenes with her trademark sass, keeping the sequel loud and colorful even if it doesn’t quite match the original’s fresh charm.

Be prepared for: the death of animals and children, jump scares, and scenes involving fire or burning.

name: The Princess Diaries
overview: A socially awkward but very bright 15-year-old girl being raised by a single mom discovers that she is the princess of a small European country because of the recent death of her long-absent father, who, unknown to her, was the crown prince of Genovia. She must make a choice between continuing the life of a San Francisco teen or stepping up to the throne.
tagline: She rocks. She rules. She reigns.

writers: Stuart Gordon, Brian Yuzna, Ed Naha, Tom Schulman
name: Honey, I Shrunk the Kids
altName: honey i shrunk the kids i
overview: The scientist father of a teenage girl and boy accidentally shrinks his and two other neighborhood teens to the size of insects. Now the teens must fight diminutive dangers as the father searches for them.
tagline: The most astonishing, innovative, backyard adventure of all time!
review:
Honey, I Shrunk the Kids is a quintessential late-80s family sci-fi adventure that still holds up as a charming, imaginative romp. It’s a blend of inventive practical effects and goofy humor, anchored by Rick Moranis’s delightfully nerdy scientist dad, Wayne Szalinski. Think E.T. meets The Borrowers, with a dash of backyard peril thrown in. While it’s not exactly high drama, it’s a wild ride of shrinking down to insect size and facing off against everyday threats that suddenly feel enormous — perfect for fans of lighthearted, practical-effect-driven nostalgia.

What stands out here is the playful creativity in the premise: shrinking kids to the size of bugs and turning the backyard into an obstacle course of danger and discovery. The tagline, “The most astonishing, innovative, backyard adventure of all time!” isn’t just hype — the film leans heavily on inventive visuals and clever set pieces that make the mundane terrifying and exciting. The tone is upbeat and silly, with some classic 80s family movie warmth, even as the kids navigate perilous terrain and evade neighborhood bullies. The writing knows its audience, mixing science gone wrong with heartfelt family moments, and Joe Johnston’s direction keeps things moving at a brisk, engaging pace.

Heads-up for those sensitive to intense peril and body horror: there’s finger and toe mutilation, and a character is burned alive, which might be jarring amid the otherwise light tone. Spiders and other bugs play a big role, so if you’re not a fan of creepy crawlies, keep that in mind. There’s also the heavy theme of a kid dying, which adds an unexpected weight to the adventure. Overall, it’s a classic with a few rough edges that might catch you off guard, but it’s mostly a fun blast from the past.
emailReview:
Honey, I Shrunk the Kids is a charming late-80s family sci-fi with inventive practical effects and Rick Moranis’s delightfully nerdy scientist dad leading a wild backyard adventure that makes the mundane feel enormous and thrilling.

Be prepared for: finger and toe mutilation, a character burned alive, spider and bug encounters, and the heavy theme of a child’s death.

writers: David Lindsay-Abaire, Lowell Ganz, Babaloo Mandel, Ron Mita, Jim McClain
name: Robots
overview: Rodney Copperbottom is a young robot inventor who dreams of making the world a better place, until the evil Ratchet takes over Big Weld Industries. Now, Rodney's dreams – and those of his friends – are in danger of becoming obsolete.

name: The Purge: Anarchy
overview: One night per year, the government sanctions a 12-hour period in which citizens can commit any crime they wish -- including murder -- without fear of punishment or imprisonment. Leo, a sergeant who lost his son, plans a vigilante mission of revenge during the mayhem. However, instead of a death-dealing avenger, he becomes the unexpected protector of four innocent strangers who desperately need his help if they are to survive the night.

name: Friday the 13th
overview: Camp counselors are stalked and murdered by an unknown assailant while trying to reopen a summer camp that was the site of a child's drowning.
tagline: They were warned...They are doomed...And on Friday the 13th, nothing will save them.

writers: Mary Rodgers, Heather Hach, Leslie Dixon
name: Freaky Friday
overview: Mother and daughter bicker over everything -- what Anna wears, whom she likes and what she wants to do when she's older. In turn, Anna detests Tess's fiancé. When a magical fortune cookie switches their personalities, they each get a peek at how the other person feels, thinks and lives.
tagline: Mondays are manic. Wednesdays are wild. And Fridays are about to get a little freaky.

name: Billy Madison
overview: Billy Madison is the 27 year-old son of Bryan Madison, a very rich man who has made his living in the hotel industry. Billy stands to inherit his father's empire but only if he can make it through all 12 grades, 2 weeks per grade, to prove that he has what it takes to run the family business.
tagline: To inherit his family's fortune, Billy is going back to school... Way back.

name: My Best Friends Wedding
overview: When she receives word that her longtime platonic pal Michael O'Neal is getting married to debutante Kimberly Wallace, food critic Julianne Potter realizes her true feelings for Michael -- and sets out to sabotage the wedding.
tagline: Julianne fell in love with her best friend the day he decided to marry someone else.

name: Red Eye
overview: After attending the funeral of her grandmother in Dallas, the Lux Atlantic Hotel manager Lisa is waiting for a flight to Miami. Due to the bad weather and consequent flight delay, she meets in the airport bar Jack Rippner, who is also in the waiting list. They sit together in the plane, and Jack reveals that he wants Lisa to change the room in Lux of an important American politician to facilitate a terrorist attempt against him. Otherwise, Lisa's father will be killed by a hit man. Lisa has to decide what to do with the menacing man at her side.

name: The Bodyguard
overview: A former Secret Service agent grudgingly takes an assignment to protect a pop idol who's threatened by a crazed fan. At first, the safety-obsessed bodyguard and the self-indulgent diva totally clash. But before long, all that tension sparks fireworks of another sort, and the love-averse tough guy is torn between duty and romance.
tagline: Never let her out of your sight. Never let your guard down. Never fall in love.

name: The Invention of Lying
overview: Set in a world where the concept of lying doesn't exist, a loser changes his lot when he invents lying and uses it to get ahead.

name: Escape Room
overview: Six strangers find themselves in circumstances beyond their control, and must use their wits to survive.

name: She's Out of My League
overview: When he starts dating drop-dead gorgeous Molly, insecure airport security agent Kirk can't believe it. As his friends and family share their doubts about the relationship lasting, Kirk does everything he can to avoid losing Molly forever.

name: Greenland
overview: A detached married couple must get their son and themselves to safety after being randomly selected to enter an underground bunker, as a massive object from space threatens to destroy the world in less than 48 hours.
tagline: It's the end of the world as we know it.

writers: Mark Perez, Adam Cooper, Bill Collage
name: Accepted
overview: A high school slacker who's rejected by every school he applies to opts to create his own institution of higher learning, the South Harmon Institute of Technology, on a rundown piece of property near his hometown.
tagline: When every college turned them down. . . they made one up.

writers: James Vanderbilt, Guy Busick, Kevin Williamson
name: Scream VI
overview: Following the latest Ghostface killings, the four survivors leave Woodsboro behind and start a fresh chapter.

writers: Rowan Atkinson, Richard Curtis, Simon McBurney, Hamish McColl, Robin Driscoll
name: Mr. Bean's Holiday
overview: Mr. Bean wins a trip to Cannes where he unwittingly separates a young boy from his father and must help the two reunite. On the way he discovers France, bicycling and true love, among other things.

name: Killer Elite
overview: Based on a shocking true story, Killer Elite pits two of the world’s most elite operatives—Danny, an ex-special ops agent and Hunter, his longtime mentor—against the cunning leader of a secret military society. Covering the globe from Australia to Paris, London and the Middle East, Danny and Hunter are plunged into a highly dangerous game of cat and mouse—where the predators become the prey.

name: Daybreakers
overview: In the year 2019, a plague has transformed almost every human into vampires. Faced with a dwindling blood supply, the fractured dominant race plots their survival; meanwhile, a researcher works with a covert band of vampires on a way to save humankind.
tagline: In 2019, the most precious natural resource... is us.

writers: Dr. Seuss, Cinco Paul, Ken Daurio
name: The Lorax
overview: A 12-year-old boy searches for the one thing that will enable him to win the affection of the girl of his dreams. To find it he must discover the story of the Lorax, the grumpy yet charming creature who fights to protect his world.
tagline: Meet the original force of nature.

writers: Shane Salerno, Don Winslow, Oliver Stone
name: Savages
overview: Pot growers Ben and Chon face off against the Mexican drug cartel who kidnapped their shared girlfriend.

name: The Ritual
overview: A group of college friends reunite for a trip to the forest, but encounter a menacing presence in the woods that's stalking them.
review:
The Ritual is a moody blend of horror and psychological thriller that leans heavily into atmospheric dread rather than jump scares. It’s the kind of forest nightmare that fans of The Blair Witch Project or Midsommar might appreciate, but with a grittier, more grounded edge. Rafe Spall anchors the cast with a performance that’s equal parts weary and haunted, helping the film avoid feeling like just another generic “friends in the woods” horror flick.

What really stands out here is the way the film builds tension through its eerie setting and slow-burn storytelling. The tagline, “Your darkest dream awaits you,” nails the vibe — this is less about overt monster action and more about creeping paranoia and the unknown stalking the group. Writer Joe Barton and director David Bruckner lean into folklore and psychological trauma, making the forest feel like a character itself, dense with menace and mystery. It’s a film that rewards patience, with its unsettling visuals and ominous score pulling you deeper into the nightmare.

Trigger-wise, be warned that this one’s heavy on animal-related distress. Several animals die or are harmed, including a dog, a cat, and even a horse, and there are unsettling moments involving bugs, snakes, and spiders. If the thought of animal suffering or death is tough for you, approach with caution.
emailReview:
The Ritual creeps under your skin with a slow-burn tension and a haunted performance from Rafe Spall, turning the forest into a menacing character all its own.

Be prepared for: multiple animal deaths including a dog and a horse, unsettling insect scenes, and intense psychological dread.

name: The Jackal
overview: Hired by a powerful member of the Russian mafia to avenge an FBI sting that left his brother dead, a psychopathic hitman known only as The Jackal proves an elusive target for the people charged with the task of bringing him down: a deputy FBI director, a Russian MVK Major,  and a jailed IRA terrorist who can recognize him.
tagline: How do you stop an assassin who has no identity?

writers: Michael Mitnick, Robert B. Weide, Lois Lowry
name: The Giver
overview: In a seemingly perfect community, without war, pain, suffering, differences or choice, a young boy is chosen to learn from an elderly man about the true pain and pleasure of the "real" world.

name: Fall
overview: For best friends Becky and Hunter, life is all about conquering fears and pushing limits. But after they climb 2,000 feet to the top of a remote, abandoned radio tower, they find themselves stranded with no way down. Now Becky and Hunter's expert climbing skills will be put to the ultimate test as they desperately fight to survive the elements, a lack of supplies, and vertigo-inducing heights.
review:
Fall climbs into the survival thriller genre with a mix of nerve-wracking suspense and vertigo-inducing visuals that will keep you gripping your seat. It’s like a high-altitude cousin to films like *127 Hours* or *The Descent*, but with an added dose of psychological tension between its two leads. The dynamic between Becky and Hunter adds a messy emotional layer — especially once you learn about their fraught past — keeping this from being just another “trapped in a perilous place” story. It’s not the most polished thriller out there, but the shaky cam and relentless tension do a solid job of immersing you in their precarious predicament.

What stands out most in *Fall* is its claustrophobic use of height and the crumbling radio tower setting, which feels like a character in itself. The tagline "Fear reaches new heights" is spot-on, especially as the characters’ physical and emotional limits are tested. The film leans heavily on the anxiety of vertigo and isolation, using creaking metal, flashing red lights, and sudden gusts of wind to ratchet up the tension. It also doesn’t shy away from messy human emotions, with Becky’s grief, Hunter’s betrayal, and the unraveling friendship adding a raw edge to the survival drama. The score and sound design amplify the dread, though the frequent shaky cam can be a bit much if you’re sensitive to motion sickness.

If you’re especially wary of intense physical danger, this one delivers plenty of heart-stopping moments, including some serious falls and injuries. The shaky cam is used throughout, ranging from mild to intense, which might not be great if you’re prone to nausea or motion sensitivity. There’s also a fair amount of swearing (PG-13 level, so it’s mostly “freakin” and light curses), jump scares, and screaming. The film deals with heavy stuff like anxiety attacks, attempted suicide, and toxic friendship dynamics, so those triggers are worth keeping in mind. Animal lovers beware, too: there are scenes involving vultures eating a live animal and other unsettling animal harm moments that might be tough to watch. Overall, *Fall* is a brutal, gritty climb that’s as much about psychological survival as it is about scaling dizzying heights.
emailReview:
*Fall* hooks you with its relentless, vertigo-inducing tension and the messy emotional fallout between its two stranded leads, making it a survival thriller that’s as much about human fragility as it is about physical peril.

Be prepared for: intense falls and injuries, anxiety attacks, attempted suicide, live animal harm involving vultures, and relentless shaky cam.

name: Funny People
overview: Famous and wealthy funnyman George Simmons doesn't give much thought to how he treats people until a doctor delivers stunning health news, forcing George to reevaluate his priorities with a little help from aspiring stand-up comic Ira.

name: As Above, So Below
overview: When a team of explorers ventures into the catacombs that lie beneath the streets of Paris, they uncover the dark secret that lies within this city of the dead.
tagline: The only way out is down.

writers: Chris Van Allsburg, David Koepp, John Kamps
name: Zathura: a Space Adventure
overview: After their father is called into work, two young boys, Walter and Danny, are left in the care of their teenage sister, Lisa, and told they must stay inside. Walter and Danny, who anticipate a boring day, are shocked when they begin playing Zathura, a space-themed board game, which they realize has mystical powers when their house is shot into space. With the help of an astronaut, the boys attempt to return home.

overview: After the disastrous food storm in the first film, Flint and his friends are forced to leave the town. Flint accepts the invitation from his idol Chester V to join The Live Corp Company, which has been tasked to clean the island, and where the best inventors in the world create technologies for the betterment of mankind. When Flint discovers that his machine still operates and now creates mutant food beasts like living pickles, hungry tacodiles, shrimpanzees and apple pie-thons, he and his friends must return to save the world.

writers: David Soren, Darren Lemke, Robert Siegel
name: Turbo
overview: The tale of an ordinary garden snail who dreams of winning the Indy 500.
review:
Turbo is a fast-paced, family-friendly animated flick that leans hard into the feel-good underdog story—only this time, the underdog is a garden snail with Indy 500 dreams. It’s got that classic “small but mighty” vibe that fans of movies like *Cars* or *Ratatouille* will appreciate, but it’s not quite as sharp or memorable as those Pixar heavy-hitters. Ryan Reynolds lends his voice to Turbo, giving the character a laid-back charm, though the story itself sticks pretty close to the usual animated sports-movie tropes. It’s a fun watch if you’re in the mood for something light, colorful, and not too demanding.

What stands out here is the sheer absurdity and heart behind the premise—snails don’t race cars, but Turbo sure thinks he can. The tagline “He’s fast. They’re furious.” nails the cheeky tone, and the animation is bright and energetic, capturing the quirky world of garden creatures with some surprisingly slick visuals. The supporting cast of voices, including Paul Giamatti and Samuel L. Jackson, bring some welcome personality and humor to the mix. The film leans into themes of believing in yourself and chasing impossible dreams, which, while familiar, are delivered with enough warmth to keep younger viewers engaged.

Heads up to those sensitive to animal harm and death triggers: despite its lighthearted packaging, *Turbo* includes some surprisingly dark moments, including the death of a dog and a kid, and a crow getting hit by a truck. There are also jump scares, flashing lights, and a scene where someone is burned alive, so if any of that sets off alarms for you, proceed with caution. The movie balances its sunny exterior with a handful of heavier beats that might catch parents off guard.
emailReview:
Turbo zooms in with a bright, energetic animation and a laid-back charm thanks to Ryan Reynolds, delivering a quirky underdog story that’s equal parts heart and absurdity.

Be prepared for: the death of a dog and a kid, a crow hit by a truck, a burning alive scene, jump scares, and flashing lights.

name: National Lampoon's Van Wilder
overview: Van Wilder has been attending college for far too many years and is scared to graduate, but Van’s father eventually realizes what is going on. When he stops paying his son's tuition fees, Van must come up with the money if he wants to stay in college, so he and his friends come up with a great fund-raising idea – throwing parties. However, when the college magazine finds out and reporter, Gwen is sent to do a story on Van Wilder, things get a little complicated.

writers: Robert Mark Kamen, Matt Cook, Ric Roman Waugh, Creighton Rothenberger, Katrin Benedikt
name: Angel Has Fallen
overview: After a treacherous attack, Secret Service agent Mike Banning is charged with attempting to assassinate President Trumbull. Chased by his own colleagues and the FBI, Banning begins a race against the clock to clear his name.
review:
Angel Has Fallen is your classic high-stakes action thriller with Gerard Butler back as Mike Banning, the loyal Secret Service agent caught in a brutal frame-up. It’s the kind of tense, no-nonsense chase movie that fans of the “Olympus Has Fallen” series will appreciate—think “Die Hard” meets a political conspiracy flick. It’s not reinventing the wheel, but it delivers solidly on the adrenaline and suspense, elevated by Morgan Freeman’s steady presence as President Trumbull, adding some much-needed gravitas.

What stands out here is the tight pacing and the way the film leans into the theme of fractured loyalty—Banning isn’t just running from the bad guys, he’s running from his own team, which adds a layer of personal betrayal to the usual action movie fare. The tagline “Loyalty is under fire” nails the emotional core, even if the plot twists are a bit by-the-numbers. Ric Roman Waugh’s direction keeps the action scenes gritty and grounded, and the supporting cast, including Jada Pinkett Smith and Nick Nolte, bring enough depth to keep the drama from feeling hollow.

Heads-up for anyone sensitive to animal-related distress: this movie unfortunately features multiple instances of animal deaths and abuse, including a dog, horse, cat, and more. Also, spiders, snakes, and bugs appear on screen, which might catch some viewers off guard. On the human side, there are triggers like child abuse, domestic violence, stalking, and gaslighting woven into the story, so if any of those are on your radar, proceed with caution.
emailReview:
Angel Has Fallen cranks up the tension with Gerard Butler’s relentless action and a gritty look at fractured loyalty, making it a solid pick for fans who like their thrillers with a personal edge.

Be prepared for: multiple animal deaths including dog and horse, spider and snake appearances, child abuse, domestic violence, and stalking.

name: Tango & Cash
overview: Ray Tango and Gabriel Cash are narcotics detectives who, while both being extremely successful, can't stand each other. Crime Lord Yves Perret, furious at the loss of income that Tango and Cash have caused him, frames the two for murder. Caught with the murder weapon on the scene of the crime, the two have no alibi. Thrown into prison with most of the criminals they helped convict, it appears that they are going to have to trust each other if they are to clear their names and catch the evil Perret.
tagline: Two of L.A.'s top rival cops are going to have to work together… Even if it kills them.

name: Gremlins 2: the New Batch
overview: Young sweethearts Billy and Kate move to the Big Apple, land jobs in a high-tech office park and soon reunite with the friendly and lovable Gizmo. But a series of accidents creates a whole new generation of Gremlins. The situation worsens when the devilish green creatures invade a top-secret laboratory and develop genetically altered powers, making them even harder to destroy!
review:
Gremlins 2: The New Batch is a wild, self-aware sequel that cranks the chaos dial way past the original’s small-town horror-comedy vibe. Joe Dante leans into satire and outright silliness, turning the lovable Gizmo and his mischievous offspring loose in a high-tech New York office park that feels like a funhouse mirror of corporate culture. If the first Gremlins was a cautionary tale about holiday mishaps, this one’s more of a madcap sci-fi romp with a sharper, zanier edge—think Ghostbusters meets a loony workplace sitcom. It’s not quite as cozy or creepy as the original, but it’s elevated by its gleeful absurdity and some standout performances, especially from John Glover’s hilariously villainous Daniel Clamp.

The film’s strength lies in how it leans into the ridiculousness of its premise. The tagline, “Here they grow again,” is a perfect wink at the sequel’s bigger, louder set pieces and the genetically enhanced monsters that push the Gremlin mythology in new directions. The office park setting offers a slick, almost cyberpunk playground that’s visually engaging, and the script doesn’t shy away from poking fun at corporate greed and tech obsession. Christopher Lee as the sinister Dr. Catheter adds a nice touch of old-school menace in the midst of the chaos, while the creative use of the laboratory setting amps up the body horror and sci-fi elements, giving the Gremlins some fresh tricks (and mutations) to keep things interesting.

Heads up for those sensitive to animal harm and violence: this one includes multiple instances of animals dying, including pets, and a fair amount of body horror and graphic mischief courtesy of the Gremlins’ antics. There’s also sexual content, a hospital scene, and some unsettling moments involving assault and miscarriage that could be tough for more sensitive viewers. Plus, if spiders, bugs, or snakes send you scrambling, be warned—they make appearances here. The film is a carnival of chaos, but it’s not without some pretty heavy triggers lurking beneath the zany surface.
emailReview:
Gremlins 2: The New Batch cranks the chaos up to eleven with a madcap sci-fi romp that gleefully skewers corporate culture while delivering standout performances and eye-popping creature mutations.

Be prepared for: pet deaths, graphic body horror, unsettling hospital scenes, sexual content, and creepy appearances by spiders and snakes.

name: Fright Night
overview: A teenager suspects his new neighbour is a vampire. Unable to convince anyone, he tries to enlist the help of a self-proclaimed vampire hunter and magician in this remake of the 1985 comedy-horror classic.

name: The Babysitter
overview: When Cole stays up past his bedtime, he discovers that his hot babysitter is part of a Satanic cult that will stop at nothing to keep him quiet.
tagline: Dream girls can be a nightmare.
review:
The Babysitter is a gleefully twisted mix of teen comedy and horror, landing somewhere between the slasher flair of *Scream* and the darkly playful vibe of *Jennifer’s Body*. It’s a wild ride that balances goofy one-liners with genuinely creepy moments, thanks in no small part to Samara Weaving’s magnetic performance as the dangerously charming Bee. While it’s not reinventing the wheel, it’s a sharp, entertaining take on the “evil babysitter” trope that knows when to lean into absurdity and when to dial up the tension.

What stands out most is the film’s willingness to go full throttle with its premise—“Dream girls can be a nightmare” isn’t just a tagline, it’s a promise. The story of Cole discovering his babysitter’s Satanic cult membership blends horror with teen angst in a way that feels fresh, thanks to Brian Duffield’s snappy script and McG’s energetic direction. The film plays with genre conventions, delivering jump scares and gore with a wink, while also weaving in themes of trust, betrayal, and survival in the most over-the-top ways possible. Plus, the supporting cast adds just the right mix of quirky characters to keep things lively.

Heads up for those sensitive to intense violence and gore—there’s plenty of blood, mutilation, and some harrowing deaths that include a kid and an animal. There’s also jump scares, flashing lights, spiders, and scenes that involve burning alive and finger mutilation, so it’s not exactly a light watch. If any of those are on your list, The Babysitter might be a bit much, but for fans of horror-comedies who like their scares served with a side of wicked humor, it hits the mark.
emailReview: The Babysitter is a gleefully twisted teen horror-comedy that rides the line between Scream-style slasher thrills and darkly playful absurdity, anchored by Samara Weaving’s magnetic and dangerously charming lead performance. Be prepared for: finger mutilation, burning alive, a child death, animal death, and plenty of blood and gore.

name: The Lucky One
overview:
U.S. Marine Sergeant Logan Thibault returns from his third tour of duty in Iraq, with the one thing he credits with keeping him alive-a photograph he found of a woman he doesn't even know. 

Learning her name is Beth and where she lives, he shows up at her door, and ends up taking a job at her family-run local kennel. Despite her initial mistrust and the complications in her life, a romance develops between them, giving Logan hope that Beth could be much more than his good luck charm.

name: Paycheck
overview: Michael Jennings is a genius who's hired – and paid handsomely – by high-tech firms to work on highly sensitive projects, after which his short-term memory is erased so he's incapable of breaching security. But at the end of a three-year job, he's told he isn't getting a paycheck and instead receives a mysterious envelope. In it are clues he must piece together to find out why he wasn't paid – and why he's now in hot water.

name: The Iron Lady
overview: A look at the life of Margaret Thatcher, the former Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, with a focus on the price she paid for power.

writers: Ryan Ridley, Robert Kirkman, Ava Tramer
name: Renfield
overview: Having grown sick and tired of his centuries as Dracula's lackey, Renfield finds a new lease on life — and maybe even redemption — when he falls for feisty, perennially angry traffic cop Rebecca Quincy.

name: Leap Year
overview: When yet another anniversary passes without a marriage proposal from her boyfriend, Anna decides to take action. Aware of a Celtic tradition that allows women to pop the question on Feb. 29, she plans to follow her lover to Dublin and ask him to marry her. Fate has other plans, however, and Anna winds up on the other side of the Emerald Isle with handsome, but surly, Declan -- an Irishman who may just lead Anna down the road to true love.
tagline: Anna planned to propose to her boyfriend on February 29th. This is not her boyfriend.

writers: Christopher Wood, Ian Fleming, Gerry Anderson, Tony Barwick
name: Moonraker
overview: After Drax Industries' Moonraker space shuttle is hijacked, secret agent James Bond is assigned to investigate, traveling to California to meet the company's owner, the mysterious Hugo Drax. With the help of scientist Dr. Holly Goodhead, Bond soon uncovers Drax's nefarious plans for humanity, all the while fending off an old nemesis, Jaws, and venturing to Venice, Rio, the Amazon...and even outer space.
tagline: Where all the other Bonds end… this one begins!

name: The Cell
overview: A psychotherapist journeys inside a comatose serial killer in the hopes of saving his latest victim.
tagline: Enter the mind of a killer.
review:
The Cell is a visually arresting psychological thriller that feels like a surreal art-house fever dream wedged into a serial killer rescue plot. Jennifer Lopez leads as Catherine Deane, a psychotherapist who literally enters the mind of a comatose killer (Vincent D’Onofrio) to save his latest victim. It’s the kind of bold, slightly bonkers concept that’s elevated by Tarsem Singh’s signature visual flair — think vivid, twisted dreamscapes that rival the likes of David Lynch or Guillermo del Toro’s more psychedelic moments. While it might not quite reach the emotional depths of Silence of the Lambs, it stands out for its audacious style and unsettling atmosphere.

What’s most worth talking about is the film’s commitment to exploring the killer’s subconscious as a nightmarish realm where reality warps and the line between hunter and hunted blurs. The tagline, “Enter the mind of a killer,” isn’t just marketing fluff—it’s the core of the film’s appeal. The score unnerves without overwhelming, and the performances, especially D’Onofrio’s chillingly intense portrayal, ground the surreal visuals in palpable dread. Vince Vaughn’s role as the victim’s father adds a grounded emotional thread, though it’s Lopez’s Catherine who carries the weight of the film’s eerie, mind-bending journey.

Heads up for those sensitive to animal-related content: The movie includes scenes featuring a dream horse that dies, along with other instances of animal distress and death—cats, dogs, and some unsettling animal imagery are present. If the “animal harm” or “animal death” triggers are high on your list, be prepared for some tough moments here. The film also features spiders and snakes, adding to its overall creepy-crawly vibe.
emailReview:
The Cell is a surreal psychological thriller that drags you deep into the twisted, visually stunning dreamscape of a comatose killer’s mind, anchored by Jennifer Lopez’s steady lead and Vincent D’Onofrio’s unnervingly intense performance.

Be prepared for: a dream horse dying, cat and dog distress, unsettling animal imagery, spiders, and snakes.

name: Repo Men
overview: In the future, medical technology has advanced to the point where people can buy artificial organs to extend their lives. But if they default on payments, an organization known as the Union sends agents to repossess the organs. Remy is one of the best agents in the business, but when he becomes the recipient of an artificial heart, he finds himself in the same dire straits as his many victims.

writers: Martin Stellman, Brian Ward, Charles Randolph, Scott Frank, Steven Zaillian
name: The Interpreter
overview: After Silvia Broome, an interpreter at United Nations headquarters, overhears plans of an assassination, an American Secret Service agent is sent to investigate.

name: The Angry Birds Movie

In this paradise, Red, a bird with a temper problem, speedy Chuck, and the volatile Bomb have always been outsiders. But when the island is visited by mysterious green piggies, it’s up to these unlikely outcasts to figure out what the pigs are up to.
tagline: They came in peace, they left in chaos.

name: Colombiana
overview: Zoe Saldana plays a young woman who, after witnessing her parents’ murder as a child in Bogota, grows up to be a stone-cold assassin. She works for her uncle as a hitman by day, but her personal time is spent engaging in vigilante murders that she hopes will lead her to her ultimate target: the mobster responsible for her parents' death.

name: Hustlers
overview: A crew of savvy former strip club employees band together to turn the tables on their Wall Street clients.

name: A Dangerous Method
overview: Seduced by the challenge of an impossible case, the driven Dr. Carl Jung takes the unbalanced yet beautiful Sabina Spielrein as his patient. Jung’s weapon is the method of his master, the renowned Sigmund Freud. Both men fall under Sabina’s spell.
tagline: Why deny what you desire the most.

writers: Gavin Scott, Adam Rifkin, Ted Elliott, Terry Rossio
name: Small Soldiers
overview: When missile technology is used to enhance toy action figures, the toys soon begin to take their battle programming too seriously.

writers: Richard Maibaum, Michael G. Wilson, Ian Fleming
name: A View to a Kill
overview: A newly-developed microchip designed by Zorin Industries for the British Government that can survive the electromagnetic radiation caused by a nuclear explosion has landed in the hands of the KGB. James Bond must find out how and why. His suspicions soon lead him to big industry leader Max Zorin who forms a plan to destroy his only competition in Silicon Valley by triggering a massive earthquake in the San Francisco Bay.
tagline: Has James Bond finally met his match?

writers: Don Rhymer, Carlos Kotkin, Jenny Bicks, Yoni Brenner, Carlos Saldanha, Laurie Craig
name: Rio 2
overview: It's a jungle out there for Blu, Jewel and their three kids after they're hurtled from Rio de Janeiro to the wilds of the Amazon. As Blu tries to fit in, he goes beak-to-beak with the vengeful Nigel, and meets the most fearsome adversary of all: his father-in-law.

name: Revolver
overview: Hotshot gambler Jake Green (Jason Statham) is long on bravado and seriously short of common sense. Rarely is he allowed in any casino because he's a bona fide winner and, in fact, has taken so much money over the years that he's the sole client of his accountant elder brother, Billy. Invited to a private game, Jake is in fear of losing his life.

name: The American
overview: Dispatched to a small Italian town to await further orders, assassin Jack embarks on a double life that may be more relaxing than is good for him.

writers: Robert Ramsey, Matthew Stone, John Romano, Ethan Coen, Joel Coen
name: Intolerable Cruelty
overview: A revenge-seeking gold digger marries a womanizing Beverly Hills lawyer with the intention of making a killing in the divorce.

name: Polar
overview: When a retiring assassin realizes that he is the target of a hit, he winds up back in the game going head to head with a gang of younger, ruthless killers.

writers: Alice Hoffman, Robin Swicord, Akiva Goldsman, Adam Brooks
name: Practical Magic
overview: Sally and Gillian Owens, born into a magical family, have mostly avoided witchcraft themselves. But when Gillian's vicious boyfriend, Jimmy Angelov, dies unexpectedly, the Owens sisters give themselves a crash course in hard magic. With policeman Gary Hallet growing suspicious, the girls struggle to resurrect Angelov -- and unwittingly inject his corpse with an evil spirit that threatens to end their family line.
tagline: For two sisters from a family of witches, falling in love is the trickiest spell of all.

name: Monsters
overview: Six years ago NASA discovered the possibility of alien life within our solar system. A probe was launched to collect samples, but crashed upon re-entry over Central America. Soon after, new life forms began to appear and half of Mexico was quarantined as an infected zone. Today, the American and Mexican military still struggle to contain "the creatures," while a journalist agrees to escort a shaken tourist through the infected zone in Mexico to the safety of the U.S. border.
tagline: After six years, they're no longer aliens. They're residents.

writers: Darren Lemke, Scott Alexander, Larry Karaszewski, R.L. Stine
name: Goosebumps
overview: After moving to a small town, Zach Cooper finds a silver lining when he meets next door neighbor Hannah, the daughter of bestselling Goosebumps series author R.L. Stine. When Zach unintentionally unleashes real monsters from their manuscripts and they begin to terrorize the town, it’s suddenly up to Stine, Zach and Hannah to get all of them back in the books where they belong.

writers: Paul Hernandez, Bob Schooley, Mark McCorkle
name: Sky High
overview: Set in a world where superheroes are commonly known and accepted, young Will Stronghold, the son of the Commander and Jetstream, tries to find a balance between being a normal teenager and an extraordinary being.

name: The BFG
overview: The BFG is no ordinary bone-crunching giant. He is far too nice and jumbly. It's lucky for Sophie that he is. Had she been carried off in the middle of the night by the Bloodbottler, or any of the other giants—rather than the BFG—she would have soon become breakfast. When Sophie hears that the giants are flush-bunking off to England to swollomp a few nice little chiddlers, she decides she must stop them once and for all. And the BFG is going to help her!

name: Hotel Transylvania 3: Summer Vacation
overview: Dracula, Mavis, Johnny and the rest of the Drac Pack take a vacation on a luxury Monster Cruise Ship, where Dracula falls in love with the ship’s captain, Ericka, who’s secretly a descendant of Abraham Van Helsing, the notorious monster slayer.
tagline: He's going to need a vacation after this vacation.

name: It Ends With Us
overview: When a woman's first love suddenly reenters her life, her relationship with a charming, but abusive neurosurgeon is upended, and she realizes she must learn to rely on her own strength to make an impossible choice for her future.
tagline: We break the pattern or the pattern breaks us.

name: Young Adult
overview: A divorced writer from the Midwest returns to her hometown to reconnect with an old flame, who's now married with a family.

name: Centurion
overview: Britain, A.D. 117. Quintus Dias, the sole survivor of a Pictish raid on a Roman frontier fort, marches north with General Virilus' legendary Ninth Legion, under orders to wipe the Picts from the face of the Earth and destroy their leader, Gorlacon.

writers: Craig Rosenberg, Doug Miro, Carlo Bernard, Kim Jee-woon
name: The Uninvited
overview: Anna returns home after spending time in a psychiatric facility following her mother's tragic death and discovers that her mother's former nurse, Rachel, has moved into their house and become engaged to her father. Soon after she learns this shocking news, Anna is visited by her mother's ghost, who warns her that Rachel has evil intentions.
tagline: Can you believe what you see?

name: Before I Go to Sleep
overview: A woman wakes up every day, remembering nothing as a result of a traumatic accident in her past. One day, new terrifying truths emerge that force her to question everyone around her.
